1.title: The lounge: the game at the brass-rimmed table
1.gm: Hook h_ferry_table comes to its decision NOW, with or without Rowan. If he is at the table and in the middle of it, this is simply that scene reaching its game: Gideon [gideon] states his terms one last time and whoever has the seat plays. If Rowan has kept out or is elsewhere on the ship: Inya [inya] takes the wager, attacks first into the counter-swing and loses (@result gideon inya gideon); a roar comes up the lounge stair, Tomi [tomi] pays out his book and Nathan reports it at full volume. If the matter was already settled, only the paying-out remains. The table is then free for anyone. @clock about 25 for a game Rowan watches.

1.title: Rounding the south point: the Academy comes into sight
1.gm: Wherever Rowan is aboard, the ship heels a little and the talk stops: the Second Chance rounds the south point. Captain Stroud [abel] names the sights over the loudspeaker in one breath — the lighthouse, the tower on the cliff, the thin white line that is the Commons beach, the clock tower over the trees — and adds that anyone still owing the galley for a cinnamon roll has thirty-five minutes. People come up from the lounge to look; a game in progress is played to its end. One short answer, then the scene is Rowan's again. @clock 5.

1.title: The horn: bags up, everyone to the rail
1.gm: One long blast. Benches empty, duffel bags are dug out of the aisles, deck boxes go into pockets; Teobalt [teobalt] reads out the order in which the luggage comes off, and nobody listens. No new game starts now: a game still running is broken off by the horn and an open wager stands until the pier. The first-years crowd the rail and watch the jetty and its painted arch grow. Give Rowan one last exchange with whoever he spent the crossing with, then let the lines go over: the docking follows at 10:40. @clock up to that minute.

1.title: The ferry docks
1.gm: The horn sounds and the Second Chance ties up at the Academy pier. Whatever is going on aboard is cut short (an unfinished wager stands and is settled ashore). @place ferry_dock: gangway, upper-years with luggage carts under the arch, then the ten-minute walk up the avenue to the Quad.

1.title: Welcome address and dorm lists
1.gm: Begins at eleven on the main steps whether or not everyone is there (details: calendar entry 'Welcome Address & Dorm Assignment'). Rowan only listens: play the address and the reading of the lists in one long answer, then Mama Odalys collecting the Commons and the walk down to the cove.

1.title: Placement Duels at the Trial Domes
1.gm: Names are called from half past two; the first-years drift up from every corner of the campus beforehand and say so. Rowan's name comes when he is there (details: calendar entry 'Placement Duel').

1.title: Welcome Supper in Mama's Kitchen
1.gm: One table, served ONCE at half past six (details: calendar entry). When the pots are empty the supper ENDS: people wash up, drift to the porches and the bonfire pit, Odalys shoos the last ones out. Nobody is urged to eat a second time.

1.title: Lights out on the bungalow row
1.gm: Odalys's head count along the boardwalk; lights out means quiet. Whoever is still out is called in by name.

2.title: Orientation 1: the Chancellor's welcome, the Charter signed
2.gm: Two hundred seats; the 36 first-years fill the front rows more or less by collar, upper-years usher. Chancellor Vicar [okonkwo] speaks from the pit, short and formidable: what the Academy is (four years, three majors, one Ladder), what it expects (attendance, honesty at the table), where the island ends for students (Umbra House on the north ridge is closed — keep off; the wild island only in daylight and never alone), and that nobody here is owed a place. Then the Academy Charter goes along the rows on a clipboard and every first-year signs (nobody reads it; Noor reads all of it and signs last). Rowan only listens: play the WHOLE address in ONE long answer with real speech, ending when the clipboard reaches him. @clock 15.

2.title: Orientation 2: every member of staff introduces themselves
2.gm: The Chancellor calls the staff down one by one. EACH speaks a line or two of their own and shows one visible habit — ALL of them, nobody skipped or summarised: Prof. Santángel [santangel], head of Competitive Play, Tempo & Resource (black turtleneck; promises nothing above 'adequate') · Ms Kirishima [hana], Rules & Judging (the youngest on staff; corrects a term in her own introduction) · Dr Blum [blum], Probability & Game Theory (chalk on both cuffs; hunts for the glasses that sit in his hair) · Prof. Ashdown [ashdown], Lore & History of the Game and the island's archaeologist (field sections at the ruins are supervised; everything else is outside the syllabus) · Coach Rox [rox], Table Practicum and Physical Conditioning, coach of the Battle Team (has the whole hall stand up and sit down again) · Ms Laurent [vivienne], Casting & Media, head of the Auxiliary commentary track (the famous voice, and she knows it) · Prof. Helical [helical], Hologram Engineering & Table Tech (the demonstration table flickers while he apologises for it) · Nurse Moreau [camille], the infirmary (where it is; water, sunscreen) · Mr Grieve [silas], grounds and lighthouse (three sentences about cliffs and tides, then nothing) · Mrs Fuentes [odalys], kitchen and warden of the Commons (waves from the back row; breakfast is not optional) · and the Founder, Chuck Kaboom, Card Design Basics, whose chair is empty: 'Mr Kaboom will join us.' Rowan may whisper with a neighbour between two speakers; otherwise play it through in one or two LONG answers. @clock about 30 in all.

2.title: Orientation 3: the three majors, the Ladder, credits, grades
2.gm: Each major is presented by its own speaker — all three: COMPETITIVE PLAY (red jackets): Santángel — the players' major and the largest, hours at a real table, life on the Ladder; Lilia Mann [lilia], Battle Team captain, adds three friendly sentences for the students. GAME DESIGN (gold jackets): Wren Ishikawa [wren], third-year, ink on her fingers, stands in for the absent Founder — design, cost, word, print and playtest cards; the Design Contest in Term 1. AUXILIARY (black jackets, code CM): Vivienne — commentary, judging and refereeing, table and hologram tech, event staff; Bex Calloway [bex] plugs the campus stream 'The Top Deck'. Then the systems everybody lives by, in plain words (this is the tutorial): THE LADDER (all 144 players ranked; yesterday's Placement results stand; challenges open on Day 12; rank decides events and next year's dorm) · CREDITS (weekly stipend on Mondays, the job board, the shops, tuition for year two without a scholarship) · GRADES (A–F each term from attendance, study and exams; a skipped class counts at once) · PROBATION (two failed courses). Write @journal School lines for Ladder, credits and grades. One or two LONG answers; @clock about 30 in all.

2.title: Orientation 4: Charter Duels, house rules, the student council
2.gm: Ms Kirishima on CHARTER DUELS: a challenge made aloud, by name, before a witness, with a stated ante cannot be refused (deferred once, up to three days); the result binds both and the ante is paid at once. An ordinary game binds nobody. House rules in brief: uniform in class, opening hours, guests sign in at Rare Hall, the Spectral Tower is by invitation, staff rooms and the tunnels are off limits, tell someone before you go into the wild. Then the STUDENT COUNCIL introduces itself from the side aisle, one line each, all five: Octavia Sterling [octavia], president · Sebastian Thorne [sebastian], vice-president (permits, sanctions) · Imara Adeyemi [imara], treasurer (job pay) · Tavita Leota [tavita], head proctor (inspections) · Pilar Estévez [pilar], events and press (the Club Fair is tomorrow afternoon on the Quad). Sessions Monday and Thursday afternoon, open to every student. One long answer; @clock about 20.

2.title: Orientation 5: the Founder turns up; timetables; tour groups
2.gm: The side door bangs. Chuck Kaboom [chuck] wanders in late, loses his notes on the steps and tells ninety seconds of a story about Tarleinn as though he had been there; the hall adores him, the Chancellor studies the ceiling. He teaches Card Design Basics on Fridays. Timetables are passed along the rows (Rowan's: classes Monday to Friday in the Morning and Midday slots, from tomorrow; @journal School). Pilar reads out the tour groups by dorm — THE COMMONS with Tavita Leota, RARE HALL with Pilar herself, SPECTRAL TOWER with Sebastian Thorne — meeting at the fountain at eleven sharp. Then ten minutes of break on the Quad (@place quad): the first moment today in which Rowan can move and talk freely.

2.title: Guided campus tour, first half (the Commons group, guide: Tavita Leota)
2.gm: Rowan walks with the eighteen Commons first-years behind Tavita [tavita]; the other two groups cross their path now and then. ONE OR TWO STATIONS PER ANSWER, each with its @place, what one sees there, one practical thing Tavita says (hours, what it is for, one rule) and one small moment among the first-years — different people every time. Stations IN ORDER, none left out: quad (the fountain; the Clock Tower bell marks every part of the day; Umbra House pointed out on the north ridge: closed, keep off) → job_board and campus_store under the arcade → library (the Card Archive only with written permission) → great_arena → trial_dome → duel_terraces → down to the cafeteria by 12:30. Three to five minutes between stations, about ten at each (@clock). Check 'Rowan's path today' for where the tour stands. He may ask, lag behind or slip away — then the tour goes on without him.

2.title: Lunch at the Mess with the whole intake
2.gm: @place cafeteria. Seating is unofficially by collar and today nobody enforces it. An ordinary free scene around ONE meal, eaten once (@did lunch eaten). At a quarter past one Tavita stands up, counts heads and collects his group.

2.title: Guided campus tour, second half
2.gm: Same rules as the first half; stations IN ORDER, none left out: design_lab (Wren does not look up; Chuck's workshop lies behind it — in only when the half-door is open) → broadcast_studio (the ON AIR lamp; Bex waves through the glass) → gym and pool (Coach Rox; the lane ropes in dorm colours) → infirmary (Nurse Camille, a jar of barley sugar) → greenhouse → theatre → past rare_lobby and, from outside only, the Spectral Tower (invitation only; @known spectral_lobby) → main_gate: the avenue down to Port Mulligan, half an hour on foot; Tavita points out where the Jungle Trail and the Cliff Path begin — daylight only, never alone (@known jungle_trail, @known cliff_path) → back on the quad at about three. Tavita's last words: classes start tomorrow in the Morning slot, timetable in your pocket. The tour ENDS there (@did campus tour finished) and the rest of the day is Rowan's own.

3.title: First bell: timetables out, up the steps
3.gm: The clock-tower bell at twenty to nine. The whole first year crosses the Quad with yesterday's timetable in hand, looking for doors; upper-years go past without looking at theirs. Wednesday for Rowan: Lore & History in the Lecture Hall now, Table Practicum in the Trial Domes at half past eleven. One short answer of finding the way with whoever walks beside him (from the Commons: Nathan and Baylee), ending at the hall door. Staying away is possible, and it is counted. @clock 10–15.

3.title: First lecture of the year: Lore & History (Prof. Ashdown)
3.gm: Prof. Ashdown [ashdown] starts on the stroke of nine and shuts the door herself. Play the opening of the lecture as a scene — her first question to the hall, who answers, who should not have — and give Rowan one moment to speak or keep his head down; then the lesson runs by the normal class rules (@class lh101, which carries the clock to the Midday bell). She ends with the reading for next week. Establish the rhythm aloud through a neighbour: classes fill Morning and Midday, everything after two is one's own.

3.title: First Table Practicum at the Trial Domes (Coach Rox)
3.gm: Coach Rox [rox] has the first-years stand in a line by height before anyone touches a deck, then says to pair up — and what happens at that word is today's timeline entry about the ferry table, if one is listed. First real table time under a teacher's eye: sleeves, how to cut, how to announce. Play the pairing-up and the start of Rowan's supervised game as a scene, then take the lesson as @class cp150 (it carries the clock past lunch to two o'clock). Rox ends at one sharp with a lap of the dome for whoever was late. The afternoon is free: the Club Fair opens on the Quad at 14:30.

3.title: Club Fair: the stalls go up round the fountain
3.gm: Trestle tables in a ring round the fountain. Pilar [pilar], the council's events secretary, runs it at a trot; Teobalt [teobalt], three days on the island like everyone else, already carries her clipboard; Sebastian [sebastian] sits in the shade and stamps club charters. Hedda [hedda] has set up a stall nobody authorised — three causes, one megaphone — and Pilar moves it, twice. Eloise [eloise] is painting the theatre club's banner instead of joining anything. Rowan can lend a hand or watch; the fair opens at half past two. @clock 5–10 an answer.

3.title: Club Fair opens: a round of the stalls
3.gm: Pilar rings a handbell and the fair is open. ONE OR TWO STALLS PER ANSWER, each a door to a person: theatre (Marit [marit] in full flight), Judge Circle (Noor [noor], exact and shy), swim squad (Sunny [sunny], flirting at once), The Top Deck (Bex [bex] wants 'a Commons voice'), photo club (Pippa [pippa]), gardening (Wren [wren], half asleep; Trixie asks about bees), astronomy, and the outdoor club, whose unnamed leader is still giving the safety talk when Ed signs; Viktor [viktor] signs only to see their maps. Each stall says in one line WHEN it meets. @clock about 8 a stall.

3.title: Club Fair: demonstrations on the fountain steps
3.gm: Pilar calls the clubs up one after another, three minutes each, and holds a stopwatch nobody respects: Marit performs both halves of a sword fight, Saoirse [saoirse] and Sunny carry a surfboard across the Quad as an argument for the swim squad, Noor rules on a question shouted from the crowd and is right, Bex interviews the fountain. Rowan only watches: play it in ONE long answer with the first-years' reactions round him, and end when Pilar announces that the sign-up sheets close at five. @clock 35.

3.title: Club Fair: last call for the sign-up sheets
3.gm: Decision time. Rowan can join up to TWO clubs without his grades suffering; each sheet he signs gets a @journal Plans line with the club's meeting time, and the person at that stall remembers that he signed. At five Pilar collects the sheets, Sebastian locks the stamp away, Teobalt counts the trestles and the fair is over: tables folded, banner carried off still wet (@did Club Fair over). Whoever missed it can still sign at any club's own meeting — missing the fair only delays this.

5.title: Bonfire: carrying the wood, lighting the grill
5.gm: The work before the party. Willas [willas] carries driftwood for everybody and shouts at someone for dropping a log; Hedda [hedda] inspects the grill and files objections; Rafa [rafa] has come down from Rare Hall with a tray and feeds whoever stands still; Odalys [odalys] counts her eighteen without seeming to. Everyone here has known everyone else for five days at most: no old friendships, no in-jokes older than Monday. Rowan can haul, lay the fire or stand about being new with the rest. @clock 5–10 an answer.

5.title: The fire is lit; the other dorms come down to the cove
5.gm: Odalys puts the match to it at dusk and the row cheers. Then the entrances, one beat each: Marit [marit] makes one; Sunny [sunny] arrives wet from the sea; Jessica [jessica] comes 'to see how the other half lives' and stays longer than she meant to; Ashton [ashton] hands out roses; Victoria [victoria] sits on a log with her parasol open against the sparks, Ophelia [ophelia] two logs behind her; Sammy [sammy] stands at the edge of the light being mysterious at nobody. One long answer, ending with a free seat on a log beside somebody. @clock 20.

5.title: Singing round the fire
5.gm: Freya [freya] has discovered the drinks and by the second verse conducts the singing with a bottle; Cas [cas] commentates the marshmallows; Trixie [trixie] introduces a moth to people. A free scene: this is where Rowan talks to whoever he chose to sit by — most routes can be opened tonight, each with ONE real exchange, not a tour of the fire. If he stayed in bungalow 7 instead, he hears the row singing through the plank wall, and that is the scene. @clock 0–5 an answer.

5.title: Firelight duels on a driftwood plank
5.gm: Someone lays a plank across two logs and deals. No holograms, cards tilted to the fire to be read, sand in the sleeves: the gentlest first games in front of people Rowan will get. Inya [inya] plays anyone who looks at her; Tomi [tomi] takes small bets; Nathan [nathan] loses loudly and demands a rematch. If Rowan sits down: @duel <whoever asked> casual | nothing but the seat. Winner stays, two games at most for him, then the plank is wanted by others. If he only watches, play one game through in a long answer. @clock 25 a game.

5.title: The talking shell goes round
5.gm: A Commons custom, announced by Odalys: whoever holds the conch tells one TRUE story, and nobody interrupts. Three or four tellers in ONE long answer, each a few lines in their own voice — Baylee [baylee] in two sentences, Livvie [livvie] something dry, Rana [rana] passes the shell on without a word — and Nathan's, which is long and embarrassing and about his brothers. Then the shell reaches Rowan: stop there and let the player tell one or pass. What he tells is remembered by those who heard it. @clock 30.

5.title: Fiona's ghost story
5.gm: The fire is low. Fiona [fiona] tells a ghost story in her deep voice — hers, from Whitby, with a proper ending — and three boys forget to breathe: Sammy, Tobias [tobias], and Gideon [gideon] at the very edge of the light, pretending to be leaving. Rowan only listens: tell the WHOLE story in ONE long answer and end on the silence after it, broken by a log settling and Trixie's shriek. @clock 20.

5.title: Embers: the other dorms walk home, the row is called in
5.gm: The party ends by itself. Rare Hall and the Tower people go up the path in twos and threes with borrowed torches — who walks with whom is noticed; Willas kicks sand over the edge of the fire; Odalys calls the row in by name, without hurry. Rowan gets ONE last exchange (a walk along the wet sand, a word on the bungalow steps) and then it is the boardwalk, the plank wall and Nathan snoring. @did bonfire over. @clock 15, then the night is his.

6.title: The first shuttle cart leaves the main gate
6.gm: Free Saturday. At the porter's lodge everyone signs the town book; the carts leave on the hour, nine to noon, and the last one back leaves Main Street at half past nine tonight (the gate shuts at ten). On Rowan's cart, if he takes this one: Tomi [tomi] with an empty binder, Inya [inya] with a shopping list, Livvie [livvie] with one rare in a hard case and nothing else. Half an hour down the avenue with the harbour opening below. @place main_street on arrival; @clock 30 for the ride.

6.title: Main Street and the Saturday stalls
6.gm: Port Mulligan opens up: unlock town places as Rowan actually walks past them (@known for the café, the arcade, the pawn shop, the harbour, the Sleeve & Binder), one or two per answer, each with what one sees from the pavement. Tomi explains prices as they go — what costs double on campus, what the stalls will haggle on. Rowan's money is tight: let the laundromat arithmetic show in what he picks up and puts back, without comment. @clock 5–10 a stop.

6.title: The Sleeve & Binder: sleeves, a mat, and what singles cost
6.gm: Dex [dex] behind the counter, gruff and fair; Mika [mika] sorting a box with her eyes half shut. Rowan needs sleeves and a mat for real-table play (Dex names the cheap ones first) and discovers at the glass case what single cards cost. At the trade counter Livvie sells her rare with a face like stone, counts the notes twice and leaves at once. Dex mentions the Friday Night Draft and the Saturday events. Buying goes through the shop; the scene ends when Rowan has what he came for or has decided to do without. @clock 10–20.

6.title: The harbour at ferry time
6.gm: The Second Chance is in from the mainland: mail sacks, crates of boosters for both shops, Captain Stroud [abel] counting something on his fingers at the rail. Fishing boats, nets, the smell of the fish market; Josie [josie] is rolling a barrel into The Mulligan and looks at Academy jackets the way one looks at one's own old photographs. A place to sit on a bollard and eat something cheap. At noon the ferry's horn goes and she leaves. The rest of the day in town is Rowan's own; the Night Market opens at six. @clock 10–20.

6.title: Night Market: the lanterns go up on the customs yard
6.gm: Dusk. Stallholders hang paper lanterns from the old crane arm and the first charcoal catches. Half the Academy drifts in from Main Street in clumps by dorm that do not stay clumps. Marit [marit] is being a different person at every stall; Pippa [pippa] is photographing lanterns. Give Rowan the yard in three sensory lines and one familiar face, then let him walk. @clock 5–10.

6.title: Night Market: skewers, carved dice and foreign printings
6.gm: A free scene among the stalls, ONE stall per answer: skewers at 2 cr, carved dice, a rack of foreign-language printings that Mika [mika] is going through with real attention, second-hand sleeves. Tomi [tomi] haggles for sport and will haggle for Rowan if asked. Whoever Rowan walks with gets a quiet exchange between two stalls. Prices are small and still add up. @clock 5–10 a stall.

6.title: The tent at the far end: Madame Oru reads decks
6.gm: At the far end, a tent with one lamp: Madame Oru [oru] reads spreads from the customer's OWN deck, 5 cr. People come out laughing. If Rowan sits down she turns three of his cards and says he sleeps in a room of three, and that one of them 'will keep the bed and lose the sleeper'. No explanation, no repeat, next customer. It must read as carnival patter tonight — nobody present takes it for more. If he does not go in, he only sees the queue. @clock 10.

6.title: Last cart back to the Academy
6.gm: The porter's lad rings a handbell on Main Street at twenty past nine: last cart. Whoever misses it walks the avenue in the dark and finds the gate shut at ten. The ride up is crowded and sleepy, paper bags on knees; somebody's head ends up on somebody's shoulder. @place main_gate, sign back in at the lodge, and the day is over: @clock 30.

7.title: Beach Day: towels down, the lifeguard flag goes up
7.gm: Ten minutes over the headland from the bungalows. Sunny [sunny] plants the flag, climbs the lifeguard chair and blows the whistle once to show she has one; Saoirse [saoirse] lays boards out on the sand; the Commons arrive in a body with Mama's cool box. Baylee [baylee] takes his shirt off and begins, visibly, to burn. Where Rowan puts his towel decides whom he has the afternoon with. @clock 10.

7.title: Volleyball: the Commons against everyone
7.gm: A net between two oars. Sides pick themselves; Inya [inya] plays as if for money, Marit [marit] narrates her own serves, Nathan [nathan] takes a cannonball run-up at the water between points and lands half of it on somebody's playmat. Rowan plays, keeps score or watches from the towels — one or two answers, a set to fifteen, and it ENDS with the losing side carrying the winners' drinks. Sunny flirts from the chair with whoever is nearest. @clock 30 for the set.

7.title: Saoirse's first surfing lesson; the rope swing
7.gm: Saoirse offers a first lesson to anyone who will take orders: ten minutes lying on a board on dry sand, then the small waves by the rocks. If Rowan takes it, three attempts and a fall told with affection; she says one true thing about his balance. The others queue for the rope swing off the leaning palm. Sunny whistles Ed back from the rocks, twice. @clock 30–40.

7.title: The towel table: cards weighted down with shells
7.gm: On a towel in the shade Georgie [georgie], in a sun hat, is annihilating upper-years one after another without looking up; Pippa [pippa] photographs the queue. Cards are held down with shells and still blow. Rowan can ask her for a game (she says yes very quietly; casual-kind, and he will probably lose), play someone else on the next towel, or just lie in the sun and listen. Pure warmth, nothing at stake. @clock 25 a game.

7.title: Last swim; the five-o'clock whistle
7.gm: Long light. A last swim out to the rock and back; Baylee is the colour of a boiled lobster and Mama's verdict is awaited with dread. At five Sunny blows three blasts, takes the flag down and the lifeguard goes off duty; towels are shaken out, the boards go back to the boathouse, the row walks home over the headland in a string. @did beach day over. This is the island at its kindest: keep it simple and let it end. @clock 30.

8.title: Judge Circle: chairs in a ring, the attendance sheet
8.gm: Seminar Room 2B after supper, a dozen chairs pulled into a ring. Noor [noor] chairs — exact, shy, and visibly braver with a rulebook in her hand; Hana [hana] sits at the back marking papers and supervises by not interrupting; Mika [mika] has come up from town with a paper bag of buns. Newcomers sign the sheet and say which ruling they brought. @clock 5.

8.title: The round: 'a ruling I got wrong'
8.gm: Round the ring, each person states a ruling they got wrong and the room argues it to the correct answer; Noor gives the reference, Mika the sleepy one-line version, Hana speaks exactly once. Three or four cases in one or two LONG answers, with real positions taken — use only this game's rules and vocabulary. When it is Rowan's turn, stop and let him bring one (an online habit that is wrong at a real table is ideal). @clock 20 an answer.

8.title: Case of the week: when can a challenge be refused?
8.gm: Someone asks whether one must accept any challenge. Noor answers without opening anything: she quotes the Charter's duel clause from memory, word for word — aloud, by name, before a witness, with a stated ante; deferred once, up to three days — and only then notices that the room has gone quiet. Hana looks up from her marking for the first time. PLANT IT: Noor is the person who knows the Charter by heart (@journal People). One answer. @clock 10.

8.title: Next week's case is set; chairs back
8.gm: Noor sets next Monday's case and thanks everyone too formally; chairs go back in rows because Hana is watching. Mika has the last cart to catch and says goodnight to the room in general. Whoever lingers gets two minutes with Noor at the door, or with Hana at the desk — the first step of two slow routes. @did Judge Circle over. If Rowan sat through the whole circle it counts as study: end the closing answer with @study rj101 instead of @clock (it uses up the rest of the evening).

9.title: Teobalt's birthday: a surprise in the council chamber
9.gm: After the delegates' briefing the council springs it on him: a cake shaped like a clipboard, with a liquorice pencil. Teobalt [teobalt] goes pink, thanks them in three numbered points, and has — it turns out — scheduled eleven minutes for this; he keeps to them. Rowan is part of it only if he knows Teobalt or happens to be in the building; a small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection. One answer. @clock 11.

9.title: Leftover cake goes round the dorms
9.gm: There is far too much cake. Teobalt has drawn up a route — Rare Hall, the Tower lobby, the Commons row — and needs a second pair of hands for the tray: an easy way to meet half the school. If Rowan carries: two or three doors per answer, a different face and one line at each, @place as they go; it ENDS on the boardwalk with the empty tray and a tick on the list. If he does not, the tray goes round without him and a slice turns up in bungalow 7 anyway. @clock 10 a stop.

9.title: The Top Deck: studio doors open, audience seated
9.gm: Thirty folding chairs behind the cameras. Pippa [pippa] is on stills, Marit [marit] is warming up the audience unasked, Vivienne [vivienne] stands at the back with her arms folded and misses nothing. Bex [bex], purple hair under a headset, counts the room and picks her victims with her eyes. Whoever sits in the front row is fair game. The ON AIR lamp comes on at seven. @clock 5–10.

9.title: ON AIR: ladder predictions and the freshman 'ones to watch'
9.gm: Live. Bex's opening monologue, the ladder predictions before the season opens on Friday, then the freshman 'ones to watch' with Pippa's photographs on the screen: Georgie, Gideon, Ashton — and a throwaway joke about 'the Wildcard kid with the online handle', which gets a laugh. Rowan only watches (from the audience, or on the common-room screen if he is elsewhere): play the segment in ONE long answer in Bex's voice and end on the laugh. @clock 20.

9.title: ON AIR: the rules quiz with the studio audience
9.gm: Bex takes a hand microphone into the chairs: three rules questions, three victims. If Rowan is in the audience she may pull him up for thirty seconds on air — a first, small public-nerve test (@check nerve 8 | thirty seconds live on The Top Deck); however it goes she is kind about it on camera. If he is not there, Marit takes the question and answers a different one. Sign-off at 19:40. @clock 15.

9.title: Off air: cables, and the crew sheet
9.gm: The lamp goes out and everybody speaks at normal volume again. Vivienne gives Bex two notes and one compliment, in that order. A crew sheet goes up by the door: camera, cables, chat moderation — shifts are available from tonight (@journal Plans; the job board has the pay). Bex, winding cable, tells Rowan what she actually thought. The show airs every Tuesday and Friday at seven. @did Top Deck premiere over. @clock 10.

10.title: Ladder registration: the clerk's desk is open
10.gm: A form in triplicate at the council chamber. Noor [noor] clerks: she checks every list card by card against the legality sheet and stamps three times. Octavia [octavia] looks at Rowan's grey collar, his handle and his list, in that order, and files him. At the next desk Sebastian Thorne [sebastian], Permits & Sanctions, is pleasant to everyone. If Rowan registers now it takes a quarter of an hour and is DONE (@did deck registered for Season 1; @journal School). The desk shuts at the Evening bell. @clock 15.

10.title: Ed's Expedition No. 1: muster at the tide pools
10.gm: Low water. Ed [ed], hat on, counts his expedition: Tomi [tomi] (who has brought rope to sell and ends up lending it), Trixie [trixie] with a jar, Viktor [viktor], who says he has come to see the pools and looks only at the cliff line — and whoever else read the poster. Ed's briefing is one sentence and a grin. Nothing anyone minds losing is to come further than this rock. @clock 5–10.

10.title: Across the pools to the north end
10.gm: Twenty minutes over weed and barnacles, one or two finds per answer: Trixie names everything in every pool and apologises to a crab; Ed wants to know of each thing whether it stings; Viktor asks Tomi, idly, what the fishermen call the coves further north. Someone goes in to the knee. The tide has turned — say so. @clock 10 an answer.

10.title: The blowhole on the rising tide
10.gm: A slot in the rock at the north end that breathes, then throws spray four metres up with a thump one feels in the feet. Ed wants to stand ON it. It is merely stupid rather than lethal: soaked, knocked flat, skinned palms. What Rowan does matters more to Ed than the spray (plot file q_ed_places_to_die): laugh, forbid, tie Tomi's rope round him, or stand there with him (@check nerve 9 | stand on the blowhole when it goes). Play the blast ONCE, properly. @clock 10–15.

10.title: The tide is coming in: back along the rocks
10.gm: Viktor says, without raising his voice, that the first gully is filling, and is believed at once. Back over the pools faster than they came, wet to the waist at the last crossing; Ed is radiant and bleeding slightly; Tomi wants his rope back dry. Whoever dawdles is cut off and loses the rest of the afternoon and a boot. On the sand someone remembers that ladder registration closes at the Evening bell. @did Expedition No. 1 over. @clock 20.

10.title: Last call: the queue down the corridor
10.gm: Forty-five minutes to the bell and the queue reaches the stairs: everyone who meant to do it yesterday. Teobalt [teobalt] walks the line handing out forms and pencils. Noor does not hurry and does not make mistakes. Whoever is still out on the rocks or the Terraces is told by somebody that it is now or the penalty. If Rowan has already registered, this is only seen in passing. @clock 10–15.

10.title: The Evening bell: the register is closed
10.gm: At the first stroke Noor rules a line under the last name and caps her pen. Anyone behind the line is late: late forms go to Sebastian's desk tomorrow, and he rules on them warmly and to the letter — ten ranks' penalty, no exceptions, a smile. If Rowan forgot, he learns this now or at breakfast. Season 1 opens on Friday morning at the board on the Quad. @clock 5.

10.title: Supper on the row; something is in Mama's oven
10.gm: Ordinary supper at the long table, except that the kitchen smells of honey and Odalys [odalys] slaps every hand that goes near the oven door. It is the first birthday on the row and nobody has known Trixie [trixie] ten days — Mama bakes anyway. Whoever knows what day it is is told to keep quiet with a look. One meal, eaten once (@did supper eaten). @clock 25.

10.title: Trixie's birthday cake
10.gm: Lights off, candles in. Trixie cries with happiness before anyone has sung a note, blows them out in three goes, and NAMES the cake (the name is hers to choose; it is a good one). The row sings badly. A small present, or simply having remembered, is worth real affection; nobody is blamed tonight for not knowing. She cuts the first slice and does not eat it. @clock 15.

10.title: The first slice goes to the bee hotel
10.gm: Trixie carries the first slice out along the boardwalk on a saucer, half the row behind her, and sets it under the bee hotel she nailed to the post by bungalow 2: 'for the girls'. Hedda approves on principle; Freya holds the torch. Then back in for the rest of the cake, and the party ends when the plate is empty (@did Trixie's birthday cake eaten). @clock 10.

11.title: Movie Night: cushions down, the screen comes down
11.gm: The pull-down screen sticks, as it will all year. Bex [bex] runs the projector; Tomi [tomi] sells popcorn he did not make; people arrive with cushions and stake out floor. Where Rowan sits, and next to whom, is the whole decision of the evening: Inya [inya] has saved nothing for anybody and says so, Pippa [pippa] is by the wall. Lights out at eight. @clock 5–10.

11.title: Tonight's feature: an old pirate picture
11.gm: Black and white, cutlasses, a ship that is obviously a model. Marit [marit] narrates over the first reel until she is silenced with a cushion. Play the film in TWO answers at most: the dark, the room's reactions, and ONE quiet moment with whoever Rowan sat beside — a whisper, a shared bag, a shoulder — which is the real scene. Nothing has to happen. End on THE END and the lights. @clock 50 an answer.

11.title: Lights up; cushions back; the walk home
11.gm: Blinking. Bex rewinds, Tomi counts his takings, cushions fly back onto the sofas. People leave arguing about whether the parrot was real. Rowan walks back with whoever he sat next to, as far as their ways go together. Movie Night runs every other Thursday. @did movie night over. @clock 10–15.

12.title: The split-flap ladder board comes to life
12.gm: Before first period the big board on the Quad clatters through all 144 names and stops. A crowd in every state of dress reads it: Lilia Mann at #1 with a gap under her that looks deliberate; Georgie at 42 on day one; Nathan about 120 and delighted; Rowan about 128 (from his Placement result); Magnus [magnus] at 126, furious about the two places and saying so to his tablet. Printed sheets are handed out by Zeynep [zeynep]. @journal School. @clock 10.

12.title: Prof. Santángel opens Season 1 from the steps
12.gm: Santángel [santangel], black turtleneck, three minutes: ranked play is open. Challenge anyone within twenty ranks; book a Trial Dome or meet on the Terraces; results are stamped at the registrar's table or they did not happen; rank moves with every ranked duel; the top eight at each snapshot qualify for events — first snapshot Day 31. He promises nothing above 'adequate'. Lilia [lilia] stands behind him and looks at the horizon. One answer; this is the ladder tutorial. @clock 5.

12.title: First challenges on the Terraces before the bell
12.gm: Half an hour before class and the Terraces are full: Dom [dom], Kenji [kenji] and Priya [priya] each take a table and a queue of challengers, playing fast. First-years dare each other. Rowan can make or take his first ranked challenge now (@duel <id> ladder | rank) if someone within twenty places is to hand — Magnus is, and is looking for him — or fix it for the lunch break. The bell at 08:55 empties the steps: Friday is Card Design, then the Practicum. @clock 5–10.

12.title: Lunch break on the Terraces: the season's first ranked afternoon
12.gm: After the Midday class the Terraces fill properly. On the middle terrace Brant [brant] and his two hangers-on have a table of their own and are 'trading' first-years — Sammy, Trixie, Mikoto — out of their rares: unequal swaps, pressed with a smile and a hand on the shoulder. Nathan [nathan] tells him, at full volume and across two terraces, exactly what he thinks of that. Brant remembers faces. Rowan can step in, back Nathan, pull the first-years away, or keep his head down and play his own ranked game. @clock 5–10.

12.title: Freya's First Friday: a driftwood fire at the cove
12.gm: After the bonfire at the pit has burnt down, the party moves over the headland. Freya [freya] — twelve days on the island and already running its social calendar — receives people at a driftwood fire like a head of state and checks that each has brought a cup. Trixie [trixie] and Hedda [hedda] are her staff. The first year out of uniform; people are still learning each other's names and getting them wrong. @clock 5–10.

12.title: Swimming in the dark
12.gm: Somebody runs at the water and then everybody does. Sunny [sunny] counts heads from the shallows out of habit; Saoirse [saoirse] floats on her back beyond the break and talks to the sky; Cas [cas] commentates from the towel he has not left. If Rowan goes in: black water, cold to the ribs, a voice close by that he has to recognise without a face — one quiet exchange out there. If not, the fire and whoever also stayed dry. @clock 15–20.

12.title: Toasts — and far too much to drink
12.gm: Freya's toasts, in ascending order of grandeur: to the row, to the north, to people whose names she has now definitely learnt. She is magnificent — funny, exact, the centre of the fire. Bottles go round faster than is wise. Rowan can drink, pretend to, or not; nobody presses a second time. Some people go home about now, in pairs. Let the night thin out by itself. @clock 10 an answer.

12.title: About one: the fire is down, and Freya needs walking home
12.gm: About one o'clock the magnificence stops quite suddenly. Freya sits down in the sand, very upright, and announces that the headland has become steeper. Trixie cannot carry her; Hedda is asleep. Whoever walks her back over the rocks to bungalow 2 hears what she says when she is not performing, and is asked in the morning what she said (plot file q_freya_northern_lights). If Rowan has gone, it is Sunny who does it. @did First Friday over. @clock 30.

13.title: Harbour Market: the stalls open along Main Street and the quay
13.gm: Bigger than the weekly stalls: the whole street and the quay, awnings to the water. Produce, rope, carved dice, a knife-grinder, and tables of second-hand cards. Josie [josie] is buying limes for The Mulligan by the crate. The first carts from the Academy unload at half past eight. Give the market in a few sensory lines and one stall per answer. @clock 5–10.

13.title: Mama Odalys does the week's shopping
13.gm: Odalys [odalys] works down the stalls with a list she does not look at, haggling in two languages; Baylee [baylee] and Rafa [rafa] are her porters and are already loaded. A third pair of arms would be welcome: a job-like favour (no pay; she remembers it, and there is a pastry in it). Rafa asks the stallholders what they cook with things; Baylee carries a sack of rice like a cushion. @clock 10 an answer; the round takes forty minutes.

13.title: The second-hand tables: playmats, binders, old printings
13.gm: Playmats and binders for a fraction of campus prices, and ONE stall of old printings worth digging through — a shoebox of commons at a credit each in which there may be something. Dex [dex] is going through it himself with a jeweller's loupe and will say what a thing is worth if asked straight; Mika [mika] buys a mat with a coffee ring on it and is happy. If Rowan digs: ten minutes and one modest find at most. @clock 10–15.

13.title: The kitchen cart is loaded on the quay
13.gm: On the quay the Commons cart is loaded to the rails; Odalys counts sacks, pays the last stall and climbs up beside the driver. Baylee walks behind so that nothing falls off. Whoever carried gets the pastry now. The market goes on until two; Prof. Ashdown's field section musters at the main gate at eleven for those who signed. @did Mama's market round done. @clock 10.

13.title: Field section: roll call at the main gate
13.gm: Prof. Ashdown [ashdown] in field boots with a clipboard: names from the sign-up sheet at the faculty wing, water bottles shown, sandals sent back. About a dozen students — Noor [noor] with a notebook, Pippa [pippa] with two cameras, Felix [felix] with paper and wax for rubbings, and Viktor [viktor], who has never come to anything. Her rules, crisply: stay behind me, touch nothing unasked, the site is not a playground. Whoever is not on the list does not come. @clock 10.

13.title: Up the jungle trail
13.gm: An hour and a quarter of climbing under the canopy, the party strung out. Ashdown sets the pace and talks over her shoulder about what the first surveyors thought they had found. ONE moment per answer among the walkers — Pippa changing film on the move, Noor asking a question with a footnote, Viktor reading the ground rather than the trees. @clock 30–40 an answer; arrive at the ravine at half past twelve.

13.title: The rope bridge, one at a time
13.gm: The Split: a ravine, a bridge of rope and planks, water a long way down. One at a time, Ashdown first and without looking. A small test of Nerve for Rowan (@check nerve 8 | cross the rope bridge without freezing); a failure is only slow and public. Viktor crosses as if it were a pavement and then looks back along the far bank, measuring something. @clock 15.

13.title: On site: Prof. Ashdown lectures among the ruins
13.gm: Low walls in the grass, a paved avenue, mosaics under tin roofs. Ashdown lectures on site, crisp and guarded: dates, what is known, what is not claimed. First sight of the mosaics — and some of the figures look like card heroes; she lets the group notice by itself and says 'coincidence is the first hypothesis'. One trench stays under a tarpaulin and is not on the tour. Rowan mostly listens: one or two LONG answers with real lecture, and one chance to ask. @clock 30 an answer.

13.title: Rubbings for credit; questions
13.gm: Wax and paper: each student takes one rubbing of a border tile for credit and hands it in before the party leaves. Viktor asks, casually, where the avenue leads. 'To a rock face,' says Ashdown, and asks Felix about his paper. He does not ask twice, and he will not come on a section again. Whoever watches her sees that the question was not casual to her either. @clock 20.

13.title: The walk back to the gate
13.gm: Back over the bridge and down, quicker than up. At the first rest Ashdown announces a second section for Saturday of week six (Day 41) and takes names. Tired, easy talk on the way down; whoever Rowan walks with has the long scene of the afternoon. At the gate about half past four she counts the party, thanks nobody and is gone. @did field section over. @clock 40–60 an answer; a handed-in rubbing counts as study for Lore — end the LAST answer with @study lh101 instead of @clock.

13.title: Bungalow 7, the night before inspection
13.gm: Inspection is tomorrow at eleven and everybody on the row knows it. Baylee's [baylee] corner is already perfect: blanket squared, boots in a line. Nathan's [nathan] side is a crime scene — clothes, wrappers, the evidence notebook, something that was once a sandwich — and he maintains that inspectors respect character. Helping him shovel it clean is a roommate scene worth having: what turns up under the bed, what he says when he is embarrassed. If Rowan does not, the room goes in as it is. @clock 30 for the job.

14.title: Inspection: the row is rung to its doors
14.gm: Odalys [odalys] beats the triangle on the kitchen porch: everybody to their own door. Tavita Leota [tavita], the head proctor, leads the council delegates along the boardwalk with the warden and explains the rule once, kindly: beds made, floor clear, no food in the rooms, nothing nailed to the walls. Every room has ONE free warning; a slip is written only the second time. Teobalt [teobalt] carries the clipboard. @clock 10.

14.title: The rounds: bungalows 2 to 6
14.gm: Door by door, about ten minutes each, heard and half seen from Rowan's own step. TWO bungalows per answer, one beat each: B2 (Trixie's matchboxes are livestock, argues Hedda), B3 (Livvie's third is immaculate; Rana answers in three words), B4 (Maisie's wiring earns the row's first warning), B5 (Ed's island map is pinned, not nailed — Tavita checks), B6 (Dmitri is still in bed and is inspected in it). Odalys's spoon points; Tavita's voice never rises. @clock 20 an answer.

14.title: Bungalow 7 is inspected
14.gm: Tavita has to duck under the lintel. Baylee's corner: perfect, and Tavita says so. Rowan's: whatever the player has made of it. Nathan's: as it was left last night — if nobody helped him it is the crime scene, he gets the room's free warning with a speech in his own defence, and a second failure will cost all three a weekend chore. Teobalt looks up, notes the stain on the ceiling over Rowan's bed and writes 'roof — B7' (it is mended within the week). @clock 15.

14.title: The list is read out on the kitchen porch
14.gm: Tavita reads the list from the porch steps: passes, warnings, no slips today. Odalys adds her own verdicts, which are not on the form. Teobalt reads out three repairs he has noted for the row and the days on which they will be done. Then Sunday lunch is on the table, the delegates are made to stay for it, and the inspection is OVER (@did dorm inspection done). @clock 10.

15.title: The half-door is open: tea is poured
15.gm: Behind the Design Lab the top half of the workshop door stands open, which is the whole invitation. Inside: a kettle, mismatched mugs, twenty people on stools, crates and the floor. Wren [wren] pours tea in her pyjamas. Chuck Kaboom [chuck] cannot find his glasses, his notes or the sugar and is happy about all three. Inya [inya] sits at the very back, being an ordinary fan. First chance to see the Founder up close: let Rowan find a seat and look at the walls. @clock 5–10.

15.title: The Founder tells a story 'from when I knew them'
15.gm: Chuck tells one story about the heroes of the game with total conviction, as a man tells of old friends — who cheated at dice, who could not swim — and corrects himself on details nobody could check. The room adores it. Facts are not guaranteed. He looks at the back row exactly once and looks away too quickly; so does she. Rowan only listens: play the WHOLE story in ONE long answer, in Chuck's wandering voice, ending on the applause and the kettle. @clock 30.

15.title: Chuck plays all comers with his impossible pile
15.gm: Chuck clears a corner of the workbench and takes on anyone with a mixed pile of cards that cannot possibly work and does, about half the time; he narrates his own mistakes with pleasure. If Rowan asks: @duel chuck casual | a story if you win. While others play, the oldest sketches on the far wall are worth a look (faded, pinned at child height, older than the game). Inya is asked by a neighbour whether she wants a go and says she is 'just watching' — badly. @clock 20–25 a game.

15.title: Wren shuts the half-door
15.gm: Wren collects the mugs, which is the signal. Chuck is steered towards something he was supposed to sign an hour ago; the stools empty. He says goodbye to people by the wrong names and means it kindly. The story hour is open most Mondays, when the half-door is (@journal Plans). Inya is the first out and does not wait for anybody. @did story hour over. @clock 5.

15.title: Eberhart's birthday: he trains
15.gm: No party. Eberhart [eberhart] is in the gym at half past six as on every evening, jacket folded on the bench, working through his sets in silence. Whoever turns up and says 'happy birthday' gets a short nod and — this is the present he gives back — a place beside him at the rack; he corrects a grip without a word. A small gift or simply having remembered counts with him far more than he shows. If Rowan trains through with him, tell the hour in one answer (@clock 60); otherwise @clock 10.

15.title: A banner in Rare Hall
15.gm: Seen through the open door of R101 from the first-floor landing: Mikoto [mikoto] has made a banner — HAPPY BIRTHDAY EBI, the letters getting smaller toward the edge — and hung it over Eberhart's bed, and is now worried it is too much. Eberhart comes back from the gym, reads it for a long moment and says 'It is straight.' From him that is a great deal. (The banner stays up exactly one day; afterwards it lies folded square in his footlocker all year.) @clock 5.

16.title: Practice Night: tables claimed, lamps lit
16.gm: The Terraces under strings of lamps, every first-year with a deck box. At the foot of the steps Zeynep [zeynep] has the Freshman Cup forms beside her ladder stamp: first-years only, free entry, registration closes on Thursday (Day 18) — not registering costs standing with Coach Rox. If Rowan signs now it is DONE (@did registered for the Freshman Cup). Tables fill by dorm and then mix. @clock 5–10.

16.title: Open testing: play a game, swap tables
16.gm: Every first-year is testing. One opponent per answer; after a game people swap. Good for learning decks: whoever Rowan plays or watches closely gives up real deck knowledge (@deck <id>). On offer: Inya [inya], who plays as if it were the final; Baylee [baylee], who apologises for a good play; Noor [noor], who announces every step; Sunny [sunny], still learning and unbothered; Ashton [ashton] for an audience; Gideon [gideon] only by appointment. @duel <id> casual | practice. @clock 25 a game.

16.title: Tomi opens the book on the Cup
16.gm: Tomi [tomi] chalks odds on the inside of his binder lid and takes small bets on the Cup: Georgie [georgie] is the favourite at odds nobody will take, Gideon second, long prices on every grey collar including Rowan (he may back himself, up to 20 cr). Rana [rana] must play the Freshman Cup a second time and snaps at the first person who says so — tonight that is Nathan [nathan], cheerfully. She takes her deck to the top terrace and tests alone. @clock 5–10.

16.title: Late tables: somebody shows you something
16.gm: The crowd thins and the useful part begins: a friend sits down across from Rowan and TEACHES — one concrete thing about tempo, about his hands at a real table, about a matchup he will meet on Friday (whoever is closest to him by now; if a technique's source condition is met, this is the moment). Up on the top terrace Rana can be joined by someone who does not mention the Cup. One real scene, not three. @clock 20–30.

16.title: Lamps out on the Terraces
16.gm: Zeynep packs her stamp at a quarter past nine and the lamps go out string by string. Last words on the steps: the Cup is on Friday, registration closes Thursday, the roster goes up Friday morning on the arena doors. People walk home comparing what they saw. @did practice night over. @clock 10.

17.title: Swim Meet: warm-up, dorm benches, the fourth swimmer
17.gm: Lane ropes in dorm colours, three benches, Coach Rox [rox] with a whistle and a clipboard. Jessica [jessica] presides from a lounger in sunglasses and is somehow the centre of the hall. The Commons relay is one swimmer short and the whole bench turns and looks at Rowan. He can swim the fourth leg (fitness, and the row's affection whatever the time), take a stopwatch at the timekeepers' table — Sunny [sunny] hands them out from the lifeguard chair — or sit and shout. Decide before the first heat. @clock 10.

17.title: Individual heats
17.gm: Fifty-metre heats, called by Rox. Priya [priya] wins hers in complete silence; Saoirse [saoirse] swims hers on her back for the pleasure of it and is disqualified, laughing; Sunny wins everything she enters by a body length and climbs straight back on the chair. If Rowan is timekeeping, this is a Sunny scene between heats: she leans down to check his watch more often than necessary. Otherwise one long answer from the benches. @clock 30.

17.title: The dorm relays
17.gm: Four by fifty, three dorms, the whole hall on its feet. If Rowan swims: the wait on the block, the changeover, the wall (@check fitness 8 | fourth leg for the Commons) — a good leg takes the Commons past the Tower into second, a bad one is forgiven before he is out of the water. Rare Hall wins because of Sunny's last leg, as everybody knew. Tell the race ONCE, properly, in one long answer. @clock 15.

17.title: Results from the lifeguard chair
17.gm: Rox reads the times and the dorm points: Rare Hall, then by what happened. A dented cup is handed up to Sunny, who hands it down to her bench. Jessica awards a prize of her own invention to the most elegant loser. The swim squad trains Wednesdays; Rox says to Rowan in passing whatever is true about what she saw. @did swim meet over. Open swim until six. @clock 10.

18.title: Inya's birthday: tres leches with a bunny piped on it
18.gm: After supper Odalys [odalys] carries it in: a tres leches with a piped rabbit that has, by accident, a very stern face. Inya [inya] says 'Rude,' is delighted, and defends the rabbit against Nathan's criticism. The row sings. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection with her; forgetting costs a little if they are close. One meal's worth of cake, eaten once (@did Inya's cake eaten). @clock 20.

18.title: A parcel by the kitchen door
18.gm: Somebody finds a parcel on the step by the kitchen door: brown paper, string, no stamp, no name but hers. Inside is a hand-carved wooden rabbit, old, the paint worn off the ears by handling. Inya goes still for one second, then tells the table it is 'from home' and puts it in her hoodie pocket, and keeps her hand there. Nobody at the table knows more than that; do not explain it. Whoever watched her face knows it mattered. @clock 5.

18.title: Afterwards, on the boardwalk
18.gm: The kitchen empties. Tomorrow morning the Freshman Cup roster goes up with legal names; tonight is the last evening on which she is only Inya Bell, and she knows it and is restless — walks the boardwalk, shuffles, will not sit. If she TRUSTS Rowan (a real friendship by now, and he is the one who comes out after her), she may tell him herself tonight, in her own blunt way, and ask him not to be weird about it. If not, she talks about the Cup and goes in early. @clock 10–20.

19.title: The Freshman Cup roster goes up on the arena doors
19.gm: Zeynep [zeynep] pins the roster to the arena doors and a copy at the job board: 36 names in alphabetical order, LEGAL names. 'KABOOM, Inya.' A crowd forms; within minutes the reverent whispering she hates has begun, people who ignored her yesterday want to say hello, and Gideon [gideon] alone is not surprised. Inya [inya] stands in front of the list with her deck box in both hands. How Rowan treats her in the NEXT HOUR — the same as yesterday, or not — matters a great deal. First-years are excused from today's classes for the Cup. @clock 5–10.

19.title: Check-in, deck check, players' meeting
19.gm: At the Trial Domes: check-in at the judges' table, lists compared with the registered ones by Lucas [lucas] and Anni [anni], decks counted. Pilar [pilar] hands armbands to her crew (scorekeepers and runners, 20 cr a day, paid this evening at Imara's table). At 10:30 the players' meeting: Ms Kirishima [hana], head judge, gives the format in six sentences — all 36, four Swiss rounds today, one game a round, forty minutes on the clock, call a judge rather than argue; top eight on the arena stage tomorrow. Santángel [santangel] watches from the gallery. Pairings go up at 10:55. @clock by what Rowan does; free time until then.

19.title: Freshman Cup: Swiss round 1
19.gm: Round 1 — Rowan's first tournament game; Nerve matters. Feature tables in Domes 1–4, the rest on the gallery tables. His pairing is on the board: a first-year he has not played much (pick by the story; not Georgie yet). @duel <id> tournament | Freshman Cup, round 1 — play it out. Around him: Nathan [nathan] loses his round while narrating his own hand aloud; Georgie [georgie] wins in eleven minutes without looking up. Results slips to the scorekeepers. If Rowan is not playing, summarise the round in one answer. @clock to 11:45.

19.title: Second Desk: headsets on for round 1
19.gm: The Top Deck's second desk — two chairs, one camera, the feed from the gallery tables — is staffed by first-year Auxiliary students. Cas [cas] has prepared four pages of notes; Victoria [victoria] has prepared a ribbon. Bex [bex] counts them in through the glass with the face of someone lending out her car. Rowan is at his own table at this hour: he hears of this at lunch or catches it on a screen, unless he is not playing. @clock 5.

19.title: Second Desk live: Cas calls the play, Victoria describes the cards
19.gm: Cas calls the play in his rich broadcast voice. Victoria, beside him, says nothing about the game at all: in complete, serious sentences she describes the CARDS — a border, a palette, the expression of a creature that is about to be destroyed. After ninety seconds Bex wants her off; the chat wants more, and says so in capitals. Ophelia [ophelia] watches from the studio door with her arms crossed. One long answer if Rowan sees it. (Plot file q_victoria_aesthetics.) @clock 20.

19.title: Freshman Cup: Swiss round 2
19.gm: Pairings by record. Play this one out too if round 1 was (or summarise if the player wants pace): @duel <id> tournament | Freshman Cup, round 2. Gideon is at table one, smooth, and audibly contemptuous of grey collars when he is paired down; Baylee [baylee] wins his game and looks round to see whether that was allowed; scouts from the inn — two strangers in linen jackets with notebooks — have appeared on the gallery. Lunch break follows at 12:35. @clock to 12:35.

19.title: Between rounds: the verdict on the second desk
19.gm: Off air between rounds. Bex has the viewer numbers in her hand and hates them for being good. Vivienne [vivienne] gives her ruling from the doorway: it is not commentary, and it stays on for round two. Cas is generous about it; Victoria has not noticed that anything was in question. Ophelia leaves before she can be seen to have been there. @clock 5.

19.title: Lunch break; standings on the board
19.gm: Forty minutes. The first standings sheet goes up by the Mess door: who is 2–0 (Georgie, Gideon, Inya and a few more), who is out of the running already. Tomi [tomi] adjusts his odds over a tray. One meal, eaten once; the talk is all matchups. Whoever Rowan eats with tells him one true thing about his next opponent. Rana [rana] eats nothing and shuffles. Back at the domes by a quarter past one. @clock 35.

19.title: Freshman Cup: Swiss round 3
19.gm: Round 3: summarise Rowan's game in one answer unless it decides his top eight (then @duel <id> tournament | round 3). THE scene of this round is at another table: Rana, repeating the year, has a won position and at match point her hands stall — she takes the safe line, the wrong line, any line but the one that ends it — and loses, unless someone steadies her beforehand or from the rail (a word, a look, not coaching: Hana is watching). Whoever saw it does not mention it to her. @clock to 14:05.

19.title: Freshman Cup: Swiss round 4
19.gm: Last round; the bubble. If Rowan can still make the top eight, this is his game: @duel <id> tournament | Freshman Cup, round 4 — win and in. Otherwise summarise. Georgie finishes 4–0; Fiona [fiona] wins her fourth and surprises everyone but her own bungalow; Sammy goes 2–2 and is thrilled; Victoria, 0–4, is content, having looked at a great many cards. The scouts write. @clock to 14:55.

19.title: Standings read out: the top eight for the arena
19.gm: Ms Kirishima reads the final standings from the bottom up; the eight for tomorrow get a card with their seed (default, see the plot timeline: Georgie, Gideon, Inya, Magnus, Fiona, Eberhart, Noor, Ashton — Rowan takes a place if he earned it). Bracket draw tomorrow at ten, arena doors at two. Rana has gone before her name is read. Pilar's crew is paid at Imara's [imara] table in the council room this evening. @did Freshman Cup day one over. The rest of the day is free. @clock 20.

20.title: Top eight: bracket draw and stage walk-through
20.gm: Saturday, the empty arena. The eight (and anyone who wants to watch from the stands) meet Ms Kirishima [hana] on the stage: seeds one to eight into the bracket, 1 v 8, 4 v 5, 2 v 7, 3 v 6; matches are best of three. Gani [gani] walks them through the stage — where to stand, which lamp means the table is live, do not look at the crowd audio. Georgie [georgie] counts the steps to her chair. If Rowan is in the eight, this is where his stomach finds out. Free until the doors open at two. @clock 20.

20.title: Open tables on the Terraces for everyone else
20.gm: The twenty-eight who are out play it off on the Terraces: open tables, no stakes but pride, and an unofficial 'wooden spoon' bracket that Nathan [nathan] has organised and is losing. Tomi [tomi] runs his book on the afternoon. Rana is not there. A free late morning: one or two games (@duel <id> casual | Terraces), lunch, and whom Rowan will sit with in the stands — unless he is playing, in which case somebody makes him eat. @clock 25 a game.

20.title: Arena doors open; The Top Deck goes live
20.gm: The Great Arena with its lights on and half the school in the stands, sitting by dorm. Bex [bex] and Vivienne [vivienne] are at the commentary desk; Gani [gani] has the projector rig humming. If Rowan made the top eight he waits in the tunnel with the other seven and can hear his own handle read out; if not, he sits in the stands with whoever he chooses — make that choice a scene. The Chancellor [okonkwo] takes her seat at 14:25 and the noise drops. @clock 10–15.

20.title: Quarter-finals
20.gm: Four matches, two at a time, best of three. Default: Georgie over Ashton, Inya over Eberhart, Gideon over Noor, Magnus over Fiona — the closest match of the day. If Rowan is in: this is the first great Nerve test, on a stage, under lights, with crowd audio (@duel <id> tournament | Freshman Cup quarter-final), and the bracket is his to change. If he watches: ONE long answer with the desk's voices and the stand's reactions, the Fiona match told properly. @clock to 15:30.

20.title: Semi-finals
20.gm: Default: Georgie over Inya — who plays the best match of her life and loses it, and says 'Rude' to nobody — and Gideon over Magnus. If Rowan is still in, his semi-final is played out (@duel <id> tournament | semi-final). Inya comes up into the stands afterwards and sits down hard next to whoever was decent to her yesterday morning. One long answer for matches he only watches. @clock to 16:20.

20.title: Interval: the stage is reset for the final
20.gm: Twenty minutes. Gani resets the table and re-aims the lamps; the desk fills the air with predictions; Tomi [tomi] closes his book. In the tunnel mouth, half in shadow, Lilia Mann [lilia] has come to watch the final and speaks to nobody. A moment for Rowan with his neighbour in the stands, or alone with his hands in the tunnel if he is the finalist. @clock 15.

20.title: The final, best of three
20.gm: Default: Georgie Santa [georgie] beats Gideon Pryce [gideon] 2–0, with the small frown she wears when a thing is going as calculated; he does nothing wrong and it is not close. If Rowan is in the final it is played out (@duel <id> tournament | Freshman Cup final) and its result stands. Lilia watches every turn and leaves before the handshake; if Rowan played with spine at any point today, she has remembered his handle. As a spectator: ONE long answer, both games. @clock to 17:30.

20.title: Prize-giving at dusk
20.gm: The Chancellor on the stage: 400 cr, a small ugly cup, and the winner's name to be painted on the arena wall. Georgie has to be nudged forward by Pippa. Gideon is gracious on camera, word-perfect — and in the corridor afterwards, where only someone who followed would see it, he breaks a pen in his fist. The stands empty towards supper; tonight is Night Market in town, carts from the gate. @did Freshman Cup over. @clock 20.

21.title: Saoirse's birthday: no party, boards on the slip
21.gm: She has taken the day off everything. At the boathouse the doors stand open as always and boards are laid out on the slip. Anyone who turns up — with a present, with a 'happy birthday', or by accident — is handed a board before they have finished the sentence; Saoirse [saoirse] is barefoot, salt to the eyebrows and in the best mood of her year. Remembering the day counts; making a fuss does not. @clock 5–10.

21.title: Out past the break
21.gm: The afternoon on the water off the boathouse beach: paddling out, waiting, the one wave. If Rowan goes: two answers at most — what she shouts across the water, what she says sitting on her board between sets when nobody else can hear, one ride or one spectacular failure. She does not talk about the team today and changes the subject once if asked. If he stays ashore he minds the camp stove with whoever else did. @clock 40 an answer.

21.title: Tea on the camp stove
21.gm: Wet hair, tin mugs. On her hammock lies a present wrapped with a ruler-straight ribbon: the tournament rulebook, from Dom Achterberg, as a joke that is also a remark. Saoirse laughs, weighs it in her hand and slides it under the short leg of the camp stove, which now stands level for the first time. 'Best thing he ever gave anybody.' The kettle boils; people drift home with the light. @did Saoirse's birthday over. @clock 15.

22.title: A picket line at the kitchen steps
22.gm: After the Midday class the row comes down to lunch and finds Hedda [hedda] on the kitchen steps: one placard (MEAT IS MURDER — ALSO ON TUESDAYS; it is Monday), one megaphone, flowers in her hair. She lets people through and shames them by name. Baylee [baylee] takes his plate out and eats on the bottom step, between the two fronts, because that is where he always sits. Trixie [trixie] holds the spare placard the wrong way up. @clock 5.

22.title: Megaphone against wooden spoon
22.gm: Odalys [odalys] comes to the door with the spoon. Twelve years she has fed this row. The exchange is loud, fast and — on Mama's side — unhurried; Hedda has facts, Odalys has lunch. The row takes sides with its forks. Rowan can speak for either, try to broker something, or eat: play it in one or two answers and do NOT let anybody win on volume. Rafa [rafa] appears in the doorway behind Mama, wiping his hands, and keeps looking at the back of the stove. @clock 10.

22.title: Mama lifts a lid
22.gm: It ends like this. Odalys goes in and lifts the lid of the pot that has stood on the back ring since Day 3 with an H chalked on it: nothing in it that ever had a face — and Rafa has been improving it daily. She fills a bowl, sets it on the step and says: 'Thirty paces from my stove with that horn, mija, or you peel.' Hedda looks at the bowl, at the chalked H, at the megaphone. Hedda peels: a sack of potatoes on the porch, placard against the wall, and the bowl is empty when Mama collects it. (Plot file q_hedda_cause.) @did picket settled. @clock 15.

22.title: Study groups: tables by course, sign-up sheets out
22.gm: After dinner the long tables on the Library's ground floor carry cardboard signs: PROBABILITY, RULES, LORE, TEMPO. Teobalt [teobalt] has made the sheets and a seating plan nobody follows. Standing groups for the whole term, meeting Monday and Thursday evenings: joining one is the low-effort way to keep a grade up. Rowan picks a table (or none) — who sits there is half the choice. @clock 5–10.

22.title: First session at the table you chose
22.gm: An hour of real work in whispers. PROBABILITY: Noor [noor] and Teobalt run it; Georgie [georgie], brought along by Pippa, corrects the answer key in pencil and is right. RULES: flashcards, fast. LORE: Baylee [baylee] sits there with the reading open at the same page for a long time and will not ask — noticing, and helping without making it a thing, is a friendship beat. Livvie [livvie] works two tables at once. One or two answers at Rowan's table. @clock 30 an answer.

22.title: Books shut: the meeting days are fixed
22.gm: Teobalt reads out the groups and their evenings (Monday and Thursday, seven o'clock, same tables) and pins the list by the tutor desk. If Rowan signed: @journal Plans, and the first session counts — end the closing answer with @study <that course> instead of @clock. Whoever shared his table walks out with him as far as the Quad. @did study groups formed.

23.title: Squall warning: shutters closed, boats in
23.gm: The harbourmaster's notice is on every board and the sky in the south-west is the colour of slate. Silas [silas] limps along the row testing shutters with the flat of his hand and says which bungalows will leak. Odalys [odalys] has the row carry in the porch chairs, the washing and the bee hotel. The air is dead still and warm. Rowan helps batten bungalow 7 or is told to. @clock 10–15.

23.title: The squall hits the row
23.gm: It arrives all at once: horizontal rain, the palms flat, the boardwalk under a hand of water. Roofs leak into saucepans. The Commons spends it bailing and laughing — Baylee [baylee] holds a torn shutter on with his bare hands for twenty minutes because letting go seems rude; Nathan [nathan] narrates the storm like a title fight; Inya [inya] and Livvie [livvie] run a bucket chain out of bungalow 3. One or two answers of happy chaos with Rowan in the middle of it. @clock 20 an answer.

23.title: Sitting it out in Mama's kitchen
23.gm: The worst is over and it simply rains. Half the row steams round Odalys's stove in blankets; she feeds whoever comes in once and hangs their socks over the range. THE quiet scene of the evening: one person who ran in from the rain beside Rowan on the bench — whoever the story has been leaning towards — and nothing to do but talk while it drums on the roof. (He may equally have sheltered elsewhere — the greenhouse, a porch — with one other person: same scene.) @clock 0–5 an answer.

23.title: The wind drops; the damage round by lantern
23.gm: By nine it is a drizzle. Silas and Odalys walk the row with a storm lantern: two shutters, a length of boardwalk rail, the roof of bungalow 7 again. Everybody is counted, dry clothes are found, the saucepans are emptied one last time. By morning the island will be washed clean and bright. @did squall over. @clock 15.

24.title: The observatory is unlocked: up the hill with jackets
24.gm: A clear night after the storm. The astronomy club's key turns in the old lock at ten and a dozen people climb the iron stair into the dome with torches hooded in red cloth. Pippa [pippa] has a tripod; Noor [noor] has the star atlas; Georgie [georgie] is up past her bedtime and nobody says so. Somebody cranks the slit open and the sky comes in. @clock 10.

24.title: Turns at the brass refractor
24.gm: One at a time at the eyepiece of the brass refractor, the others waiting in the dark with cocoa from a flask: Saturn like a drawing of itself, the moon's edge, a cluster Noor names in a whisper. A quiet, lovely night. Whoever Rowan stands next to in the queue will remember this night WITH him: give that pair one unhurried exchange in low voices, hands round the same tin mug. Nothing is wrong tonight; do not hint that anything will be. @clock 10 an answer.

24.title: Star trails from the catwalk
24.gm: Out on the catwalk round the dome Pippa opens the shutter for a long exposure of star trails over the dark north ridge and asks everyone not to breathe on the tripod. At the far end of the rail Viktor [viktor] is not looking at the sky at all: he is watching the ridge, where a house stands with no lamps in it. Asked, he says he is 'resting his eyes'. Rowan may stand with either. @clock 10–15.

24.title: Midnight: the dome is closed; the walk down
24.gm: At midnight the slit is cranked shut and the key turned. The walk down the hill in a loose line under a sky that everybody now knows a little: Georgie asleep on her feet between Pippa and Noor, Viktor already gone by another path. Rowan walks down beside the person he stood with. @did stargazing over. @clock 20, and then bed.

25.title: Cas's birthday: everybody behind the news desk
25.gm: The studio in the dark, a dozen people crouched behind the news desk with a cake, shushing each other: Rafa [rafa] organised it, Bex lent the key. Rowan is among them if he knows Cas or was pulled in from the corridor. Footsteps; the door. @clock 5.

25.title: Lights on: Cas commentates his own surprise party
25.gm: Lights. Cas [cas] takes it in at a glance, clips his microphone on out of pure reflex and COMMENTATES: 'And they have gone with the classic hide-behind-the-desk formation — a bold choice, Abernathy visibly moved — is that a cake? It IS a cake —' He cannot stop. He does the candles, the singing, his own speech and a replay. It ends only when Rafa puts food in his mouth. One long answer in his broadcast voice. @clock 15.

25.title: Cake on the news desk
25.gm: Paper plates on the news desk. Without the microphone Cas is quieter than anyone expected and thanks people one at a time, by name, as if reading credits. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection. The party is over when the cake is; Bex wants her studio back by half past eight. @did Cas's birthday over. @clock 15.

26.title: Friday Night Draft: sign-up and seating
26.gm: The back tables of the Sleeve & Binder. Entry 60 cr at the counter (@credits -60 if Rowan plays), keep what you pick. Dex [dex] seats eight-player pods by drawing names from a dice bag; Mika [mika] judges with a sleepy smile and a mug. In Rowan's pod, if he enters: Nathan [nathan], Inya [inya], Tomi [tomi], Kenji [kenji] and three townspeople. If he does not, he can watch from the rail for nothing. @clock 10.

26.title: The draft: open, pick one, pass
26.gm: Three boosters each, opened one at a time: take a card, pass the rest. Rowan's online grind does not help here and his reads do. Nathan drafts badly and LOUDLY — announces what he took, asks what he should have taken, takes the shiny one — and is having the time of his life; Kenji drafts in total silence; Tomi prices every pack as it goes by. One or two answers; let the player make two real picks. Then twenty minutes of deckbuilding. @clock 20 an answer.

26.title: Three rounds in the pod
26.gm: Three short rounds inside the pod with the decks just built: @duel <id> casual | draft pod, round <n> for the one that matters, the others summarised. Nathan loses to Inya and to a fisherman, wins one by accident and celebrates it as a title. Mika rules on two questions without getting up. Winner of the pod gets two boosters from Dex. Ends at a quarter past nine: @did Friday draft over. @clock 20–25 a round.

26.title: The walk home along the harbour road
26.gm: The last cart has gone; they walk — the harbour road, lamps on the water, the avenue. Nathan talks the whole way: his picks, his brothers, the fisherman. Then, unprompted and at about half his usual volume, he tells Rowan that this is the best month he has ever had, and that Rowan is 'all right for a guy who never talks'. Make this good and ENTIRELY ordinary. No omen of any kind. Through the gate before ten; he goes to bed still talking. @clock 35.

26.title: Lights out in bungalow 7
26.gm: An ordinary Friday night, and it must read as one. Baylee [baylee] is asleep in a minute; Nathan [nathan] finishes a sentence he began on the avenue, then snores. The row is quiet, the sea is loud. FOR THE CLOCK: when Rowan lies down, close the answer with @clock up to 02:10 (FIXED TIMES shows how long; at most 240 at a time) or simply with @sleep — the game stops the clock at 02:10 by itself, so the night is not skipped. If he is awake or out, play that; the next point finds him wherever he is.

26.title: Small hours on the boardwalk
26.gm: 02:10 (canon; plot timeline t_bang). A concussion that lifts dust from the rafters; a green-white flash through the shutters; every window on the island rattles, every dog in Port Mulligan barks. The whole row is out on the boardwalk in blankets — Odalys [odalys] counting, Inya [inya] barefoot, Rana [rana] for once saying what everyone thinks. Over the north slope a glow, fading within a minute. The clock tower has stopped. Nobody knows anything; let them guess wrongly and vividly. Rowan can talk to anyone. @clock 5–10 an answer.

26.title: Half past two
26.gm: {H?{H=nathan?Nathan comes out of bungalow 7 banging a pan, Tomi's [tomi] good torch belted to his head, deck box in his jacket 'in case it wants a game'. He announces that it is a crashed spaceship, that he will be the first human to shake hands with it, and that everyone else is a coward — takes two of Mama's empanadas and goes up the jungle trail alone. Nobody stops him; people laugh. Rowan may go after him: Nathan outpaces him in the dark and is lost to him at the rope bridge. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is Nathan being Nathan.|{H=baylee?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail alone at half past two with Tomi's torch. Baylee had offered to go along and been told he would scare the aliens. He stands on the step for ten minutes. Then he fills a water bottle at the kitchen tap, says to whoever is nearest — Rowan, if he is awake — 'Somebody ought to walk behind him,' and follows, without a light, at the pace of a man walking a fence line. Nobody stops him; nobody thinks of it. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge and he is back by four, scratched and loud, having met no one: Baylee had taken the old cattle track to come out above him. Play it as comedy with one quiet figure in it. Do NOT telegraph anything.|{H=ed?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail at half past two with Tomi's torch.
