And this time the pan has woken Ed Venture. He comes out of bungalow 5 at a dead run, hat on, bootlaces flying, no torch — 'IS IT DANGEROUS?' — and is past Nathan before the trailhead. Nobody stops him; people cheer. Nathan cannot keep up, his torch dies at the rope bridge, and he is back by four swearing the cowboy cheated. Ed crossed the bridge without slowing down. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is Ed being Ed.|{H=tobias?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail at half past two with Tomi's torch. The whole row watches him go — which is exactly when Tobias Crowe goes out of the back window of bungalow 6 with a rucksack and no light. Only Dmitri [dmitri] sees it, and Dmitri says nothing; he never has. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge and he is back by four, loud and scratched, having met nobody. Tobias was already above him. Play the pan as comedy; the window is one line in a notebook. Do NOT telegraph anything.|{H=sammy?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail at half past two with Tomi's torch. Sammy Counts stands at the edge of the crowd in his long coat and writes one line in the numbered notebook. Then, fifty paces behind Nathan and without a light — because being seen to be afraid of the dark would be worse than the dark — he follows. Nobody notices; nobody ever does. When Nathan turns back at the rope bridge with a dead torch, Sammy steps off the path and lets him pass, and then cannot make himself be the second one who turned back. Nathan is home by four. Play the pan as comedy; the coat is a shape at the back of it. Do NOT telegraph anything.|{H=fiona?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail alone at half past two with Tomi's torch. Fiona Blackwood has been knitting on the porch of bungalow 4 through all of it. She puts the needles down, says in her real voice — light, northern, the one nobody is meant to hear — 'Well. Somebody ought to see it properly,' takes the storm lantern off the kitchen hook and walks up after his torch at her own slow pace. Nobody stops her; half of them think it is part of the act. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge; he passes her coming down, tells her the bridge is closed, and is home by four. She says 'Mm,' and goes on. Play the pan as comedy and the lantern as one small light going up the hill. Do NOT telegraph anything.|{H=freya?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail alone at half past two with Tomi's torch. Freya Nordlicht, three drinks in and delighted, announces to the boardwalk that the night has at last become worth staying up for, and goes up after his torch with the bottle in her hand, singing. People cheer her off. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge; he finds her sitting on it finishing the bottle, tells her the whole thing is closed, and is home by four. When the bottle was empty she went on, because the other way led to a quiet room. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is Freya being Freya.|{H=hedda?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail alone at half past two with Tomi's torch. Then Hedda Njord on the kitchen steps with the megaphone: the north slope is where the frigatebirds nest, there will be burnt chicks up there, and has ANYONE on this row thought of that? Nobody has. She goes up after his torch with the megaphone and her tin of bandages, still shouting statistics over her shoulder. People laugh. Nathan's torch dies at the rope bridge and he is home by four; she had left the trail below it to look for nests. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is Hedda being Hedda.|{H=sunny?Nathan and the pan, as always: spaceship, cowards, up the jungle trail alone at half past two with Tomi's torch. His torch dies at the rope bridge and he is home by four, loud and scratched. Nobody else from the row goes up, and the row goes back to bed. (The one who goes is not on the row tonight. At five Sunny Aldane comes down from Rare Hall for her run, hears from Dmitri [dmitri] on his porch that somebody went up the mountain alone in the dark, does not wait for the rest of the sentence, and runs: three hours' hike is seventy minutes at her pace. If Rowan is awake at five he sees her go by.) Play the pan as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything.|Nathan comes out of bungalow 7 banging a pan, Tomi's [tomi] good torch belted to his head, deck box in his jacket 'in case it wants a game'. He announces that it is a crashed spaceship, that he will be the first human to shake hands with it, and that everyone else is a coward — takes two of Mama's empanadas and goes up the jungle trail alone. Nobody stops him; people laugh. Rowan may go after him: Nathan outpaces him in the dark and is lost to him at the rope bridge. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is Nathan being Nathan.}}}}}}}}}|one of the row comes out of bungalow 7 banging a pan, Tomi's [tomi] good torch belted to his head, deck box in his jacket 'in case it wants a game'. He announces that it is a crashed spaceship, that he will be the first human to shake hands with it, and that everyone else is a coward — takes two of Mama's empanadas and goes up the jungle trail alone. Nobody stops him; people laugh. Rowan may go after him: one of the row outpaces him in the dark and is lost to him at the rope bridge. Play it as comedy. Do NOT telegraph anything: this is one of the row being one of the row.}

26.title: The row goes back to bed
26.gm: The glow is gone and it is cold. Odalys herds the row indoors; Viktor [viktor] stays on the end of the boardwalk looking north until she says his name twice. If Rowan followed {H}, he comes back down the trail alone about now with scratched shins. One bed in {H:bungalow} stays empty and {O} says he will be back for breakfast{H=nathan?, he always is|}. NOW Rowan may sleep (@sleep).

27.title: Saturday morning in bungalow 7
27.gm: Bright, washed, ordinary — and the clock tower still stands at 02:10. {H=@room?{H}'s bed has not been slept in|Word comes along the boardwalk before breakfast that {H}'s bed in {H:bungalow} has not been slept in}; {H:his} phone is under the pillow. {H=nathan?Baylee [baylee] has folded {H=nathan?{O}'s|Nathan's} blanket for him.|Nathan [nathan] is asleep face down with his boots on and a dead torch in his fist{H=baylee?.|; {O} [{O:id}] has folded {H}'s blanket for {H:him}.}} At breakfast the row tells last night to each other in six versions; Odalys [odalys] sets {H}'s place and says {H:he} will come back hungry. Nobody is worried yet{H=nathan? — he does things like this|}. Keep it light. @clock 10–20.

27.title: The tower clock starts again
27.gm: Wherever Rowan is: the bell. Silas [silas] has been up the tower; the clock jerks from 02:10 to the right time and strikes a quarter past eight, and he comes down without a word to anyone. Word goes round with the chimes that there is a HOLE on the far north slope — forty metres of black glass, three hours' hike — and that nothing is stopping anybody from going to look. Bex's crew is already loading a handcart. @clock 5.

27.title: Half the school sets off up the north slope
27.gm: From nine, parties leave by the jungle trail and the rope bridge: three hours up, three back (hike 3 — it costs most of the day). Viktor [viktor] went at first light, alone. If Rowan goes, he reaches the rim about noon: a 40-metre bowl of fused black glass, still warm to the hand, no wreck, nothing in it, and students standing round the edge being disappointed — and he is NOT in the Commons at midday, where {H} comes home; he meets him at supper. If he stays, the next point is his. @clock 60–90 an answer.

27.title: Midday at Mama's Kitchen
27.gm: {H} [{H:id}] strolls in along the boardwalk with glass dust in {H:his} hair, to a hero's welcome. {H=nathan?It grins {H}'s grin, says 'Told you. Cowards,' at about half the usual volume, says it found 'a big hole, nothing in it', and eats — six plates, for an hour, neatly. It does not insult anyone.|It wears {H}'s face exactly, {H:ret}.{H=@row? It goes to bungalow 7 afterwards, not to its own, and sits down on the floor between the beds to wait for Rowan.|{H=@near? Afterwards it comes down the boardwalk and sits on the steps of bungalow 7, to wait for Rowan.|}}} From this moment play the replacement EXACTLY as CORE 4.3 describes: nearly perfect, slightly literal, kind. Nobody notices anything; Odalys is only pleased he is eating. Do not explain, underline or hint. @clock 10 an answer.

27.title: The Top Deck: special broadcast goes live
27.gm: Unscheduled, the ON AIR lamp at half past twelve on a Saturday. Bex [bex] is first with it and knows it: eyewitness calls from all three dorms (the flash, the windows, a dog that will not come out from under a bed), a map with a circle on it. If Rowan was on the boardwalk last night he is a witness she WANTS on air — a runner finds him, or she waves him in from the corridor: sixty seconds, live. One long answer in her voice. @clock 20.

27.title: On air: a photograph from the observatory
27.gm: Pippa [pippa] brings in the star-trail plate she exposed over the north ridge and it goes up on the screen: the curved trails — and one green streak straight across them. Bex says the word 'crater' on air, as a rumour, and asks who is going up to look; by evening she will have footage. Pippa keeps looking at the plate after the camera has left it. @clock 10.

27.title: Sign-off; a visit from the staff room
27.gm: Bex signs off with a promise of more at seven. In the doorway stands Vivienne [vivienne], who has come down from the staff room with the line that will be official by evening: 'a meteorological event; nothing to worry about.' She says it pleasantly and twice. Bex writes it down in a way that shows what she thinks of it. @did special broadcast over. @clock 5.

28.title: Pippa's party: the paper-crown photo booth
28.gm: Marit [marit] has thrown it and directs it: a bedsheet backdrop, a box of paper crowns, Pippa's own camera on a tripod with a cable release, so that for once the photographer is IN the pictures. Everyone who comes in is crowned and shot, singly and in heaps. Pippa [pippa] laughs in the right places and is, to anyone who knows her, somewhere else. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection. @clock 10.

28.title: Presents; Georgie's card
28.gm: Presents on the sofa. Georgie [georgie] has made a card by hand — a dragon, coloured in, a great deal of glitter — and stands rigid with worry that it is babyish. Pippa looks at it properly, for the first time today entirely present, and pins it to the board over the mantel before opening anything else. If Rowan brought something, now. @clock 10.

28.title: Cake and photographs
28.gm: Cake; the crown pictures will be printed by Tuesday. Pippa is distracted again and, asked by someone she trusts, says why: she spent the morning in the darkroom with the plate from the observatory, enlarging the green streak. Things that fall get faster. This one slows down before it lands. She says it lightly and changes the subject to cake. Leave it there. @did Pippa's birthday over. @clock 15.

29.title: A Chancellor's notice goes up on the board
29.gm: Pinned over everything else, on headed paper: all trails beyond the rope bridge closed until further notice — unstable ground — field sections suspended; an all-school assembly in the Great Arena at 14:15, attendance expected. A crowd reads it on the way to first period. Those who hiked up on Saturday or Sunday are suddenly the only ones who have seen it. '{H}' reads the notice twice, with interest, and asks what 'until further notice' is measured in. @clock 5.

29.title: Tape and a rota at the north trailhead
29.gm: At the campus-side anchor of the rope bridge: staff tape, a trestle table, a rota. Silas [silas] has brought a chain and a padlock for the nights. Coach Rox [rox] takes the first watch with a flask. Prof. Ashdown [ashdown] argued against the closure this morning and lost; she is here anyway, tight-lipped, counting her field tools back across the bridge. From now on the crater takes a Night slot, the coast, the tubes or Viktor — and being caught inside the cordon is a formal warning. Rowan sees this only if he walks out here; on a class day that is a skipped lesson. @clock 10.

29.title: The assembly bell: the school files into the arena
29.gm: The tower bell, then the whole school crossing the Quad at once. In the arena the proctors seat people by dorm and year; Tavita counts rows. Staff on the stage in a line of chairs. The Commons first-years sit together; '{H}' takes the seat next to Rowan and looks about {H:him} with open, friendly attention. A hum of rumour, then the Chancellor stands and it stops. @clock 10.

29.title: The Chancellor's address
29.gm: Chancellor Vicar [okonkwo], calm and exact, without notes: on Friday night a meteorite struck the uninhabited north slope. Nobody was hurt. There is no danger. The site is closed for everyone's safety while the ground is surveyed; lessons, the Ladder and the term continue as planned. Rowan only listens: play the WHOLE address in ONE long answer with real speech. Midway '{H}' [{H:id}] leans over and asks {H:him}, interested, why everyone is sitting in rows facing one person. Students nearby laugh. It is a good question. @clock 15.

29.title: Dr Blum on meteorites
29.gm: The Chancellor asks Dr Blum [blum] to say something reassuring about meteorites. He stands, finds his glasses in his hair, and cheerfully gives the odds of one striking this island in any given century — which are terrible, which is to say it should not have happened, which he seems to notice only as he says it. Santángel [santangel] studies his shoes. The Chancellor thanks him quickly. One answer. @clock 5.

29.title: Questions from the floor; dismissal by dorm
29.gm: Three questions are taken. Bex's [bex] — whether students may see the survey — is answered with a courteous no before she has finished it. Dismissal by dorm, Tower first. On the steps outside, the school decides in a hundred conversations that it was a meteorite and rather exciting. @did assembly over. The rest of the afternoon is free; the council sits at half past three as every Monday. @clock 10.

29.title: Dusk: the chain goes on
29.gm: At dusk the day watch packs up the trestle and Silas hangs the chain across the bridge head and snaps the padlock. He stands a moment looking over the ravine, then limps down with the lantern. Tape by day, a chain by night: that is the cordon (canon, Day 29). Anyone watching from the trees learns when the watch changes. @clock 5.

30.title: Movie Night: a flying-saucer double bill
30.gm: By popular demand, four days after the bang: the school is still treating it as a joke. Marit [marit] has cut paper saucers and hung them from the lamp; Bex [bex] threads the projector. The Commons come as a block — Inya [inya], {H=baylee?{O} [{O:id}]|Baylee [baylee]}, and '{H}' [{H:id}], who has brought {H:his} own cushion and sets it down with care. He will sit wherever Rowan sits unless Rowan arranges otherwise; who is on Rowan's OTHER side is his to choose. @clock 5–10.

30.title: First feature: the invasion film
30.gm: Saucers on wires, a town hall, a scientist nobody listens to. The room heckles happily. '{H}' watches the invasion with complete attention and laughs at every joke exactly half a second after everyone else. ONE answer for the film: the dark, the heckling, that half-second, and whatever passes between Rowan and the person on his other side. {H=baylee?Nathan, who talks through every film, has not said a word since the titles.|Baylee watches {H} more than the screen and says nothing.} @clock 70.

30.title: Second feature
30.gm: Reel change, popcorn, half the room leaves and the rest spread out on the cushions. The second film is shorter and worse and nobody minds. A quieter hour: the scene in the dark belongs to Rowan and whoever stayed beside him. '{H}' does not fidget, does not comment and does not look away from the screen once. ONE answer, ending on the lights. @clock 55.

30.title: Lights up; the walk back to the cove
30.gm: Cushions back, paper saucers taken as souvenirs. On the path down to the cove '{H}' says quietly, as a considered opinion, that the visitors in the film were 'very rude: they did not ask what the rules were'. {H=nathan?Inya laughs, because it is a {H} thing to say. It is almost a {H} thing to say.|Inya laughs, because it is the kind of thing {H} says. It is almost the kind of thing {H} says.} Do not underline it. @did movie night over. @clock 15.

31.title: Last ranked games before the snapshot
31.gm: Half an hour to the Evening bell and the Terraces are frantic: everyone within reach of a better number is hunting a last ranked game, and everyone sitting on a good one has become hard to find. Zeynep [zeynep] stamps slips without looking up. If Rowan wants one more result on the board, it has to be asked for NOW (@duel <id> ladder | rank) and finished before the bell; a game still running at six does not count. @clock 5 an answer.

31.title: The Evening bell: the board freezes
31.gm: On the first stroke the split-flap board on the Quad clatters once through every row and stops dead. A crowd reads it in silence, then all at once. Lilia [lilia] at one, the gap under her wider. Rowan's own number is whatever he has made it. And somebody says aloud what several have just seen: {H:sig} has climbed FORTY places in four days. '{H}' is not there to be congratulated. @journal School. @clock 5.

31.title: Prof. Santángel reads the tryout seeds
31.gm: Santángel [santangel] from the steps, Coach Rox [rox] beside him with her arms folded: the top eight players NOT on the Battle Team are read out and seeded into Friday's tryouts for the one reserve slot; everyone else may enter the open bracket — sheet at the arena door until Thursday evening. Dom [dom], Kenji [kenji] and Priya [priya] stand at the back looking at the eight the way one looks at a menu. If Rowan is among them, his name is read like any other. One answer. @clock 10.

31.title: The open-bracket sheet at the arena door
31.gm: A sheet of paper and a pencil on a string. First-years dare each other: Gideon signs without breaking stride, Magnus after consulting his tablet, Mikoto because someone laughed. Rowan can sign (Friday, 14:00, tournament-kind and hard: @journal Plans) or not; Rox, passing, says in one sentence what she would need to see from him. @did snapshot read. @clock 5–10.

32.title: Paper dragons: helping Pippa set up
32.gm: Pippa [pippa] has planned this for weeks and is up a ladder with a mouthful of drawing pins: paper dragons on strings, a cake with a plastic egg on it, party hats. It is the first birthday party Georgie has ever had with people near her own age. Helping set up counts for a great deal with both of them. Willas [willas] arrives early, is handed a party hat, puts it on and dares anyone to comment. @clock 10–15.

32.title: Georgie's birthday party
32.gm: Georgie [georgie] is led in with her eyes shut. Keep it bright and childlike: the dragons, the egg, a game of pass-the-parcel that three upper-years take far too seriously, Willas guarding the cake. For once she looks exactly her age — speechless, pink, holding Pippa's sleeve. A small present or simply turning up is worth real affection. One long answer of party. @clock 30.

32.title: A serious game as a present
32.gm: What she would really like, and would never ask for: a serious game, played properly, by someone who does not go easy on her. If Rowan offers it as his present: @duel georgie casual | a birthday game, played to win. She says yes very quietly and wins or loses with her whole attention; either way it is the best present on the table. Otherwise Willas plays her, loses, and is gracious about it at the top of his voice. @clock 25.

32.title: Half past bedtime; tryouts are tomorrow
32.gm: Pippa calls time: the guest of honour is asleep on her feet. Clearing up, someone says the Battle Team tryouts are tomorrow — and it turns out Georgie believes they are not for her: too young, a first-year, nobody said. SOMEONE should tell her she is allowed to enter (if Rowan or anyone does, plainly and kindly, she thinks about it all night). @did Georgie's party over. @clock 10.

33.title: Tryouts: sign-in, seeds, kit
33.gm: The arena floor cleared, cones out, four duel tables at the far end. Coach Rox [rox] with a stopwatch round her neck: one slot, second reserve, and she is not looking for the best deck. The eight seeds and the open bracket sign in — among the first-years Gideon [gideon], Magnus, Eberhart, {H=fiona?{O}|Fiona}, Ashton, Noor, Mikoto, and '{H}' [{H:id}]. The team stands along the wall: Lilia [lilia], Willas [willas], Dom [dom], Saoirse [saoirse], Kenji [kenji], Priya [priya]. Rowan enters if he signed or signs now. @clock 10.

33.title: Circuits on the arena floor
33.gm: Rox runs it like a fitness test: shuttle runs, planks, stairs of the stands, no pause. Priya drills the first-years' group and is the fairest assessor there — she counts honestly and says so when someone has more in them. Mikoto cannot stop laughing through the planks; Willas loses his temper and shouts at him, and five minutes later hands him his own water bottle. '{H}' does every set and is not out of breath. If Rowan is in it: @check fitness 8 | Rox's circuits. One or two answers. @clock 35.

33.title: First table: duels while exhausted
33.gm: Straight off the floor to the tables, pulse still up: each candidate plays a team member, who uses a practice deck. Hands shake; that is the test. Rowan's game, if he is in: @duel <dom|kenji|priya> tournament | tryout, first table (hard). Half the field is thanked and sent to the stands after this round. '{H}' beats Kenji's practice deck flawlessly, without one wasted action, and says 'Thank you for the game' in the right place. @clock to 15:50.

33.title: Second table
33.gm: Eight left. Another circuit — shorter, nastier — then the second table. '{H}' beats Dom's practice deck the same way; Dom resets his pieces very precisely afterwards. Lilia, who has watched the afternoon from the wall with her usual seventy per cent of attention, comes off the wall and watches every game he plays with the first real interest she has shown all year. If Rowan is still in: @duel <id> tournament | tryout, second table. Otherwise ONE long answer from the stands. @clock to 16:40.

33.title: The final table
33.gm: Four candidates, one table, Lilia's own deck on the other side for whoever Rox points at. Surviving to this table is ENOUGH to be noticed by her, whatever happens on it. If Rowan is here: @duel lilia tournament | tryout, final table — he is not expected to win; how he loses is what she looks at. Gideon plays his best game of the term. Georgie, if she was encouraged to enter, plays without looking up and the hall goes quiet. @clock to 17:25.

33.title: Rox thanks the field
33.gm: Rox lines them up. No name today: the result goes up tomorrow at nine, here. She gives three people one sentence each. To '{H}', who has not lost a game: no — 'You don't look tired. I don't trust it.' He thanks her correctly and asks what tired should look like. Lilia is already gone. The team stacks cones. @did tryouts over. @clock 10.

34.title: The team lines up on the arena floor
34.gm: Saturday, nine o'clock, a thin crowd in the lower stands: yesterday's candidates, their friends, Pippa [pippa] with a camera. The Battle Team lines up in jackets — Priya [priya] at the end of the line, first reserve for a second year. Coach Rox [rox] walks out with a small box in her fist. Nobody talks. @clock 10.

34.title: Coach Delgado names the reserve
34.gm: One name. By default: Gideon Pryce [gideon], who steps forward and thanks the coach in a short, prepared, perfect speech. If Georgie tried out and won it: Georgie [georgie], who hides behind Pippa. If Rowan earned it: Rox pins the Battle Team pin on him, crooked, and gives him ONE sentence of real feedback about his hands. Priya applauds correctly — exactly as long as is right — and goes to hit the bag. One answer. @clock 10.

34.title: Afterwards, in the tunnel
34.gm: The stands empty through the tunnel. Dom [dom] says there — not quietly, to nobody in particular — that the wrong starter is being protected on this team. Willas [willas] hears it, stops, and does not turn round; someone moves him along. Whoever is walking behind them hears it too. The new reserve reports for conditioning on Monday before dawn. The pre-release in town starts at half past eleven; carts from the gate. @did reserve named. @clock 10.

34.title: Pre-release 'Tidebreak': registration
34.gm: The Sleeve & Binder is full to the door: the new set, a week early. Entry 90 cr at the counter (@credits -90 if Rowan plays), seats by number. Dex [dex] stacks sealed product like a man laying bricks; Mika [mika] head-judges in a paper crown someone made her. From the Academy: Inya [inya], Kenji [kenji], Tomi [tomi] with an empty binder, and Livvie [livvie], who has paid her entry in small coins. Prices will move all weekend — Tomi and Mika are both worth listening to. @clock 10.

34.title: Sealed pools opened; deckbuilding
34.gm: Everybody opens the same number of boosters and builds from that and nothing else. A format in which Rowan's online grind does not help and his READS do: nobody knows these cards yet. One answer for the opening (let the player see what kind of pool he has — @pack for each booster if the game hands them out), one for a real building decision. Livvie sorts hers by resale value before she looks at what they do. @clock 20 an answer.

34.title: Three rounds of sealed
34.gm: Three rounds, forty-five minutes each. Play ONE out (@duel <id> tournament | Tidebreak pre-release, round <n>) and summarise the others. Inya loses to a card she has never seen and demands to read it; Kenji wins all three and is not satisfied; a fisherman's daughter of twelve beats Tomi and he pays up on a side bet he should not have made. Mika rules on new cards from the release notes, yawning. @clock 40 a round.

34.title: Prize boosters; the trade counter
34.gm: Prizes by record: boosters from Dex's hand. Then the trade counter, which is the real event — the set's first prices are being made in this room. Livvie sells EVERY card she opened, prize boosters included, before she leaves the shop, and walks out with notes folded small. If Rowan opened something good, Tomi and Dex both make an offer and they are not the same. Second flight tomorrow, same times. @did pre-release Saturday over. @clock 10–20.

35.title: Pre-release, second flight: registration
35.gm: Sunday's flight: fewer people, better prepared. Entry again 90 cr (@credits -90). Yesterday's players know which commons are good; the prices on Dex's slate have already been rubbed out and rewritten twice. Livvie [livvie] is here again for the prize boosters and has brought a sandwich this time, because Odalys put it in her bag. Mika [mika] has kept the paper crown. @clock 10.

35.title: Second flight: build, then three rounds
35.gm: As yesterday: forty-five minutes to open and build, then three rounds. If Rowan plays both days, play out a DIFFERENT moment from yesterday — a pool that has to be built round one strange card, an opponent from the town league. @duel <id> tournament | Tidebreak, second flight for one round, the rest summarised. If he only comes to trade or watch, one answer at the rail. @clock 40 an answer.

35.title: Prizes; the weekend's prices settle
35.gm: Last prizes of the weekend. Dex chalks the settled prices on the slate and that is what the new set costs until the next ferry. Livvie sells out a second time and for the first time this term buys something for herself — sleeves. Tomi counts what the weekend made him. The carts go back up the avenue; Sunday evening on campus is quiet. @did pre-release weekend over. @clock 10–15.

35.title: Engraved invitations at the Tower door
35.gm: The Spectral lobby in candlelight. Thandi [thandi], the junior warden, has the guest list and reads names off engraved cards. Grey collars are not on it — unless Jessica [jessica] or Georgie [georgie] brings one as her guest, and either will if Rowan has given her reason to (then he is signed in under her name, and she is answerable for him). Without that he gets no further than the lobby and hears the terrace from below. @clock 5–10.

35.title: Ashton's party on the Tower terrace
35.gm: The terrace pool lit from below, a string trio from Port Mulligan, a table of things on sticks. Ashton [ashton] throws his own party and is — annoyingly — a generous host: he knows every guest's drink, introduces people to each other with one true compliment each, and gives Rowan (if he got in) exactly the same welcome as a white collar. Three of his ex-girlfriends stand at the balustrade comparing notes and reach a verdict. One free scene; @clock 5–10 an answer.

35.title: The toast
35.gm: Ashton taps a glass and toasts not himself but his guests, by name, round the terrace, a rose for every woman — including the three at the balustrade, who accept theirs with identical expressions. A small present or simply having come counts with him more than he lets on: for a moment he is only a boy who is pleased that people came. Guests leave from nine. @did Ashton's party over. @clock 15.

36.title: Freya's birthday: the fire is lit and the island turns up
36.gm: {H=freya?Her party at the fire, the one the row has been promised for a week, and it is exactly as loud as her last one. Somebody hands her a whole bottle of aquavit as a dare, as somebody always does. She drinks it the way you drink water after a run — all of it, in one, without her eyes watering — and hands it back empty. Then she sits and waits, politely, hands on her knees. After a minute she asks: 'When does it begin?' People laugh. Hedda leans in to smell her breath, laughing, and stops. Do not explain; let the player's skin crawl on its own. @clock 20.|Her birthday is an event the whole island attends, invited or not: all three dorms on the sand, upper-years, two people from town. Freya [freya] receives them at the fire in a crown Trixie wove and has an exact word for each. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection; she will know tomorrow who did. '{H}' [{H:id}] stands where the crowd is thickest, smiling at it. @clock 5–10.}

36.title: Aquavit, and the first toasts
36.gm: {H=freya?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Freya' [freya] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|A bottle with a label nobody can read goes round with thimble glasses, and Freya toasts in ascending order of grandeur. Then someone hands '{H}' a whole bottle as a dare, the way one would have dared the old {H} (plot file c_m1_aquavit — follow that entry for what {H:he} does with it and what can be seen). Rowan can drink or not; nobody presses twice. One or two answers. @clock 10 an answer.}

36.title: The song in a language nobody knows
36.gm: {H=freya?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Freya' [freya] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|Freya stands on a log and teaches the island a song from home: verses nobody can follow, a chorus anyone can. A free hour round the fire while it catches on — the place for ONE real conversation with whoever Rowan came for, or with Freya herself in a gap between verses, when she is funnier and quieter than her legend. It is Monday; the careful ones leave about half past nine. @clock 5 an answer.}

36.title: Towards midnight: everybody knows the chorus
36.gm: {H=freya?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Freya' [freya] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|By midnight the whole beach has the chorus by heart and sings it at the sea. Freya conducts with both arms and is carried once round the fire. She will remember ALL of it tomorrow, which nobody else can say. Odalys lets it run until the stroke of twelve and then stands on the boardwalk with the spoon, and that is the end. @did Freya's birthday over. @clock 30.}

37.title: Auditions: sign the sheet, take a page
37.gm: The Little Theatre, work lights on. Marit [marit] directs with a megaphone she does not need; Pippa [pippa] hands out pages; Felix [felix] is already painting a wave. This year's pageant for the Night of Masks: 'The Founder's Shipwreck'. Parts: the Deckhand, the Storm, the Parrot, a chorus of Heroes. No experience needed. Really. Taking any part is a Nerve track with an audience at the end (Day 54). Rowan signs for a reading or sits in the stalls. @clock 5–10.

37.title: Readings: the Deckhand, the Storm, the Parrot
37.gm: One by one on the bare stage. Three or four auditions in ONE long answer, each a few lines: someone who is secretly good, someone who is the Storm with their whole body, a Parrot that stops the room. Chuck Kaboom [chuck] has drifted in at the back and enjoys the Parrot enormously. Vivienne [vivienne] watches two readings from the door and writes one name down. If Rowan reads: stop before his turn and let the player do it (@check nerve 8 | read for a part in front of the theatre club). @clock 30 an answer.

37.title: The chorus of Heroes; blocking the cave scene
37.gm: Everyone who read is put in the chorus on the spot and Marit blocks the big scene: the shipwrecked Founder finds the cave. Chalk marks, a ladder for the cave mouth, people walked from A to B by the shoulders. Chuck, who was laughing a minute ago, watches them build the cave for about a minute, gets up without a word and leaves by the side door. Marit takes it as a note on her blocking. @clock 20.

37.title: Marit reads the cast list
37.gm: Marit reads the cast from the edge of the stage as though announcing a coronation. If Rowan read, he gets a part that fits what he did (@journal Plans: rehearsals Thursday afternoons, performance on the Night of Masks, Day 54); if not, the chorus still has room and she says so, at him. Work lights off at nine. @did pageant auditions over. @clock 10.

38.title: Outdoor Club: helmets and roll call at the main gate
38.gm: A dozen students at the lodge in boots. The club's leader (unnamed, a patient fourth-year) hands out helmets and lamps, checks every permission slip — the slip excuses today's two classes — and gives the safety talk again for {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} [ed], who signs the book with a flourish. Viktor [viktor] is on the list and has, for once, brought exactly the right kit. It is a FULL day: back about half past four, so whoever comes cannot also work the orchard harvest. @clock 10.

38.title: Up the old tramway to the east shoulder
38.gm: Two hours along the rusted tramway cutting that climbs the volcano's east shoulder — outside the closed area, as the leader says twice at the fork where tape crosses the other path. Sleepers, ferns, a tipped ore wagon. One moment per answer among the walkers; Viktor walks at the back and counts paces under his breath. At the top: a hole in the ground the size of a room, a cold breath coming out of it, and a knotted rope. @place lava_tubes. @clock 50–60 an answer.

38.title: Down the knotted rope into the first chamber
38.gm: One at a time down the skylight on a knotted rope with a safety line (@check nerve 8 | down the rope into the dark, if Rowan goes). Below: the first chamber — black rock that glitters back at every lamp like frost, a floor of rippled stone, tunnels leading off that the trip does NOT enter. {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} leans over every edge there is (if today's timeline lists an entry about {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed}, it happens here). The leader counts helmets. @clock 20 an answer.

38.title: Torches off: real dark
38.gm: The leader has everyone sit, and on a count of three all lamps go out. Real dark, the kind with no shapes in it; someone giggles, then nobody does. A full minute. From one of the passages comes a faint warm draught and, under the silence, a clicking — slow, irregular. Lamps on. 'The mountain settling,' says the leader, a little too quickly. One answer; let the player sit in it. @clock 10.

38.title: Lunch in the chamber; a head count
38.gm: Sandwiches on the rippled floor. At the count there is one helmet too few: Viktor. He slipped into a side passage and is gone forty minutes; the leader is frightened and angry and will not let anyone look. He walks back in as the search is being organised, chalk dust on his hands, with a lie about a dropped lamp. Whoever watched which passage he came out of — and saw that it was not the one he went into — knows more than the leader. (He was already down here alone two nights ago.) @clock 15 an answer.

38.title: Up the rope; home by the tramway
38.gm: Up the rope, slower than down, and the long walk home in the heat; the leader keeps Viktor directly in front of her the whole way. Easy, tired talk; {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} has a new favourite place. At the lodge about half past four helmets are counted in and slips handed back. The harvest is nearly over — there is only the cider left. @did lava tube trip over. @clock 60–90 an answer.

38.title: Harvest: ladders, crates and rows are given out
38.gm: Twenty minutes east on the plantation road, after the Midday class. Odalys [odalys] runs it from the back of the kitchen cart; Silas [silas] hands out ladders and picking poles and says which trees are not to be climbed. Paid by the crate — about 20 cr for the afternoon, more for the strong. Rowan is given a row and a partner: {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee], Livvie [livvie], Inya [inya] or Tomi [tomi], by where he happens to stand. @clock 10.

38.title: Picking: mango and guava
38.gm: The gentlest afternoon of the term. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} is in his element — reaches what others need a ladder for, shows how to twist rather than pull — and, for once, TALKS: about soil, about what this ground wants, about home. If the technique he teaches has its source condition met, this is where. Tomi keeps the tally; Inya eats one in four. Silas's goats graze between the trees and will not go into the northern rows; he does not make them. One or two answers. @clock 40–50 an answer.

38.title: Water break in the shade
38.gm: Odalys bangs a ladle on the cart: water, everyone, now. Livvie has not stopped once — she is paid by the crate — and on the way to the cart she goes grey and sits down very suddenly. Odalys has her in the shade with her head down before anyone else has moved, says one quiet, exact sentence to her, and puts a guava in her hand. Livvie is back on her feet in ten minutes and furious about the lost crate. @clock 15.

38.title: The last rows; crates counted
38.gm: The last rows in long light. Then the count at the cart: Tomi reads the tally, Odalys pays out in notes from an apron pocket (@credits +20 | orchard harvest — more if Rowan really worked, and she quietly rounds Livvie's lost crate up). The cart is loaded for the kitchens. @did harvest done. @clock 30 an answer.

38.title: Cider under the trees
38.gm: Silas has a barrel of last year's in the shade and taps it without ceremony. Tin mugs, bare feet, the sun going down through the leaves; those who went down the lava tubes straggle in dusty in time for this. Somebody asks Silas why the goats will not go north, and he says goats are particular. Home on the cart or on foot behind it. @clock 20.

39.title: The Top Deck: a birthday edition, live
39.gm: A special Thursday show: Bex [bex] celebrates live on air. Streamers on the cameras, the crew in paper hats, the audience chairs full. It is a loud, happy show — callers sing, the ladder segment is conducted entirely in birthday metaphors, Marit delivers a tribute nobody asked for. Rowan only watches (audience, crew if he has a shift, or a common-room screen): ONE long answer in the show's voice. @clock 35.

39.title: A cake that says BREAKING
39.gm: Last segment: the crew wheel in a cake iced like a news banner — BREAKING — and Bex has to cut it on camera with a cable knife. She signs off with her mouth full: 'Back Friday. Nothing ever happens here, but if it does, you'll hear it from me first.' The lamp goes out. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection. @clock 10.

39.title: Off air
39.gm: Cake on the mixing desk, which is forbidden. Off air Bex is tired, pleased and already planning Friday's rundown on the back of a paper plate. A good half hour to be one of the people winding cable with her. Let it be simply a nice evening at the studio. @did Bex's birthday show over. @clock 10–20.

40.title: The tower bell, out of turn
40.gm: Canon (plot timeline t_h1). Wherever Rowan is: the clock-tower bell — not the hour but a slow single toll that does not stop, which no first-year has heard before. Upper-years know it: the emergency toll. Windows open along the row; Odalys [odalys] stands on the kitchen porch with a dishcloth in her hand, not moving. Nobody knows anything yet. (At dawn Silas found Brant Kessler in Trial Dome 3; that is not known to anyone on the row.) One answer. @clock 5.

40.title: Trial Dome 3
40.gm: For a player who goes there before it is taped at about half past eight: Silas [silas] at the door, grey in the face; Ms Kirishima [hana] and Nurse Camille [camille] inside; Bex [bex] already there with a camera, being moved back. Brant [brant] is upright in the chair, eyes open, chain on, breathing, nobody home. The score clock stopped at 02:10; a ring of melting frost on the dais; the cards he extorted stacked neatly on the far side, sorted by owner; ONE after-hours entry in tidy handwriting on the booking sheet. A glimpse only — then the Chancellor [okonkwo] arrives and the corridor is cleared. @clock 5–10.

40.title: An ambulance cart crosses the Quad
40.gm: During first period, seen from classroom windows: the infirmary's cart crossing the Quad at a walk, a blanketed shape sitting upright on it, Camille beside it with one hand on its shoulder. Every lecturer on campus stops for a moment and then goes on. Dome 3 is taped shut 'for recalibration'. Camille opens Ward B. If Rowan is in class he sees it from his seat; the lesson continues. One answer. @clock 5.

40.title: Lunch
40.gm: Wherever Rowan eats: by lunch the word is 'seizure', and everybody has it from somebody reliable. The ante column of the Dome 3 booking sheet has been blacked out; Bex has been told, by name, what she may not broadcast, and sits with her camera in her lap. Brant's two hangers-on eat alone. '{H}' [{H:id}], if Rowan eats where {H:he} does, says mildly: 'Nothing is his now. That was the agreement.' Nobody hears it as anything but {H} being {H}. Do not underline it. @clock 10 an answer.

41.title: Regatta: boats out, crews wanted
41.gm: Bunting along the quay. The town carries on, pointedly: nobody here mentions the Academy's bad week first. Dinghies are rigged on the slip; fried squid in paper cones; Josie [josie] has a trestle bar outside The Mulligan. Saoirse [saoirse] is varnishing something that is already a boat mostly by courtesy and needs a crew of ONE — Rowan will do, if he can take orders. Captain Stroud [abel] sounds the Second Chance's horn for the start before he sails at noon. The field section planned for today does not happen. @clock 10.

41.title: Rowing heats across the harbour
41.gm: Four-oared gigs across the harbour and back, town against town, then town against Academy: {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] strokes a scratch student crew that loses by a length and demands a rematch. Silas [silas] holds the finish flag at the mole and gives every verdict in one word. On the quay, fishermen say between heats that the north side has gone dead — no gulls, nothing on the lines. Dex [dex] tells whoever asks that he threw Brant's two hangers-on out of his shop this morning for trying to sell 'his collection'. One or two answers. @clock 20 an answer.

41.title: The dinghy class
41.gm: Three laps round the buoys. If Rowan crews for Saoirse: she gives orders in single words and expects them done before she has finished (@check fitness 8 | crew Saoirse's dinghy and do exactly as told); the boat leaks, she sails it like a blade, and on the last leg she lets the sheet out and laughs aloud. She wins the class — narrowly with a bad crew, by a street with a good one, alone if he said no. Tell the race ONCE in one long answer. @clock 40.

41.title: Prizes on the quay
41.gm: The harbourmaster gives out pennants from a fish crate; Saoirse's goes on the boathouse door. Fried squid for the crews, on Josie. If Rowan sailed, Saoirse says in one sentence what he is like in a boat, which with her is a character reference. The bunting stays up; the town drifts to The Mulligan. @did regatta over. The afternoon in town is free. @clock 15.

42.title: Fiona's birthday: candles on the steps of Bungalow 4
42.gm: {H=fiona?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Fiona' [fiona] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|Black candles in jam jars down the steps of bungalow 4, a cake with black icing, Fiona [fiona] in her best lace receiving visitors in the crypt voice and plainly enjoying herself. Maisie [maisie] runs a cable out of the window. The row comes by in ones and twos. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection. @clock 5–10.}

42.title: Presents
42.gm: {H=fiona?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Fiona' [fiona] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|An embarrassment of presents from boys. {H=sammy?'Sammy's'|Sammy's} [sammy] is a book of ghost stories he has clearly read first. {H=tobias?'Tobias's'|Tobias's} [tobias] is a bunch of flowers that were growing on the Spectral terrace this morning. And there is an unsigned box, expensive, in tissue paper, that can only have come from the Tower; she reads the blank card twice. Each giver watches the others. Fiona thanks all three in exactly the same voice. One answer. @clock 15.}

42.title: Maisie's present
42.gm: {H=fiona?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Fiona' [fiona] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|Maisie's present is a black light she wired herself. Plugged in, it turns the lace violet, the icing luminous and everybody's teeth alarming; the porch shrieks. It is the one Fiona keeps ON. Cake by black light, eaten once; the party is over when the jars burn down. @did Fiona's birthday over. @clock 15.}

42.title: After midnight on the porch
42.gm: {H=fiona?The row has made her a cake with black icing and a small marzipan coffin, as a joke she would have loved, and she does everything right: the tilt of the head, the low 'How very thoughtful. I shall be buried with it,' the pause. The table waits for the laugh — the real one, an octave up, that always gets out on her birthday. It does not come. She thanks everyone, by name, correctly. Asked for a speech, she says what her mother says over the dead, word for word, kindly. Somebody laughs, late. Do not explain; let the player's skin crawl on its own. @clock 20.|After midnight the row is dark but for one violet window. Fiona has taken her knitting out to the porch of bungalow 4 and sits under the black light without the voice, counting stitches. Two doors up, on the porch of bungalow 6, Dmitri [dmitri] is awake in his blanket, as he is every night. Neither has said anything yet. Whoever is still up can sit with either. @clock 10.}

43.title: Squad training at the pool
43.gm: The swim squad's Monday set, Baraka [baraka] on the pool deck with the watch. 'Sunny' [sunny] swims her four hundred. Every length is the same, to the hundredth, and the total is the time she swam at seventeen, before the shoulder — the one that was going to take her to the Games; half the squad knows that number by heart. She climbs out breathing as she went in, does not ask what it was, and stands at arm's length while they cheer. Baraka shows Rowan the watch as if it were broken. If asked, she says, easily: 'It does not hurt any more. Nothing does.' Do NOT explain. @clock 15.

43.title: Library, extended hours — Monday: the review tables are set out
43.gm: Study week: the Library stays open until midnight. Probability table: Noor [noor] and Teobalt [teobalt] with a stack of past papers, Georgie [georgie] solving them faster than they are handed out. Quiet floors upstairs for those who work alone. The school is subdued this week; people come in groups. Rowan chooses a table, a floor and — which matters more — WHO he studies beside. @clock 5–10.

43.title: Evening session at the review tables
43.gm: Real work in whispers; steady work beats cramming, and each session this week counts normally. Dr Blum [blum] wanders through about eight, answers three questions with a fourth, and leaves his chalk behind. Play ONE exchange at Rowan's table — a problem cracked together, a wrong answer, a biscuit passed under the desk — then close: end that answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it uses up the evening and brings the clock to ten). If he would sooner talk than work, it is an ordinary scene and nothing is counted.

43.title: Midnight: the Library closes
43.gm: For those who stayed on after ten: at twenty to twelve the head librarian walks the floors turning lamps down. Books are stacked on the returns trolley, somebody is woken. And then the thing this week has that others did not: nobody walks home alone. Groups form at the door by dorm without anyone saying why, and the Commons go down to the cove together with one torch. Rowan walks with whoever he worked beside. @clock 20.

44.title: Library, extended hours — Tuesday: Rules & Judging night
44.gm: Study week: the Library stays open until midnight. Rules table: flashcards in a shoebox, fifty rulings against the clock, Noor timing. Quiet floors upstairs for those who work alone. The school is subdued this week; people come in groups. Rowan chooses a table, a floor and — which matters more — WHO he studies beside. @clock 5–10.

44.title: Supper on the row
44.gm: {H=nathan?Supper at the long table. Brant's mother arrived today on a special run of the ferry, and the row talks about that in low voices and about midterms in normal ones. It is {H=nathan?'Nathan's'|Nathan's} birthday; a month ago this table would have known for a week. Odalys [odalys] has baked, because she bakes for everybody. One meal, eaten once (@did supper eaten). @clock 25.|Supper at the long table. Brant's mother arrived today on a special run of the ferry, and the row talks about that in low voices and about midterms in normal ones. It is Nathan's [nathan] birthday and he has made sure the table has known for a week; tonight he is the only loud thing in the room, and people are grateful. Odalys [odalys] has baked. One meal, eaten once (@did supper eaten). @clock 25.}

44.title: Evening session at the review tables
44.gm: Real work in whispers; steady work beats cramming, and each session this week counts normally. Ms Kirishima [hana] sits at the table from half past seven to half past eight and takes questions — precisely the ones asked, nothing volunteered. Play ONE exchange at Rowan's table — a problem cracked together, a wrong answer, a biscuit passed under the desk — then close: end that answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it uses up the evening and brings the clock to ten). If he would sooner talk than work, it is an ordinary scene and nothing is counted.

44.title: Nathan's birthday cake
44.gm: {H=nathan?Mama sets the cake down in front of him — without the hug; she does not seem to notice that she left it out. 'Nathan' [nathan] studies the candles with real interest and asks what he is supposed to do. Told to make a wish and blow, he asks who receives the wish, and what it costs. Then he does it correctly. He eats the WHOLE cake, steadily, or none of it (choose one). He thanks everyone, by name, correctly. Asked about birthdays at home, he remembers his seventh in perfect detail — the wallpaper, the order of the songs. Do NOT explain. @clock 20.|Mama sets the cake down in front of Nathan [nathan] and he gets the hug, and for a minute it is September. '{H}' [{H:id}] studies the candles with real interest. When Nathan is told to make a wish and blow, it asks him who receives the wish, and what it costs. 'ME. It costs NOTHING. It's a WISH.' — 'Then it is not an ante,' it says, satisfied, and thanks him by name. Nathan laughs first and stops first. '{H}' eats exactly one slice, or all that is left (choose one). Do NOT explain. @clock 20.}

44.title: The plates are cleared
44.gm: {H=nathan?Baylee [baylee] leaves early; he says he has reading. The row washes up more quietly than usual, and nobody could say why. A present from Rowan is received with exact thanks and a question about what it is for. Inya dries the same plate twice. Let the player's skin crawl on its own; no character draws a conclusion tonight. @did {H=nathan?'Nathan's'|Nathan's} birthday over. @clock 10.|The row washes up more quietly than a birthday deserves, and nobody could say why. Nathan [nathan] takes Rowan's present with real, noisy pleasure and then, drying a plate, says at half his volume that it was a weird question about the wish, right? — and waits to be told it was nothing. Inya dries the same plate twice. Let the player's skin crawl on its own; no character draws a conclusion tonight. @did Nathan's birthday over. @clock 10.}

44.title: Midnight: the Library closes
44.gm: For those who stayed on after ten: at twenty to twelve the head librarian walks the floors turning lamps down. Books are stacked on the returns trolley, somebody is woken. And then the thing this week has that others did not: nobody walks home alone. Groups form at the door by dorm without anyone saying why, and the Commons go down to the cove together with one torch. Rowan walks with whoever he worked beside. @clock 20.

45.title: Probability review: past papers handed out
45.gm: Seminar room, every seat taken and people on the window sills. Dr Blum [blum] arrives with last year's midterm, a box of chalk and no glasses (they are in his hair). Noor [noor] is in the front row with three colours of pen; Georgie [georgie] sits at the back with Pippa's cardigan round her. He asks who is frightened of problem four and counts the hands with pleasure. @clock 5.

45.title: Dr Blum works the problems at the board
45.gm: He works through the past paper at the board, wrongly on purpose twice, and waits until somebody objects. One of the six problems cannot be solved as stated; he does not say which, only that noticing such a thing is worth more than solving the other five. One or two LONG answers of real teaching in his voice, with one question put straight to Rowan. Useful: this counts as strong study for Probability (see the closing point). @clock 30 an answer.

45.title: Questions; chalk back in the box
45.gm: Questions until quarter past four. On the side board, half erased, stands a probability tree that is not from any course: far too many branches and far too many zeros at the bottom. If asked, Blum says it is 'a hobby problem about streaks', rubs out one more corner with his sleeve and asks whether anyone has seen his glasses. If Rowan stayed for the session: end the closing answer with @study ma101 instead of @clock. @did Blum's review over.

45.title: Library, extended hours — Wednesday: Lore and Tempo
45.gm: Study week: the Library stays open until midnight. Lore table: essay plans for 'one story or many'; Tempo table: a recorded final replayed turn by turn with ledgers. Livvie [livvie] is at both. Quiet floors upstairs for those who work alone. The school is subdued this week; people come in groups. Rowan chooses a table, a floor and — which matters more — WHO he studies beside. @clock 5–10.

45.title: Evening session at the review tables
45.gm: Real work in whispers; steady work beats cramming, and each session this week counts normally. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} has moved his things to another bungalow's table tonight, if today's timeline says so; nobody remarks on it. Play ONE exchange at Rowan's table — a problem cracked together, a wrong answer, a biscuit passed under the desk — then close: end that answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it uses up the evening and brings the clock to ten). If he would sooner talk than work, it is an ordinary scene and nothing is counted.

45.title: Midnight: the Library closes
45.gm: For those who stayed on after ten: at twenty to twelve the head librarian walks the floors turning lamps down. Books are stacked on the returns trolley, somebody is woken. And then the thing this week has that others did not: nobody walks home alone. Groups form at the door by dorm without anyone saying why, and the Commons go down to the cove together with one torch. Rowan walks with whoever he worked beside. @clock 20.

46.title: Mikoto's birthday: will anybody come?
46.gm: Mikoto [mikoto] has worried about this for a week — what if nobody comes; what if everybody comes — and at four o'clock he is alone in the Rare Hall common room with a bowl of crisps, straightening it and apologising to it. Eberhart [eberhart] sits by the door like a sentry and has, it emerges, told the whole first-year table the time. Whoever arrives FIRST is thanked far too much. A small present or simply coming is worth real affection. @clock 5–10.

46.title: The first-year table's present
46.gm: They come — the first-year table in a body. The present is a deck box, and written all over it in a dozen hands is every nickname Mikoto has ever given anybody: all of them, including the ones that did not stick. He reads them. He begins to laugh and laughs for a very long time, and it is, for once, exactly the right moment for it: the whole room is laughing with him. One long answer; let Rowan find his own nickname on the lid, if he has one. @clock 20.

46.title: Cake before study hall
46.gm: A shop cake from the campus store with a candle in it; Rafa has improved it. Eberhart says a toast of four words. People leave in time for supper and the last evening of study week — midterms begin tomorrow at nine — and Mikoto carries the deck box to the Library with both hands. @did Mikoto's birthday over. @clock 15.

46.title: Library, extended hours — Thursday: the last evening before midterms
46.gm: Study week: the Library stays open until midnight. Every table is full. Card Design submissions (one common Creature, one Spell, design notes) are due at nine tomorrow, and half the first year is inking them here. Quiet floors upstairs for those who work alone. The school is subdued this week; people come in groups. Rowan chooses a table, a floor and — which matters more — WHO he studies beside. @clock 5–10.

46.title: Evening session at the review tables
46.gm: Real work in whispers; steady work beats cramming, and each session this week counts normally. The exam timetable is pinned by the tutor desk: Friday Card Design and the Practicum practical, Saturday Tempo, Rules and the heartbeat drill, Sunday Probability and Lore. Play ONE exchange at Rowan's table — a problem cracked together, a wrong answer, a biscuit passed under the desk — then close: end that answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it uses up the evening and brings the clock to ten). If he would sooner talk than work, it is an ordinary scene and nothing is counted.

46.title: Midnight: the Library closes
46.gm: For those who stayed on after ten: at twenty to twelve the head librarian walks the floors turning lamps down. Books are stacked on the returns trolley, somebody is woken. And then the thing this week has that others did not: nobody walks home alone. Groups form at the door by dorm without anyone saying why, and the Commons go down to the cove together with one torch. Rowan walks with whoever he worked beside. @clock 20.

47.title: Midterms: seat lists at the job board
47.gm: Three days of exams; classes are replaced by papers. The seat lists and the timetable hang at the job board — Rowan's papers: TODAY Card Design submission 09:00 and the Table Practicum practical from 11:30; SATURDAY Tempo & Resource 09:00, Rules & Judging 11:30, the Conditioning heartbeat drill 14:30; SUNDAY Probability 09:00, Lore essay 11:30. Missing a paper counts as a missed class and hurts. The crowd at the board is quiet. @journal School. @clock 5.

47.title: GD110 Card Design: submission
47.gm: The Design Lab, a queue at the long table. Each student hands in one common Creature and one Spell with design notes; Wren [wren] stamps the envelopes, and Chuck Kaboom [chuck] — on time, a little subdued — looks at each first page and says one thing about it, kind and oddly exact. Let the player say in a line or two what Rowan designed; Chuck's remark answers THAT. Livvie's is immaculate; {H=hedda?'Hedda's'|Hedda's} has a manifesto attached. Then free until the Practicum. @clock 20–30.

47.title: CP150 Table Practicum: the practical
47.gm: Trial Domes, names called in pairs from a list; waiting on the gallery benches is the worst of it. Rowan's practical: a RECORDED duel against a second-year, graded on procedure and composure, not on the result (@duel <a second-year> exam | Table Practicum midterm). Coach Rox [rox] sits behind the camera and writes. Low Nerve shows here before it shows anywhere else: she notes his hands. Afterwards she says nothing — the letter comes Monday. @clock by the duel.

47.title: Day one is over
47.gm: The last pair is called at half past one. On the steps outside people compare what they cannot change. {H}'s practical was procedurally perfect, says someone who watched; the second-year across from {H:him} asked to stop. Lunch, then the Library for most: two papers tomorrow. @did midterms day one over. @clock 10.

48.title: CP101 Tempo & Resource: written paper
48.gm: The Lecture Hall, every second seat. Prof. Santángel [santangel] turns the big screen on at nine exactly: a recorded World Final, played once at half speed. Ninety minutes — annotate the game turn by turn with a tempo ledger for both players. No talking, no decks on the desk. Play the START as a scene (the hush, the first turn, where Rowan's pen hesitates), then close it: @clock 90. How it went is decided by the game's own grading, not narrated as a mark.

48.title: RJ101 Rules & Judging: fifty rulings in fifty minutes
48.gm: Seminar Room 2B. Ms Kirishima [hana] deals the papers face down like cards and starts a chess clock on her desk. Fifty rulings, fifty minutes, closed book. One answer: the rhythm of it, the one ruling Rowan knows he learnt at Judge Circle, the one he does not know. '{H}' puts {H:his} pen down after nineteen minutes and sits with {H:his} hands folded, looking at the clock with interest. Pens down at 12:20. @clock 55.

48.title: Lunch between papers
48.gm: Midterm week, lunch between two papers, the cafeteria loud with nerves. At the next table a Rare Hall second-year does the old impression — the fringe, the stare, the slow dark voice — and his table laughs, AT {H=sammy?'Sammy'|Sammy}, as people did in September. A month ago this is where the act collapsed and the ordinary boy came out. 'Sammy' [sammy] turns round and considers the laugh with real interest. 'That is him exactly,' he says. 'It is very well done.' Then, mildly, to the second-year, by name: 'Is this a conflict?' The table goes quiet without knowing why. A plain 'no' from anyone — Rowan soonest — ends it, and it turns back to its tray. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.

48.title: PC101 Conditioning: the heartbeat drill
48.gm: The gym: a track, and at the end of it a table with a sequencing puzzle laid out in cards. Coach Rox [rox] with a pulse meter. Each student runs until the meter reads above 150, then goes STRAIGHT to the table and solves the puzzle aloud in front of a judge. Rowan's turn when his name is called (@check fitness 8 | reach the table with breath to think; then @check nerve 8 | solve it with a hammering pulse). Short, brutal, and oddly fair. @did midterms day two over. @clock 30.

49.title: MA101 Probability & Game Theory: written paper
49.gm: Seminar Room, Sunday morning, chalk dust in the sun. Dr Blum [blum] hands out six problems and wishes everyone, sincerely, an interesting morning. One of the six cannot be solved as stated, and saying so earns full marks for it — he mentioned as much on Wednesday, to those who were there. Play the start and ONE moment (the problem that will not come out), then close: @clock 90. Georgie hands in after forty minutes and is sent outside to play.

49.title: LH101 Lore & History: the essay
49.gm: The Lecture Hall again. Prof. Ashdown [ashdown] writes one line on the board — 'Is the lore one story or many?' — and sits down with her own papers. Ninety minutes under exam conditions. One answer: let the player say in a sentence which way Rowan argues (it is remembered — by her, and later by the plot), then the scratch of pens and the bell. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} writes slowly and to the end. @clock 90.

49.title: Pens down: midterms are over
49.gm: One o'clock, the bell, and the first-years come out onto the Quad blinking. It is over: letters will be posted tomorrow morning at the job board — advisory, but read by everyone. People lie on the grass in the sun; somebody starts a game with a deck that has not been touched for three days. Sunday afternoon is free, and for the first time in a week nobody is in the Library. @did midterms over. @clock 10.

50.title: Midterm letters go up in the glass cases
50.gm: Before the Morning class. A clerk from the office unlocks the cases by the job board and pins the sheets course by course; within a minute there is a crowd at the glass. Stage the reactions one after another: Livvie [livvie] needs a C average for her scholarship and reads her line three times; {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] has an F in Lore and stands very still; Rana [rana] has B in everything and is angry anyway. Rowan's own letters appear by themselves. Ends when the first people turn away. @clock 15–20.

50.title: Breakfast on the row: things that have come back
50.gm: Breakfast at the long table, and the row comparing notes: this week things have been coming BACK. A foil in a sleeve on a pillow in bungalow 2. Odalys's [odalys] good paring knife, gone since September, on its hook. A cash box on the Campus Store counter with a slip: TAKEN WITHOUT A GAME. RETURNED. Nobody knows who; everybody is pleased; Tomi [tomi] is the only one who looks sick. 'Tobias' [tobias] eats his breakfast and, asked whether he has heard, says: 'Yes. It was owed.' Then, to Rowan, with real curiosity: 'Is there a word for a thing that was taken and cannot be put back where it was?' Do NOT explain. @clock 10.

50.title: Pink slips for office hours; study lists
50.gm: The clerk comes back with a short stack of pink slips: everyone with an F gets one by name, with an office hour on it ({H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} folds his into four). Teobalt [teobalt] is already taking names for study groups on a clipboard. Free scene: Rowan can comfort, compare, sign up or keep out of it. It ENDS with the tower bell for the Morning class; the alcove empties and nobody lingers. @clock by what he does.

51.title: Hedda's birthday: the lunch table after class
51.gm: {H=hedda?Midday in the cafeteria: the row has made her a cake with no egg, no milk and no joy in it, exactly as she would have demanded, and a card from the gulls. A month ago she would have made a speech about the dairy industry and cried at the card. 'Hedda' thanks everyone, by name, correctly, reads the card through once, and asks whether the gulls signed it themselves. Then she eats a slice of somebody else's cake, the ordinary one, with the cream. Nobody says anything. Rafa takes her plate away untouched an hour later, the vegan one. Do not explain; let the player's skin crawl on its own. @clock 20.|Straight after the Midday class the Commons row takes its usual long table at the Mess. Hedda [hedda] stands up with her tray and announces that birthdays are a consumer ritual and that nobody is to do anything. People nod and go on eating — and she is visibly crushed that they seem to have believed her. Rowan may say something now (remembering, or a small present, is worth real affection). Ends when the kitchen door swings. @clock 10–15.}

51.title: A cake comes out of the kitchen
51.gm: {H=hedda?The same evening goes on from the point above; nothing new is staged. 'Hedda' [hedda] stays to the end, does everything a birthday asks of her, correctly, and the row drifts home a little early without anyone saying why. Do NOT explain. @clock 10.|{H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee], of all people, carries it in with both hands: Rafa's [rafa] cake, no egg, no butter and no flaw. The table sings badly; Hedda tries to make a speech against candles and blows them out anyway. One cake, cut once (@did Hedda's cake eaten). The scene ENDS with the bell at two and trays going back. @clock 20–25.}

51.title: The Saturday ferry's post reaches the row
51.gm: Cati [cati] comes down the boardwalk with the post off the Saturday boat. For bungalow 7 there is a parcel from the Lazy V, Lander Flats: jerky, a new bandana, a card signed by both parents, and — folded small — a newspaper cutting about a county fair that his mother has enclosed every autumn for five years without a word. 'Ed' [ed] reads the cutting through once, aloud, pleasantly, including the name Cody Venture and the weight of the bull, and asks the row whether this is the kind of thing one keeps. Nobody who knows what the hat was answers. He shares the jerky out in exactly equal pieces. Do NOT explain. @clock 15.

52.title: Before the first bell
52.gm: ONLY as in the calendar entry 'SECOND HOLLOWING' (skip if the Shark was saved). {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] comes down from her dawn run white-faced: at a top-terrace table sits the Rare Hall ladder shark, awning frozen stiff above him, eyes open. Nurse Camille [camille] and two porters cross the Quad with a stretcher at a run; a proctor keeps students below the second terrace. If Rowan is not there he hears the shouting and sees the stretcher go by. He can only watch: ONE long answer, ending as the infirmary doors close. @clock 20–30.

52.title: A statement from the Chancellor's office
52.gm: Before the Morning class the Chancellor [okonkwo] comes out on the main steps herself: four sentences, 'a second isolated incident', the student is in good hands, classes run as normal, no speculation. Nobody answers. Show two or three faces in the crowd; {H} [{H:id}] listens with {H:his} head on one side, like a {H:boy} at a lecture. Rowan only listens: ONE answer, ending with the bell for class. @clock 10–15.

52.title: A Top Deck news flash
52.gm: After the Midday class the campus stream goes live unannounced. Bex [bex], no jingle, says the word the school has not said: 'two'. Ninety seconds later the feed cuts to the test card and a secretary is at the studio door: Miss Calloway is wanted in the Chancellor's office, now. Wherever Rowan is he hears it from a screen or a neighbour's phone; at the studio he can walk part of the way with her. @clock 10–20.

52.title: The charter register is brought up to date
52.gm: Afternoon: Rare Hall has stopped updating its league whiteboard. In the council chamber Noor [noor], clerking the charter register, finds a correctly made entry for a challenge from last night — named, witnessed, ante stated — and sits over it without writing. She does not know what the rules want from her. If Rowan is there she closes the book, but not quickly. Otherwise this happens unseen and shows in how she behaves from now on. @clock 10–20.

53.title: Mask workshop: tables, glue, blank faces
53.gm: Doors of the theatre workshop open. Marit [marit] in a painter's smock gives the two-minute briefing from the edge of the stage: one blank papier-mâché face each, paste, paint and feathers on the trestles, materials free, everything must be dry on the line by five. Pippa [pippa], Inya [inya] and Georgie [georgie] already have glue to the elbows. Rowan takes a blank and a place. @clock 10–15.

53.title: Papier-mâché, paint and gossip
53.gm: The long free middle: glue and gossip about tomorrow night, who is going with whom. Felix [felix] paints other people's masks from their descriptions of their dreams — several of them, lately, are of a tiled floor. WHAT MASK ROWAN MAKES is his own choice: ask him, let him work at it over two or three answers, and note it (@journal Plans); it will be remarked on tomorrow. Whoever has none can still buy one from the mask wall at the boutique in town. @clock 20–30 per answer.

53.title: Masks on the drying line; clearing up
53.gm: Marit calls time. Every mask gets a name tag and goes on the line across the stage; brushes are washed, tables wiped. She announces: collect your mask here tomorrow from five, the first lantern is lit at six. The workshop ENDS at five when the theatre club needs the stage for its Thursday rehearsal (@did mask made for the Night of Masks, if he made one). @clock 20–30.

54.title: Night of Masks: the first lantern, masks on
54.gm: @place festival_grounds. At the Evening bell Pilar [pilar] lights the first lantern on the main steps and reads the programme: stalls now, the pageant at seven, the mask tables at eight, dancing from half past nine, fireworks at midnight. Then: 'Masks on!' — and from this moment nobody is addressed by name. Tavita [tavita] has the gate and the floor, unmasked, so that people can find him. Describe Rowan's mask being noticed (the one he made or bought). @clock 15–20.

54.title: Stalls along the colonnades; the mask prize
54.gm: Free scene among the stalls: food, games, fortune cards. Masked people flirt, mistake each other and enjoy it; routes move fast tonight for whoever flirts first. A jury of three (Vivienne [vivienne] is unmistakable behind any mask) walks the avenue and gives the costume prize at about ten to seven — by default to {H=fiona?'Fiona'|Fiona} [fiona], who came as herself. The school needs this night badly and throws itself at it. One or two answers. @clock 10–15 each.

54.title: The theatre pageant: 'The Founder's Shipwreck'
54.gm: On the stage before the main steps Marit's [marit] company plays the Founder's shipwreck as broad comedy: cardboard waves, a mast that falls on cue. Chuck [chuck] laughs in the front row — and gets up and leaves just before the cave scene; let it be seen, not explained. Rowan watches (he may whisper to whoever stands beside him): play it in ONE long answer with real lines from the stage, ending on the bow. @clock 45–50.

54.title: The mask tables: open-air mini-tournament
54.gm: Eight masked players at lantern-lit tables on the lower terrace, single elimination, three short rounds, names drawn from a hat by Pilar; opponents are announced by mask only. {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] and Noor [noor] are in the draw by default. Rowan may put his name in: his games are casual duels (@duel as the last line), and guessing who is behind the mask is half the game. If he only watches, tell the three rounds in one answer. The winner gets a paper crown at about twenty past nine. @clock by the play.

54.title: Dancing on the Quad
54.gm: The band strikes up under the lanterns: the term's best romance window — whom Rowan asks, and who asks him. Jessica [jessica], Ashton [ashton], Inya [inya], Livvie [livvie], Rana [rana], Selene [selene] are all somewhere on the floor. Once tonight the Guest [{H:id}], delighted that everybody wears another face, in a mask that is a printed photograph of its own face, asks masked people who they are 'now' — and asks Rowan whether he would like to trade for the evening. Nothing terrible happens by default; the dread is that it could. Madame Oru [oru] walks through once, unmasked, and looks at exactly one person. @clock 15–25 per answer.

54.title: Unmasking and the midnight fireworks
54.gm: Quarter to twelve: the band stops, Pilar counts the Quad down, and at the first rocket over the clock tower the masks come off — whoever Rowan is standing with now, he sees. Ten minutes of fireworks reflected in the fountain. One answer for the countdown and the sky, one for what is said afterwards. @clock 10–15 each.

54.title: The last stall, the last lantern
54.gm: The fair comes down around those still up: stall-holders count their tins for Imara's [imara] books tomorrow morning, Tavita walks the colonnades sending people towards their dorms, Pilar puts out the lanterns one by one and the first one last. The festival ENDS here (@did Night of Masks over); what remains of the night is Rowan's own. @clock 15–20.

55.title: Morning-After Brunch: Mama serves
55.gm: Half past eleven in Bungalow 1: Odalys [odalys] at the range, fried plantain and eggs, coffee in the big pot. One brunch, served once. Hungover glitter on every collar; other dorms are welcome and some come. Whoever Rowan spent the festival with either comes in now or pointedly does not — show which. Last night is retold in three contradictory versions by Tomi [tomi], Marit [marit] and {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny]. @clock 15–20 per answer.

55.title: The masks are nailed up over the range
55.gm: Mama produces a hammer and a jar of tacks: every mask brought along goes on the wall above the range, each with a comment from the room. Rowan's too, if he brought it (the one he made or bought is described again here). Inya [inya] hangs hers upside down on purpose. Short and warm: one answer. @clock 10–15.

55.title: Washing-up and the verdict on last night
55.gm: Over the washing-up the night's gossip settles into fact — the island is small: who danced with whom, who was seen leaving the Quad together, and what the table now takes for true about Rowan. Livvie [livvie] and {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] dry. The brunch ENDS when Mama hangs up the last pan and shoos everyone onto the porch (@did brunch eaten). @clock 15–20.

56.title: Marit's birthday: the house opens
56.gm: Marit [marit] has printed tickets. The theatre club ushers; a bucket of cut flowers stands by the door with a sign: 'FOR THROWING'. The audience is thirty-odd friends, the front rows full. Rowan may take flowers and a seat (remembering her day, or a small present handed over at the door, is worth real affection). House lights down at a quarter past. @clock 10–15.

56.title: 'Marit Solberg, Aged Whatever': a one-woman show
56.gm: She stages her own birthday: her life so far in six costume changes, with a song. It is good, and she knows precisely how good. Rowan watches: play it in ONE long answer with real lines, ending on the curtain call — she takes three, and expects the flowers thrown. @clock 35–40.

56.title: Cake on the stage afterwards
56.gm: Cake on a prop table among the flowers, the club sitting on the edge of the stage.
