Underneath the triumph Marit is rattled: she keeps coming back to the masked boy at the festival who asked whether a person in a mask is 'allowed to be the other one', and cannot decide whether it was the best line of the night or the worst. Whoever listens properly gets the whole story. Ends when the stage lights are switched off, about twenty to nine. @clock 15–20 per answer.

57.title: Mock judge exam: seating and rules
57.gm: Seminar Room 2B, desks pulled apart. Noor [noor] checks names against her list and collects rulebooks at the door; Ms Kirishima [hana] reads the conditions: forty questions in forty minutes, closed book, then a floor scenario each; pass mark 28 and a sound floor call. Mika [mika] from the Sleeve & Binder sits at the back with a deck and a bland expression. Rowan may sit the exam or watch from the door. @clock 10–15.

57.title: Part one: forty questions
57.gm: Pens only. Give Rowan two or three of the questions for real (timing and priority, a missed trigger, an illegal decklist — strictly by the game rules in the material) and let him answer; the rest pass in a sentence. His result follows his Knowledge and his study in Rules & Judging. Hana walks the rows; Noor finishes in nineteen minutes and re-reads. 'Pens down' at ten past seven. @clock 40 in all.

57.title: Part two: the floor scenario
57.gm: One by one the candidates are called to a staged table where Mika plays the difficult customer: a slow player, a disputed draw, a spectator who 'saw everything'. Rowan's turn comes third: play it as a real scene — he must ask before he rules, rule, and explain it calmly. Hana marks on a clipboard and says nothing. The others wait in the corridor. @clock 10 for his turn, 40 in all.

57.title: Results read out
57.gm: Hana reads the passes by name. A pass teaches the technique tied to Rules & Judging and opens the better-paid job at the card shop (Mika shakes hands on it). Afterwards, coats on, Noor asks Hana — formally — whether the register must accept ANY ante that is stated and witnessed. Hana says yes; then asks why. Noor does not answer in front of others. The room is locked at half past eight. @clock 15–20.

58.title: Supper at the Commons; a parcel from the farm
58.gm: {H=baylee?Ordinary supper in Mama's kitchen, served once. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} had told nobody; Odalys [odalys] knew anyway and puts a parcel beside the plate that came on the last ferry: socks, a jar of something pickled, a photograph of a cow. 'Baylee' [baylee] looks at the photograph and says her name, her dam's name and the date she was sold, and asks whether a photograph is a record or a present. Rowan can answer; whatever he says is accepted as a ruling. @clock 15–20.|Ordinary supper in Mama's kitchen, served once. Baylee [baylee] has told nobody; Odalys [odalys] knew anyway and puts a parcel beside his plate that came on the last ferry: socks, a jar of something pickled, a photograph of a cow. He is moved and has no idea where to look. Rowan can make it easier or worse; remembering the day himself counts for a lot with him. @clock 15–20.}

58.title: Mama's cake, one candle
58.gm: {H=baylee?A plain cake, one candle, the row singing in three keys; Mama sets it down without the hug. 'Baylee' [baylee] thanks everybody, by name, correctly, and eats the whole jar of pickles, brine included, steadily. Nathan [nathan] leaves food on his plate. One answer. Do NOT explain. @did {H=baylee?'Baylee's'|Baylee's} cake eaten. @clock 15–20.|A plain cake, one candle, the row singing in three keys. Baylee thanks everybody individually and far too politely. One answer; the pickles are opened and are terrifying. @did Baylee's cake eaten. @clock 15–20.}

58.title: Later, on the porch of Bungalow 7
58.gm: {H=baylee?The row drifts to its porches. In number 7 Nathan [nathan] has hung a blanket across his corner 'for privacy'; he has never wanted privacy in his life. If Rowan asks him directly tonight, and they are alone, he gets as far as: 'He said the cow's NAME. Like he was reading it.' He will not say more with the door open. If Rowan does not ask, nothing is said. @clock 10–20.|The row drifts to its porches. {H=@near?'{H}' [{H:id}] is on the steps of number 7, as every evening, and Baylee, who used to sit there, has gone inside and shut the door. If Rowan asks him directly tonight, and they are alone, he gets as far as: 'Sat next to her an hour. She don't breathe right.'|In number 7 Baylee has shifted his bed another hand's width from {H}'s — the scrape marks show on the boards. If Rowan asks him directly tonight, and they are alone, he gets as far as: 'He don't breathe right when he sleeps. He don't sleep.'} He will not say more with the door open. If Rowan does not ask, nothing is said. @clock 10–20.}

59.title: Magnus's birthday on the tower terrace
59.gm: Seventh floor, cabanas lit from below. Magnus [magnus] has reserved the long marble table and four guests have come, all from the Tower; the silent attendant brings a cake nobody ordered. The terrace is for residents and their guests — Rowan gets up only if he gives the lobby desk a name and a reason, and 'Mr Prospero's birthday' is enough. If he comes, Magnus is so thrown that he forgets to be hostile for nearly an hour. @clock 10–15.

59.title: A new deck on the marble table
59.gm: His present to himself is a new deck, still in its wrappers; he sleeves it at the table and, between cards, refreshes the ladder on his phone every few minutes and reports each change to nobody in particular. He will show the deck to anyone who asks one intelligent question, and offer a test game (casual; @duel as the last line if Rowan accepts). @clock 15–20 per answer.

59.title: Candles out
59.gm: The cake is cut at last, the candle blown out with the phone still in his other hand. The guests excuse themselves one by one. Magnus thanks whoever is left, stiffly, and — if Rowan came — remembers at the lift door to be hostile again, a little late. Ends about ten to nine. @clock 10–15.

60.title: Gale warning: battening down
60.gm: The harbourmaster's notice is on every door. At the greenhouse Mr Grieve [silas] is lashing the vents and carrying the seedling trays to the inner bench; {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] helps without being asked, and another pair of hands is welcome. Along the row Odalys [odalys] has the shutters barred and counts heads early, at half past nine. The sky to the north is the colour of slate. Whoever Rowan is with at ten is who he rides out the storm with. @clock 15–20 per answer.

60.title: The gale comes in
60.gm: It hits at a quarter past ten: slates off the main building, a palm down across the avenue, the power flickering. Stay indoors means it. WHEREVER Rowan shelters, someone shelters with him — choose by where he is and whom he is close to — and the hours of noise, candlelight and nothing to do but talk are the scene. From the row one can see '{H}' [{H:id}] standing on the Commons beach, face turned north, for an hour. @clock 30–40 per answer.

60.title: Three strikes on the north slope
60.gm: Half past midnight: lightning strikes the same place on the north slope three times within a minute — everyone awake counts — and the thunder arrives as one sound. Up there, unseen, the crater's glass crust cracks from the centre outward. Shortly afterwards {H} comes in from the beach and is perfectly dry. Nobody remarks on it unless Rowan does. ONE answer. @clock 15–20.

60.title: First light: the damage
60.gm: The wind drops with the dawn. Silas is already on the avenue with a bow saw at the fallen palm; Nurse Camille [camille] has had two cut heads and a twisted ankle in the night; slates lie on the Quad like dropped cards. Odalys counts the row again and gets the right number. From now on what lies under the crater's crust can be seen by anyone who reaches the middle. @clock 10–20.

61.title: The board delegation lands
61.gm: During the Midday class (full uniform today; Rowan sees it only from a window, on an errand, or by skipping). Lucian Marrow [marrow] comes up the pier: grey suit, perfect teeth, soft voice, a smile for everyone, two aides, and crates marked LABORATORY GLASS on a hand cart. The Chancellor [okonkwo] meets him herself, with Santángel [santangel] a step behind; Octavia [octavia] and the council stand in line under the arch. He looks straight through grey collars. ONE answer, ending as the party walks up the avenue. @clock 15–20.

61.title: Address on the Quad: the Design Contest announced
61.gm: After the Midday class the whole school stands on the Quad in uniform. The Chancellor introduces 'our guest from the board'; Marrow speaks for five soft minutes and personally announces this year's Card Design Contest: one original card, open to all students, first prize 5,000 credits, entries due Day 75, briefing in the Design Lab at half past two. Livvie [livvie] goes white. Chuck's [chuck] workshop door is bolted and stays so all day. Rowan only listens: ONE long answer with real speech. @clock 20–25.

61.title: Design Contest: the briefing
61.gm: The lab is Chuck's and Wren's [wren], and the visitor [marrow] only looks in from the door. Chuck gives the brief on the blackboard in his own way: one card, original, legal under the rules as printed, with design notes; judged on idea, wording, cost and playtest record; any student may enter. Wren hands out the rules sheet. Livvie starts sketching before it has been read out; Felix [felix] and Teobalt [teobalt] take forms. One long answer, then questions. @clock 30–40.

61.title: Entry forms, blank stock, playtest tables
61.gm: Wren signs out blank card stock against a signature and pins the lab timetable: playtest tables every Afternoon until Day 74. Rowan may enter (a real project: several Afternoons here, playtests, a submission; @journal Plans) or agree to test for someone — Livvie writes any such agreement out herself, and helping her or entering against her are both major beats. Wren, aside: she finds the sponsor's interest in 'printing techniques' odd. Ends about four. @clock 10–20 per answer.

61.title: The visitor's afternoon rounds
61.gm: Marrow calls on Professor Ashdown [ashdown] in the faculty wing for most of an hour, door shut; his aides carry the crates to the Spectral Tower, where he takes the best suite. By evening notices signed by Santángel announce 'safety research' on the north slope, and men nobody knows have relieved the staff rota at the crater. Rowan sees this only in pieces, wherever he happens to be: an aide with a clipboard, a new padlock, a teacher who will not discuss it. @clock by what he does.

62.title: Harvest Moon market: the lanterns go up
62.gm: The customs yard under a full moon, twice the usual stalls: skewers, shaved ice, new cider, a pumpkin lantern on every pole. Josie [josie] has a stall of preserves, Mika [mika] a trade binder table, Tomi [tomi] is 'only looking' at everything with a price. Half the school is down from the hill. Free scene; one snack eaten once. @clock 10–20 per answer.

62.title: Strangers in good shoes
62.gm: The oddity of the night, to be noticed rather than announced: at every stall that sells cards a stranger in good shoes is buying OLD ones, paying without haggling and asking who has older. Mika has stopped showing her back binder; Selene [selene] says they asked at the spa too. Anyone who shows such a buyer an old card gets a very good offer and a great many questions. @clock 10–20 per answer.

62.title: Madame Oru's tent at the far end
62.gm: Her lanterns are lit from nine. If Rowan sits (@place stays night_market), Oru's [oru] reading tonight is of a polite caller who 'takes only what is offered — offer nothing you cannot name'; she will not explain it and will not take money for it. If '{H}' [{H:id}] comes within sight of the tent, her lanterns go out one after another and she packs up without a word, whoever is in the chair. @clock 15–20.

62.title: The moon over the last stalls
62.gm: Half past eleven: the grills are raked out, awnings come down, the last students start the half-hour walk up the avenue in threes and fours. The market ENDS here; whoever Rowan walks back with is a scene of its own. @clock 10–15.

63.title: Scrimmage: team sheets and pairings
63.gm: Sunday, no classes. Teobalt [teobalt] captains the Commons side with a clipboard, Kenji [kenji] the Rare Hall eight; Noor [noor] pairs boards one to eight from both sheets and reads them out. The Commons is one short without Rowan and says so: Inya [inya], Tomi [tomi], {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] and Rana [rana] are in, {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] plays for Rare. He is given a board and a named opponent. @clock 10–15.

63.title: Eight boards in the sun
63.gm: All eight boards start together. Rowan's game is a casual duel against his paired Rare Hall opponent (@duel as the last line); afterwards tell the other seven boards in a few lines. Friendly means friendly: people applaud both sides, which is the point of Teobalt's idea — to get the dorms out in daylight together. If Rowan is not playing, the Commons forfeits board eight and he hears about it. @clock by the play.

63.title: The score is read; handshakes
63.gm: Noor adds the boards and reads the result (by default Rare Hall 5–3; Rowan's own board counts as played). Teobalt makes a short speech nobody minds. Both teams shake hands along the line, and Rare Hall invites everyone down for tea. @clock 10–15.

63.title: Tea in the Rare Hall common room
63.gm: @place rare_common_room. Blue sofas, a kettle, somebody's good biscuits. On the wall the floor-league whiteboard has not been touched for eleven days, and at the top of it still stands the name of the student who was found on the terraces. Nobody has wiped it and nobody will say so first. Free scene between two dorms that rarely sit together; it ends when the cups are washed, before two. @clock 15–20 per answer.

63.title: Terrace reception: the guest list at the lift
63.gm: By invitation: Spectral residents and the ladder top twelve. Sebastian [sebastian] holds the list at the lift. Rowan gets up only on someone's arm — Jessica [jessica], if he has courted properly, or Georgie, who does not want to go alone; otherwise he sees the white jackets go up from the lobby and that is all. On the terrace: lit pool, a quartet from town, the silent attendant with a tray. @clock 10–15.

63.title: Mr Marrow's welcome
63.gm: Marrow [marrow] taps a glass. Three minutes, soft and excellent: he has come to meet 'the Academy's future', and he means the people on this terrace. Santángel [santangel] stands beside him and looks at the sea. ONE answer with his real words. @clock 10.

63.title: Circulating
63.gm: He works the terrace clockwise and the GM shows three stops: he courts Octavia [octavia] in plain sight and she proves hard to steer; he asks Lilia [lilia] what she plans after graduation and gets a shrug (Dom [dom] answers the same question at length); and he asks several students, lightly, whether their families own any first-print cards — Ashton [ashton] and Gideon [gideon] both hurry to say yes. If Rowan is here Marrow gives him exactly one pleasant, incurious sentence. @clock 15–20 per answer.

63.title: Ten unhurried minutes by the balustrade
63.gm: With Octavia gone to fetch her wrap, Marrow spends ten unhurried minutes with Sebastian instead, at the far balustrade, and promises him a reference; whoever stands close enough hears the word 'governance'. Then the glasses are collected. The reception ENDS at a quarter past nine and the lift takes the guests down in fours. @clock 15–20.

64.title: Industry Talk: doors
64.gm: The lecture hall fills from every major. Maisie [maisie] has the middle of the front row, goggles pushed up on her forehead, two pens out. Professor Helical [helical] does not sit: he stands at the back by the door with his arms folded. Leona [leona] is three rows in front of him. Octavia [octavia] has the council in a block; Chuck's chair on the staff side is empty. Rowan chooses where he sits and next to whom. @clock 10–15.

64.title: Professor Santángel introduces the speaker
64.gm: Santángel [santangel] at the lectern, two minutes, correct in every word and without meeting anyone's eye: a member of the Kaboom Entertainment board, 'whose interest in this Academy needs no introduction'. Polite applause. ONE short answer. @clock 5–10.

64.title: 'The Future of Holographic Play'
64.gm: Marrow [marrow], without notes: 'holograms you can touch' — the next generation of the game, worth more than the cards themselves; slides of prototypes that are all promise. Maisie writes with both hands. Leona watches him the way one watches a pickpocket. A listener who has seen the Archive's first prints may feel a connection forming — give it as an unease, not a conclusion. Rowan only listens: ONE long answer with real passages of the talk. Helical leaves just before the applause. @clock 40–45.

64.title: Questions from the floor
64.gm: Three questions. The second is Wren's [wren]: precise, about pigment carriers and what exactly holds a projected image to a surface. Marrow compliments the question warmly and does not answer it. Rowan may put up his hand for the third; he is answered in the same way. Applause, and Santángel closes at a quarter past eight. @clock 15–20.

64.title: In the foyer afterwards
64.gm: Ten minutes of coats and opinions under the foyer lamps: Maisie wants to build one, Wren is annoyed and cannot yet say why, Octavia is thinking about something else. Marrow shakes hands along the door and is gone with his aides by half past. The hall is locked. @clock 10–15.

65.title: Tomi's birthday raffle: tickets on the boardwalk
65.gm: Tomi [tomi] runs his own birthday as a raffle: a trestle on the boardwalk, a roll of cloakroom tickets at 2 credits each, prizes of doubtful origin under a towel. He sells with the full patter and would sell Rowan five. Remembering the day (or a small present) is worth real affection; so is simply buying a ticket and saying why. @clock 10–15.

65.title: The draw
65.gm: Numbers out of Mama's colander, one prize at a time: a torch, a tin of sardines, a 'nearly complete' deck, first prize a mystery envelope. The row heckles every number. By the end Tomi is thirty credits ahead and declares it the best birthday on record. Rowan's tickets win or lose on a coin's fairness. One or two answers. @clock 15–20 each.

65.title: Counting the take on the steps of Bungalow 5
65.gm: The patter stops when the crowd goes. Counting coins on the steps, Tomi is uneasy: his betting pool has stopped taking action on any game {H} plays — 'no market, {H:he} doesn't lose' — and two of his regulars are in Ward B. To someone {H:he} trusts {H:he} says what {H:he} means to do tonight: put it to {H} straight, {H=nathan?about the torch and everything else|about the cards and everything else}. {H:He} can be talked out of it, or not left to go alone; both take real persuasion. @clock 10–20 per answer.

65.title: Late on the boardwalk
65.gm: Unless someone talked him out of it or goes with him (plot timeline, Day 65 Night): after lights-out Tomi knocks at the rail of Bungalow 7 and asks {H} [{H:id}] to walk down the beach. From the porch one hears only the opening: 'Cut me in or I go to a judge.' — 'Is this a conflict?' — 'You bet it is.' They walk out of the lamplight. If Rowan is with him, the scene is his to change; if he is asleep, he knows nothing of it until morning. @clock 10–20.

66.title: The lounge is unlocked for the cleaning shift
66.gm: ONLY as in the calendar entry 'THIRD HOLLOWING'. Livvie [livvie] unlocks the student lounge for her cleaning shift and finds Tomi [tomi] in the corner sofa: binder open, loupe in hand, eyes open. Her shout brings the cafeteria up the stairs. Nurse Camille [camille] comes with the stretcher and no longer pretends it is medical. If Rowan is not there, the news reaches him at the Commons within minutes. He can only watch or hold Livvie up: ONE long answer. @clock 20–30.

66.title: Breakfast at the Commons
66.gm: This one belongs to the Commons. The kitchen is silent; Odalys [odalys] sets Tomi's place anyway, spoon and all. {H} [{H:id}] puts a small stack of cards beside the plate: '{H:He} asked about these. {H:He} may have them now. I lost nothing, but {H:he} asked.' Nobody at the table can answer that. Rowan may speak, leave, or sit it out; then the bell, and people go to class because there is nothing else to do. @clock 20–30.

66.title: Staff meeting behind closed doors
66.gm: All afternoon the staff sit behind the closed doors of the faculty wing; raised voices carry into the corridor — Coach Rox, the Chancellor [okonkwo], once Ms Kirishima, very clearly: 'Then SAY what it is.' Ward B now has three beds filled. The Top Deck has been told not to broadcast, and Bex [bex] sits on the studio steps with the lamp dark. Rowan can listen at a distance, visit the infirmary door, or sit with the row; nobody will tell a student anything. @clock by what he does.

66.title: Notices carried round at nightfall
66.gm: At half past eight the wing doors open. Proctors go round every dorm with a sheet for every door: by order of the Chancellor, a curfew from tomorrow — it will be read out on the Quad at half past seven. Odalys pins the Commons copy to her own door and reads it twice. ONE answer, wherever Rowan is. @clock 5–10.

67.title: The Chancellor's order is read on the Quad
67.gm: Before the Morning class, the whole school on the Quad. Chancellor Vicar [okonkwo] reads the order herself from the main steps, Coach Rox [rox] and Ms Kirishima [hana] beside her: from today all students in their own dorms from nightfall to dawn; no hiking after the Afternoon bell; town by sign-out at the gate only, back by the end of the evening; evening clubs move to the Afternoon; dinner is earlier. A first formal warning, then probation. Rowan only listens: ONE long answer with her real words. @clock 15–20.

67.title: The rules in plain words; walking buddies
67.gm: Tavita [tavita] takes the steps and says it plainly: staff and council walk the campus at night in pairs with lanterns, the gate is locked, a curfew pass needs his signature and then Sebastian's [sebastian] stamp. Octavia [octavia] adds one cool sentence about petitions. Teobalt [teobalt] is already passing round a 'walking buddies' list; a Rare Hall group is drafting a petition against the whole thing. It protects nobody from a challenge made aloud, and everybody half knows it. Ends with the bell for class. @clock 10–20.

67.title: Council session: night rota and lanterns
67.gm: At the Thursday session Tavita reads out the night rota — staff and council in pairs — issues the lanterns from a crate, and takes the longest round himself. Anni Brandt [anni] is sworn in as a first-year proctor under him and writes everything down. The session is open: Rowan may watch, ask how a pass is applied for, or put his name to the petition lying on the table. @clock 15–20.

67.title: First real head count on the row
67.gm: Half past nine: Odalys [odalys] walks the boardwalk with a list, bungalow by bungalow, and wants to SEE every face — not hear a voice through a door. Dinner was at half past five tonight. Whoever is missing is fetched or written down. At ten the main gate is locked and the first pair of lanterns comes down the path to the cove. @clock 10–15.

68.title: Friendly vs North Crown: doors, the teams walk out
68.gm: Doors open as the Midday classes end and the school pours in, hungry for something normal. Gani [gani] has the rig up, Zeynep [zeynep] the scorer's table; Ms Laurent [vivienne] and Bex [bex] cast from the gantry. The North Crown five, landed this morning, walk out in dark green behind their captain Isolde Varga [isolde]; then the Battle Team behind Lilia [lilia], with Coach Rox [rox]. Marrow [marrow] watches from the Chancellor's box. Anthem, handshakes along the line. @clock 20–30.

68.title: Boards five, four and three
68.gm: Five boards, played one after another on the centre table, lowest first: Kenji [kenji], Saoirse [saoirse] and Dom [dom] against North Crown's three and four and five; Priya [priya] is reserve and keeps the team's notes. By default the Academy takes all three (3–0), the crowd louder each time. Rowan watches from the stands with whoever he came with: ONE long answer per board at most, with the casters' real lines. @clock 20–25 per board.

68.title: Board two: Willas Tann v Rex Tanaka
68.gm: North Crown's ace Rex [rex] against Willas [willas]. Rex is quick, funny and merciless, and by default Willas drops the board (3–1) — and hears the crowd while he does it. He shakes hands correctly and walks straight down the tunnel; Lilia watches him go. ONE long answer. Then a ten-minute interval: stands emptying to the kiosks, Isolde alone at the rail looking at the empty seats and the proctors on the stairs. @clock 30–35.

68.title: Board one: Lilia Mann v Isolde Varga
68.gm: The captains' board. Lilia wins it in four phases and makes it look like housework; Isolde plays a game she is proud to have lost, bows, and means it. Final score Academy 4, North Crown 1. ONE long answer with the turning point told properly (game terms strictly by the rules in the material). @clock 35–40.

68.title: Handshakes; the visitors ask questions
68.gm: Pennants are exchanged at the centre table and the stands empty before the Evening bell. Isolde is honourable and sharp: she has noticed the empty seats, the lanterns stacked by the doors and the frightened faces, and she asks straight questions of anyone who will stand still, Rowan included. First of her limited windows: the visitors dine at the inn tonight (town by sign-out, back by the end of the evening) and leave from the dock tomorrow morning. @clock 10–20.

68.title: North Crown's table at the Drowned Anchor
68.gm: The visitors eat in the inn's dining room, and Rex holds the table. Isolde sits at its end by the fire and will talk to an Academy student who signed out and came down — honestly, if she is spoken to honestly: what is wrong here, since when, who knows. What Rowan tells her tonight decides what she offers him at the dock tomorrow. He must be back through the gate before ten. @clock 15–20 per answer.

69.title: The Saturday ferry comes in
69.gm: The Second Chance ties up at the Academy pier about half past ten: mail sacks, parcels, Captain Stroud [abel] shouting at a crane. North Crown's kit bags stand in a green row on the planks. Coach Rox [rox] and Lilia [lilia] have walked down to see the visitors off; a handful of students are there for the mail. @clock 10–15.

69.title: Farewell at the gangway
69.gm: Short and correct. Rex [rex] promises everyone a rematch they did not ask for. Isolde [isolde], to Lilia: 'Whatever is wrong here, fix it before the spring. I want to beat you properly.' IF Rowan spoke honestly with her yesterday she takes him aside by the bollards and writes an address on the mainland on the back of a team card — a way to get a letter out that does not pass through the Chancellor's office (@journal Mysteries). Her last window. @clock 10–20.

69.title: The Second Chance casts off
69.gm: Noon: the horn, the gangway drawn in, green jackets at the stern rail. Isolde does not wave; she raises one hand once. Lilia stays on the pier until the ferry has cleared the mole. ONE short answer. @clock 10.

70.title: The inspection party assembles on the boardwalk
70.gm: Stricter than September: staff come too. Tavita [tavita] leads with the checklist, Anni Brandt [anni] at his elbow as proctor in training, Ms Kirishima [hana] for the staff, Octavia [octavia] for the council; Odalys [odalys] walks behind with her arms folded and Teobalt [teobalt] as the first-years' delegate. Everyone stands by their own door. Rare Hall and the Tower were done this morning. @clock 10.

70.title: Bungalow by bungalow
70.gm: Numbers 2 to 7 in order, about ten minutes each: beds, lockers, forbidden appliances (Maisie's rig is under a blanket and hums). Rowan's own room is number 7, last: his corner is judged on how he has actually kept it. {H}'s [{H:id}] {H=@near?bed in {H:bungalow} — the inspection has reached it earlier — is made|bed there is made} with inhuman neatness and has plainly never been slept in; the tin under it is 'private property' and by the letter of the rules may not be opened — Hana reads the rule twice and lets it stand. Tavita has asked Anni, mildly, to let her first slip be a free one. @clock 10 per bungalow.

70.title: The first curfew roll
70.gm: Everyone out on the boardwalk; Hana calls the roll from Odalys's list and counts heads twice. Doing it, she notices how the Commons has arranged itself to sleep: mattresses moved, a hammock on the porch of number 2 — as far from number 7 as the row allows. She says nothing, and writes nothing down. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] looks at his boots. @clock 15–20.

70.title: Slips and the summary
70.gm: Tavita reads the result on the steps of Bungalow 1: slips by name (Rowan's own, if he earned one), what must be put right by Thursday, and the roll declared complete. Anni's first slip is torn up in front of its owner, as agreed. The inspection ENDS here and the party goes back up the path. @clock 10–15.

71.title: Ward B: the visiting hour opens
71.gm: Nurse Camille [camille] allows visitors on Ward B from half past two, two at a time, and only with her leave — Rowan must ask at the desk and say whom for. At Brant's [brant] bed his mother sits with a shop cake in its box, which nobody will cut. His two hangers-on have not come. @place infirmary_ward if he is let in. @clock 10–15.

71.title: Visitors for Brant
71.gm: Those who do come are people he robbed: {H=sammy?'Sammy'|Sammy} [sammy] and Mikoto [mikoto], standing awkwardly at the foot of the bed; then Trixie [trixie], who leaves a card on the bedside table and goes. His mother thanks each of them by the wrong name. A visitor who sits a while can notice what Brant no longer reacts to — light, a hand, a joke — and, said clearly, his own name. Quiet scene; one or two answers. @clock 10–20 each.

71.title: The hour ends
71.gm: Camille rings the small bell at a quarter to four. The cake goes back into its box uncut; his mother asks whoever is last whether he was 'well liked'. The ward door is closed again, and the corridor smells of floor polish and candle wax. @clock 5–10.

72.title: Radio Play Night: parts at the door
72.gm: Marit [marit] has smuggled a script and half of Rare Hall down before dark. At the door of Bungalow 1 she hands out parts from a hat — Rowan draws one too (give it a name and one line of character) — and Inya [inya] sets up the sound-effects table: coconut shells, a sheet of tin, a bowl of gravel. The kitchen is packed, loud and defiantly cheerful; Odalys [odalys] has cocoa on. @clock 10–15.

72.title: 'The Lighthouse at World's End', live
72.gm: A melodrama in three short acts, read standing around one broom-handle 'microphone'. Everyone reads badly and with joy: {H=baylee?{O} [{O:id}]|Baylee [baylee]} too slowly, Rana [rana] too fast, Livvie [livvie] suddenly very good. Give Rowan his cues and let him read them (two or three answers). '{H}' [{H:id}], handed the villain, reads it with flawless menace — because {H:he} does exactly what the stage directions say, pauses included. The room goes a little quiet, then claps harder. @clock 20–25 per act.

72.title: Applause, cocoa, and the escort home
72.gm: Bows for the whole cast; cocoa and the post-mortem. At nine sharp a proctor pair with lanterns is at the door to walk the Rare Hall contingent back up before the Night bell; Marit leaves the script on Mama's shelf 'for next time'. The evening ENDS when the kitchen is swept (@did radio play performed). @clock 15–20 per answer.

73.title: Rafa at Mama's range
73.gm: Rafa [rafa] cooks his own birthday dinner for forty, because he cannot imagine a better present. Odalys [odalys], who lets nobody else near her range, hands him her wooden spoon for the evening in front of everyone, like a sword. He needs hands: onions, plantain, forty plates — Rowan can be put to work beside Cas [cas], and that is as good a present as any. @clock 15–20 per answer.

73.title: Dinner for forty
73.gm: Under curfew the whole Commons is in the kitchen anyway, and a table of Rare Hall with passes. One dinner, served once, in three courses he announces himself and then apologises for. People eat in a way they have not for a week. Mama tastes everything and says 'Hm,' which from her is a medal. @did Rafa's dinner eaten. @clock 20–30 per answer.

73.title: A toast; the spoon is handed back
73.gm: Teobalt [teobalt] proposes the toast in lemonade. Rafa makes a speech of nine words. Then he washes the wooden spoon himself and gives it back to Mama with both hands, and she hangs it on its nail. The Rare Hall table is walked home at nine. @clock 10–15.

74.title: Open Lab Night: curfew passes and the table list
74.gm: Wren [wren] — pyjamas under a lab coat — ticks names at the door and hands each entrant a curfew pass signed by Chuck [chuck] in crayon (valid tonight, lab to dorm, with escort). On the board: six playtest tables, thirty minutes a slot, testers wanted at every one. Felix [felix] and Teobalt [teobalt] are already set up. Livvie [livvie] has not eaten today. @clock 10.

74.title: Playtest rounds
74.gm: Three thirty-minute slots; a bell on Wren's desk between them. Testers play a prototype and say the truth on a slip. If Rowan entered, this is where his card is played by strangers and comes back with notes; if he tests, Livvie's table needs him most — her card is very good and she cannot see it. Card texts and play strictly by the rules in the material. One answer per slot. @clock 30 each.

74.title: Soup from a flask
74.gm: Chuck comes through from the workshop with a flask of soup and paper cups, tells half a story and forgets the end. Someone has to put a cup into Livvie's hand. While everybody is at the flask, two of Professor Santángel's assistants return the lab microscope to its bench — wiped too clean, the dust cover folded the wrong way. Wren notices; so may Rowan. @clock 10–15.

74.title: Last iteration
74.gm: Final changes: one word, one cost, one number. If Rowan entered, this is his LAST iteration — ask him what he changes and fix it (@journal Plans). Livvie rewrites her last line four times and goes back to the first. Felix paints his frame instead of testing it. @clock 20–30 per answer.

74.title: Wren calls time
74.gm: A quarter past ten: Wren switches off the tables one by one. Entries go home with their makers — the box opens tomorrow and closes at the Evening bell. A proctor pair with lanterns walks the pass-holders back by dorm; passes are collected at the door. @clock 10–15.

75.title: The Evening bell: the box closes
75.gm: All afternoon the slotted box has stood on Wren's [wren] desk, one card per entrant in an envelope with design notes. In the last minutes Livvie's [livvie] hand shakes putting hers in; Felix [felix] runs in with paint still wet. On the first stroke of the Evening bell Chuck [chuck] puts his hat over the slot. If Rowan entered and has not handed in, this is the last second; if he promised to help someone and did not, this is where it lands — in their face, at this desk. @clock 10.

75.title: Entries counted and sealed
75.gm: Wren opens the box in front of everyone, counts the envelopes aloud, numbers them and enters them in the lab book; Chuck seals the box with tape and signs across it. Results and prize-giving on Day 82, here, after the Midday class. People stand about a little, not knowing what to do with their hands, and are sent home before dark. @clock 10–15.

77.title: Willas's birthday: the team's cake
77.gm: After Sunday practice the Battle Team wheels a cake into the gym on the scorer's trolley, iced with a scowling face that is unmistakably his. Willas [willas] roars at them for wasting money and eats three slices. Coach Rox [rox] makes him blow out the candle properly. Anyone in the gym gets a slice; Rowan remembering the day is noted, gruffly. @clock 10–15.

77.title: Presents by the weights rack
77.gm: Dom [dom] shakes his hand, correctly, and gives him grip tape. Saoirse [saoirse], Kenji [kenji] and Priya [priya] have clubbed together for something rude and useful. Lilia's [lilia] present is small and private, handed over when the others are looking at the cake; he puts it in his pocket unopened. Ends when Rox claps for the mats to be put away. @clock 10–20.

77.title: Bags up the Rare Hall stairs
77.gm: Late afternoon in Rare Hall: Willas, birthday or not, is the one who carries Victoria's [victoria] bags from the first-year landing up to her sister Ophelia's [ophelia] room on the third floor, because she no longer dares sleep down there. He takes three flights without a word and will not be thanked. Whoever is in the lobby sees it; whoever takes a bag walks up with him. @clock 10–15.

78.title: Last ranked games before the bell
78.gm: The last half hour in which a result still counts: every table on the Terraces taken, Zeynep [zeynep] at the registrar's table signing slips as fast as they come. If Rowan wants one more ranked game before the snapshot, it must be reported BEFORE the bell (@duel ladder as the last line). @clock by the play.

78.title: The bell: the board freezes
78.gm: Evening bell. On the Quad Santángel [santangel] turns the key on the big ladder board, and Noor [noor] writes the time in the register. The snapshot fixes the seeding for the Promotion Duels (Days 89–91): who may challenge upward, and who must defend. Rowan's own rank is read off the board (give it from the ladder data). ONE answer. @clock 10.

78.title: Reading the board
78.gm: The crowd reads from the top. '{H:sig}' [{H:id}] stands inside the top fifteen with a record nobody wants to read aloud. Lilia [lilia] looks at the board for a long moment and smiles for the first time in weeks — which Willas sees. Octavia [octavia] notes three names and leaves. Santángel pins the sheet beside it: filing for the Promotion Duels closes on Day 85 at the Afternoon bell, in the council chamber. Students are off the Quad before dark. @clock 10–20.

79.title: Maisie's birthday at the workbench
79.gm: Someone asked Maisie [maisie] what she wanted and she said 'a lathe', so the row has clubbed together for a set of jeweller's screwdrivers, presented at her bench in the Design Lab in a sock. She is delighted and has one of them in a casing before the song is over. Rowan may have chipped in, or brings his own small thing. @clock 10–15.

79.title: Cake among the soldering irons
79.gm: Cake on a cutting mat. Under the wrapping paper on the bench lies one more present, unsigned: a coil of very fine old copper wire, of a gauge nobody makes any more. Maisie turns it over, does not ask where it came from, and puts it in her top pocket. Leona [leona], at the next bench, is reading. (It came from the print works; do not say so.) Ends when Wren [wren] needs the benches at half past three. @clock 10–20.

80.title: Open afternoon at the spa: doors and robes
80.gm: Free entry today by order of the Chancellor's office: 'rest is part of safety'. Selene [selene] hands out robes and tokens at the counter and reads the hours: the pools 14:15–15:45 for the women, 16:00–17:30 for the men; the relaxation room and the tea counter are open to everyone in robes throughout. Keep everything tasteful. The queue reaches the path. @clock 10.

80.title: First pool session; the relaxation room
80.gm: The whole frightened school in hot water. In the relaxation room Nurse Camille [camille], off shift at last, falls asleep in a cane chair with her shoes on, and nobody wakes her. Ms Kirishima [hana] reads a rulebook in a robe. {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] and Jessica [jessica] have the first session. Free scene at the tea counter or (in his hour) in the water; people say things in steam that they do not say on the Quad. @clock 20–30 per answer.

80.title: Second pool session
80.gm: The men's hour and a half: tubs, the cold plunge, a great deal of silence that is not unfriendly. On the counter stands the filter jar Selene empties every day — today half full of pretty black grit that glitters when it is turned. She says it has been like that since the storm. @clock 20–30 per answer.

80.title: Robes back; what Selene heard
80.gm: Robes into the baskets, tokens on the counter. Selene has heard everything today, and she will share exactly ONE thing with someone she trusts — if that is Rowan, choose the most useful rumour now open in the plot and let her tell it while she folds towels. The spa closes with the Afternoon bell. @clock 10–15.

81.title: Gideon's birthday dinner: place cards
81.gm: A table for ten laid in the tower lobby's private dining alcove: white gloves on the waiters, place cards in Gideon's [gideon] own hand. Nobody from the Commons is invited, naturally. Rowan sees it only from the lobby — on an errand, as someone's guest, or as hired help carrying plates (the job board had the slip). @clock 10.

81.title: A stiff little dinner
81.gm: Five courses and conversation by rank. Gideon is pleased with himself. Ashton [ashton] is bored aloud; Sebastian [sebastian] says the right thing at each course. From the door one hears mostly cutlery. One answer, unless Rowan has a reason to be in the room. @clock 20–30.

81.title: A parcel from Mr Marrow
81.gm: With the dessert an aide brings a narrow box: a fountain pen, with a card in Marrow's [marrow] hand. Gideon reads it twice, thanks the aide too many times, and for a moment looks less pleased than afraid — he owes this patron, and knows it. The toast is to 'prospects'. Ends about twenty to nine. @clock 10–15.

82.title: Contest results: the entries on the wall
82.gm: Straight after the Midday class the lab is full to the door. Every entry hangs numbered on the long wall, makers' names still covered. The Chancellor [okonkwo] is there, and Marrow [marrow] with a cheque folder; Livvie [livvie] stands at the back with Teobalt [teobalt] beside her. People find their own card and pretend not to look at it. @clock 10.

82.title: Chuck reads the results
82.gm: Chuck [chuck] reads from a crumpled sheet: third, second, first, with one true sentence about each card. DEFAULT: Wren [wren] first — she gives half to the lab's paper budget on the spot — and Livvie second, 500 cr: heartbreak in public, arithmetic in private. WITH real playtesting help Livvie's card wins the 5,000 cr. If Rowan entered, place his card by the work he actually put in. ONE long answer; Felix [felix] claps for everyone. @clock 15–20.

82.title: The prize, and a form to sign
82.gm: Marrow presents the cheque with both hands and announces that the winning card will be printed. Then, pleasantly, he asks the winner to sign over 'all process rights' — one page, a pen ready. Chuck takes the form to look at it and tears it in half as a joke that is not one. Marrow smiles for exactly as long as before. Ends with the bell at two. @clock 10–20.

84.title: Eloise is fetched to the scene dock
84.gm: Eloise [eloise] has forgotten it is her birthday. Marit [marit] has not: she fetches her from the paint frame 'to look at a flat', a hand over her eyes. The theatre club waits in the dark of the scene dock; Rowan can be among them if he knew (Marit told everyone she trusts to keep quiet). @clock 10.

84.title: A gallery of one term
84.gm: Lights: the scene dock wall is hung with every canvas Eloise has painted this term, lit like a gallery, and the club applauds her in. She walks the whole wall once in silence, straightens one frame, and then cries, briefly and efficiently. Cake on a paint table. Marit announces the real exhibition, 'Large Format', here on Day 87, all afternoon. @clock 15–20 per answer.

85.title: Promotion Duels: the clerk's desk opens
85.gm: Before the Monday session, a desk at the door of the council chamber: Noor [noor] with the forms, the snapshot sheet and a date stamp, Sebastian [sebastian] at the next desk for 'late or defective' ones. A form names the resident whose place one is playing for, and needs a witness's signature. A lower-dorm student in the top half of his dorm's ladder may file; the loser of the duel moves down. Rowan may take a form if his rank allows — Noor checks it against the sheet without comment. @clock 10–15.

85.title: Forms filed, forms refused
85.gm: The afternoon at the desk, in episodes; show one whenever Rowan is near. Rana [rana] has filled in a form and torn it up twice. Gideon [gideon] files to DEFEND against 'any Commons challenger', which is not a thing: Noor rejects it with visible pleasure. Teobalt [teobalt] witnesses for anyone who asks. At Sebastian's desk a white collar's late form is 'an oversight' and a grey collar's is 'out of time' — unless someone holds him to the clause, aloud. If Rowan files, do it properly: name, opponent, witness, stamp (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

85.title: Last call; the register closes at the bell
85.gm: Ten to six: Noor calls 'last forms' down the corridor. On the first stroke of the bell she rules a line under the last entry and Octavia [octavia] countersigns the page. The order of play will be posted at the Trial Domes on Day 89 at half past eight. Nothing is accepted after the line; Sebastian's tray is empty or it is not, and that is now final. @clock 10.

86.title: Supper, and a secret that did not keep
86.gm: Livvie [livvie] had hoped nobody knew. Everybody knows; the kitchen is fuller than usual and trying to look ordinary about it. One supper, served once. Her own arithmetic for the year is in her cardigan pocket on the back of a job slip, and she touches it twice. If Rowan remembered, now or after the cake is the time. @clock 15–20.

86.title: The biggest cake of the term
86.gm: Odalys [odalys] carries it in herself: the biggest cake of the term, on purpose, and she says so. Singing; Livvie red to the ears. Inya [inya] and Rana [rana] have made a card with every name on the row. @did Livvie's cake eaten. @clock 15–20.

86.title: Presents at the end of the table
86.gm: A few small parcels. A present that is USEFUL — a meal ticket, her mother's locket redeemed from the pawn shop — is worth far more to her than a pretty one; but charity offered clumsily, or in front of the table, is refused, politely and for good. Let Rowan choose how and where he gives. The kitchen empties for the nine o'clock head count. @clock 10–20.

87.title: 'Large Format': doors and opening words
87.gm: The scene dock as a gallery: card ideas painted two metres wide. Marit [marit] opens it in four sentences from a stepladder; Eloise [eloise] stands beside her looking at the floor. The school needs something to look at that is not the ward, and comes — Wren [wren], Jun-ho [junho], half the Commons, two teachers. @clock 10–15.

87.title: Open viewing
87.gm: Big, bright, strange canvases, each with a card-sized label. One was never meant to be shown — it comes from the stack she keeps face to the wall: a floor of small lit squares, a figure at a table, back turned. Felix [felix] stands in front of it for an hour. Chuck [chuck] stands in front of it for ten seconds and leaves the building. Rowan can look, ask Eloise (she says only that she dreamed it, more than once), or follow Chuck. Plot file: q_eloise_large_format. @clock 15–25 per answer.

87.title: A polite enquiry about a price
87.gm: A polite young man from the board's staff, catalogue in hand, asks Eloise what THAT one costs, and whether there are sketches. She does not know what to say; Marit knows several things to say. Whether it is sold, withdrawn or simply turned to the wall again can depend on who is standing beside her. @clock 10–20.

87.title: Lights down in the scene dock
87.gm: Half past five: the last visitors, the lamps switched off row by row. Eloise counts the canvases as if one might have left by itself. The exhibition ENDS; the paintings stay hung until the end of term. @clock 10.

88.title: The long table is carried out
88.gm: At the Evening bell the Commons carries Mama's long table, and two more from the porches, out onto the boardwalk under strings of lamps. Guests from every dorm arrive with curfew passes and a dish or an appetite: Willas [willas] with a ham under his arm, Pippa [pippa] with a camera, Georgie [georgie] with a pie she is not allowed to carry alone. Odalys [odalys] seats people so that no dorm sits together. Rowan can carry, lay places, or bring a dish of his own. @clock 15–20.

88.title: The Harvest Table
88.gm: One dinner, served once, passed hand to hand down forty places. Late November, lamps swinging; Nurse Camille [camille], off shift for exactly one hour, eats like someone who had forgotten how. Rana [rana], Inya [inya], Livvie [livvie], {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] and Viktor [viktor] are all within reach. Tomorrow some of these people play each other for their beds, and for one hour nobody says so. @did Harvest dinner eaten. @clock 20–30 per answer.

88.title: One thing you are thankful for
88.gm: Mama raps a glass: each person says ONE thing they are thankful for, round the table, no passing. Give six or seven real answers in different voices, funny and not. When it reaches '{H}' [{H:id}] {H:he} says, after thought: 'I am thankful that the rules here are written down.' A pause, then the next person. Rowan's own turn comes — ASK the player and wait for his answer. @clock 15–20 per answer.

88.title: Pie, washing-up, passes
88.gm: Pie and coffee; Camille goes back up the path at a quarter past eight. A washing-up chain from the table to the kitchen sink. At nine the proctor pairs collect the guests dorm by dorm against their passes, and the tables go back to the porches. The evening ENDS with Mama's count of the row. @clock 15–20.

89.title: Promotion Duels, day one: check-in and deck check
89.gm: In place of today's classes for everyone playing or working (a sanctioned absence). At a table before the Trial Domes Noor [noor] ticks names against the filings and Ms Kirishima [hana] checks every deck against its registered list, card by card. The order of play for all three days is pinned up: Domes 1, 2 and 4 today and tomorrow, the Great Arena on Sunday; Dome 3 remains closed and taped. First-year Auxiliary students test microphones under Bex's [bex] eye. If Rowan filed, his duel is listed for tomorrow, 10:30, Dome 1. @clock 15–20.

89.title: Opening: the terms are read
89.gm: Classes are suspended for players, witnesses and crew; everyone else is expected in class and half of them are here anyway. Santángel [santangel] reads the terms from the steps of Dome 1: ONE duel each, binding, before two witnesses; the challenger plays for a named resident's place and the loser moves down; no deferrals; results are posted on Day 92 and take effect with the new term. Octavia [octavia] witnesses for the council. Rana [rana] is at the rail with her arms folded: she did not enter. ONE answer. @clock 10–15.

89.title: Morning session: Commons challengers
89.gm: Through both class slots (a sanctioned absence for players and crew): six duels across three domes, forty-five minutes each, cast live by nervous first-years with Ms Laurent [vivienne] correcting them off-air. Tell them in summary — a line or two each, real names — except one: at about eleven '{H}' [{H:id}] wins {H:his} in six turns and, asked to sign for the Rare Hall bed, declines: 'I have a {H:mate}.' The witness writes it down as said. Rowan watches from the gallery or works the event if he signed on. @clock 30–45 per answer.

89.title: Afternoon session
89.gm: After an hour's break for lunch, six more. The one to tell properly: Inya [inya] wins hers, cleanly, shakes hands, and declines the Rare Hall bed without giving a reason; Teobalt [teobalt], witnessing, asks her twice if she is sure. Elsewhere a second-year loses his room and takes it badly on the steps. One long answer for Inya's duel, the rest in summary. @clock 30–45 per answer.

89.title: The day's results are signed
89.gm: At half past four the domes are locked. At the table Noor reads each result back to both players and both witnesses, and all four sign the register; Hana initials every line. Nothing is posted yet. Play resumes tomorrow at half past nine. @clock 10–15.

90.title: Promotion Duels, day two: roll call and deck check
90.gm: Saturday. Roll call at nine before the domes; decks are checked again, because Hana [hana] checks again. If Rowan filed, today is his day: Noor [noor] confirms his opponent — the resident he named — his two witnesses, and Dome 1 at 10:30. People who love him are being unhelpful in different ways. @clock 15–20.

90.title: Morning session; Dome 1 at 10:30
90.gm: Six duels. IF ROWAN FILED: at 10:30 he is called into Dome 1 — formal, binding and watched, on the cast with Bex [bex] beside a first-year: start it with @duel against the named resident as the last line; winning means Rare Hall from Day 106 (by default he does not win). The scene after it, either way, belongs to whoever waited at the door. If he did not file he watches, and the session is told in summary. @clock by the play, otherwise 30–45 per answer.

90.title: Afternoon session: the defences
90.gm: The Rare Hall residents who were named defend their places; several do. A third-year who has lived on the second floor since his first week loses in the last phase and sits on in the dome after the lights are down. Gideon [gideon] watches every Commons result from the gallery and takes notes. In summary, one or two answers. @clock 30–45 per answer.

90.title: Results signed; the Arena order is posted
90.gm: Register as yesterday: read back, four signatures, Hana's initials. Santángel [santangel] pins the order for the last day: the Great Arena, doors at ten, the Rare Hall challenges for Spectral places on the main stage. @clock 10–15.

90.title: Anni's birthday: seating plan, by the clock
90.gm: Anni [anni] has scheduled it: forty-five minutes, the tower lobby, a seating plan on an easel, eight chairs. She starts on the stroke of half past six. Rowan gets a chair only if he was put on the plan (she asks people formally, days ahead) or is brought by Noor [noor] or Georgie [georgie]; otherwise he may hand something in at the desk, which she notes. @clock 10.

90.title: Presents, in order of seating
90.gm: Noor's present is a red pen with Anni's initials; Georgie's is a hand-drawn certificate, 'BEST FLOOR MONITOR', which Anni declares she will frame, and means it. Tea, one slice each. Then she mentions, as an irregularity, that a wrapped romance novel was left at her door this morning with no card — and watches the faces. Who left it is for Rowan to work out, if he cares to. She closes the party at a quarter past seven exactly. @clock 15–20.

91.title: Promotion Duels, day three: the Great Arena
91.gm: Sunday; the last day moves to the Great Arena and the whole school comes. Gani [gani] has the rig, Zeynep [zeynep] the scorer's table; Bex [bex] and Ms Laurent [vivienne] sit behind two first-year casters like driving instructors. Santángel [santangel] reads the order: four Rare Hall challenges for Spectral places, one duel at a time on the centre table. @clock 15–20.

91.title: Rare Hall against the Tower: duels one and two
91.gm: Two duels before lunch, each with its own crowd. White collars defend with their floor in the front rows; Octavia [octavia] sits with neither side. Tell each as ONE long answer with the casters' real lines and the turning point (game terms strictly by the rules in the material). One of the two challengers wins: the Tower will have a new resident, and somebody a smaller room. @clock 45–60 per duel.

91.title: Duels three and four
91.gm: After the break, the last two — the final one is the most watched game of the term so far. Whatever the result, both players get the arena's applause, which they have not had for weeks. Rana [rana] leaves before the end. One long answer per duel. @clock 45–60 per duel.

91.title: The register is closed
91.gm: On the stage Noor [noor] reads the last results back and takes the last signatures; Hana [hana] initials the page and Santángel closes the register with both hands. He says only: the new dorm lists go up at the job board tomorrow morning; moves take effect at the start of the Spring Term. The Promotion Duels END (@did Promotion Duels over). The arena is cleared before dark. @clock 10–15.

92.title: The new dorm lists go up
92.gm: Before the Morning class Octavia [octavia] and Noor [noor] pin three lists in the glass cases: Commons, Rare Hall, Spectral Tower, as they will stand next term. Who rises, who falls; collars will change after the break. Odalys [odalys] has come up the hill for it: she reads the Commons list with her lips moving and says only, 'Well. More for supper.' Rowan's own line is on the list where his result put him. @clock 10–15.

92.title: Finals study week: the Library notice
92.gm: Teobalt [teobalt] pins the second notice: finals are in four days; the Library keeps extended hours all week, to nine in the evening, and proctors walk students home in dorm groups at 20:00 and 21:00 — nobody walks alone. He has a sign-up sheet for study tables. Sessions this week count. Ends with the bell for class. @clock 10–15.

92.title: Last escort from the Library
92.gm: Nine o'clock at the Library doors: a proctor pair with lanterns, a list, students in three groups by dorm. The Commons group takes the long path down to the cove with the lantern in front. Whoever studied until now walks in it; the talk on the way is tired, kind and about nothing. @clock 15–20.

93.title: Viktor signs out for the Windbreak Campsite
93.gm: Viktor [viktor] does not celebrate. He signs the book at the gate after class and spends the afternoon at the campsite's fire ring with a map and his father's journal — today he is one year closer to the age his father was in the last photograph. He told nobody; whoever knows him knows where he is. Someone who simply turns up and sits down is tolerated, then welcome (remembering the day is worth real affection; do not sing). @clock 15–20 per answer.

93.title: Tea from a billy can
93.gm: ONLY if Rowan is there and has his trust: over tea Viktor says the name Aleksander Hale aloud for the first time, or opens the journal at the place where twelve pages were torn out and lets him look (@journal Mysteries). Without that trust he talks about tides and contour lines, and it is still a good hour. @clock 15–20 per answer.

93.title: Back before the Afternoon bell
93.gm: At five he kills the fire properly and packs up: the wild is closed after the Afternoon bell and he will not give the proctors a reason. The walk down the ridge path takes most of an hour; they sign back in at the gate before six. @clock 40–50.

94.title: Review clinic: Rules & Judging
94.gm: Seminar Room 2B, every desk taken; Noor [noor] in the front row, Georgie [georgie] with coloured pens, Teobalt [teobalt] handing round a list of past questions. Ms Kirishima [hana] works through the paper's shape: the written part, then the oral — three rulings defended for ten minutes. She puts two real questions to the room and one to Rowan. Counts as strong study for the course. Two answers. @clock 35–40 each.

94.title: Ten minutes over time
94.gm: Hana keeps the room. Without being asked she repeats, slowly and exactly, what makes a challenge formal — made aloud, by name, before one who counts — and then, twice, that nobody is ever obliged to MAKE one. She looks tired and very young. Nobody writes it down, and everybody will remember it. ONE answer with her real words. @clock 10–15.

94.title: Review clinic: Probability
94.gm: Dr Blum [blum] arrives with chalk on both cuffs and the wrong folder. Eight problems of the kind the final will set; the formula sheet is allowed and he shows how to build one. He hunts for his glasses in the middle of problem five. One problem is put to Rowan at the board. Counts as strong study for the course. The room is cleared at a quarter past five. @clock 40–45 per answer.

95.title: Midnight on the porch of Bungalow 6
95.gm: A birthday that begins at midnight, because that is when Dmitri [dmitri] is awake. It is inside the Commons' own row and the proctors' lanterns pass above it. One by one, whoever has ever drunk his tea turns up on the porch of number 6 in a blanket, with a candle in a mug: {H=sammy?'Sammy'|Sammy} [sammy] and {H=tobias?'Tobias'|Tobias} [tobias] first, then others. If Rowan ever sat up with him, a tap on the window of number 7 invites him too. Quiet voices; finals begin in the morning. @clock 10–15.

95.title: Tea for everyone who is awake
95.gm: He makes tea for every mug on a spirit burner and is not sure where to put his hands. Somebody has a present: a tin of the black tea he rations. He says it is the first birthday he has not spent alone on purpose — once, without looking up. Nobody makes anything of it. @clock 15–20.

95.title: Candles out
95.gm: At one Odalys's window lights for a moment and goes dark again: she knows, and allows it, and it is over. Mugs are rinsed at the pump; people go back to their bunks. Dmitri stays on the porch. Morning comes early: @sleep when Rowan is in bed. @clock 10.

96.title: Finals, Friday: seats and exam rules
96.gm: The lecture hall with every second seat taped off. Santángel [santangel] reads the rules for all three days: bags at the wall, no phones, a spoken word is a failed paper; cheating is an automatic F and a hearing. The exam timetable from the job board is read once more. Rowan's first: Card Design, in the Design Lab at a quarter to nine. @clock 10.

96.title: Final: Card Design Basics (submission)
96.gm: @place design_lab — across from the hall. Chuck [chuck] collects the term's work at a trestle: a five-card mini-archetype with its playtest log. Each student lays the five cards out, and he asks one question about one card — usually the right one. Rowan's is judged on what he actually built in the lab this term and on how he answers. Then waiting on the benches while the others go. One or two answers. @clock 15 for his turn; the session ends at half past ten.

96.title: Final: Table Practicum — the call list
96.gm: At the Trial Domes Coach Rox [rox] reads the call list and the draw. Each candidate plays one duel in a dome before a three-person staff panel — today Rox, Ms Kirishima [hana] and Santángel — who mark procedure and composure, not only the result. Dome 3 is taped off; nobody looks at it. Rowan is told his opponent and his time. @clock 10–15.

96.title: Final: Table Practicum (practical duel)
96.gm: Rowan's turn before the panel: play it as a scene — the walk in, three faces behind a table — then the duel itself (@duel against the drawn classmate, exam kind, as the last line). Afterwards the panel says nothing and writes a great deal. The last pair comes out at two; the day's exams END there, and the rest of Friday is for study or sleep. @clock by the play.

97.title: Finals, Saturday: Tempo & Resource — the draw
97.gm: Santángel [santangel] draws opponents from a card box, by ladder rank order, and issues the ledger sheets: both players' tempo is kept turn by turn DURING play, and the ledger is graded, not only the result. He says so once. Rowan gets his opponent, his dome and a sharpened pencil. @clock 10–15.

97.title: Final: Tempo & Resource (practical duel with ledger)
97.gm: Rowan's exam duel against the drawn classmate (@duel, exam kind, as the last line): between turns he must keep the ledger — mention it, and let Technique and his study in the course show in how clean it is. Santángel walks the domes and reads over shoulders without a sound. Ledgers are handed in at half past ten. @clock by the play.

97.title: Final: Rules & Judging — the written paper
97.gm: Seminar Room 2B, Ms Kirishima [hana] invigilating, Noor [noor] two desks away writing without pause. One hour. Give Rowan two or three of the rulings for real (strictly by the game rules in the material) and let him answer; the rest passes in a sentence. Pens down at half past twelve. @clock 60 in all.

97.title: Final: Rules & Judging — the oral
97.gm: Ten minutes each, alone with Hana across one desk: three rulings to defend against her questions. Rowan's slot comes as called; play it as a real exchange — she is exact, fair, and gives nothing away, and she does not let a right answer stand on a wrong reason. The corridor outside is the real scene for everyone waiting. @clock 10 for his turn; all orals are done by two.

97.title: Final: Physical Conditioning (circuit and mat tables)
97.gm: Coach Rox [rox] with a stopwatch: the full circuit, and then — pulse still up — a composed-play test at the mat tables. Fitness decides the first half and Nerve the second. One long answer; {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] laps half the class and apologises for it. Showers, and the Saturday exams are over by a quarter past four. @clock 60–75.

98.title: Finals, Sunday: Probability & Game Theory
98.gm: Dr Blum [blum] hands out eight problems; an open formula sheet is allowed, and he has forgotten his own. Give Rowan one problem for real and let him work it; the rest goes by Knowledge and study. The hall is silent but for Blum patting his pockets. Papers in at half past ten. @clock 90 in all.

98.title: Final: Lore & History of the Game (essay)
98.gm: Professor Ashdown [ashdown] writes the task on the board: an essay, plus a source critique of one of the Founder's tales — she has chosen the shipwreck. Two hours. Ask Rowan in one line what he argues, and let that, his Knowledge and his study decide. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee], three seats along, writes very slowly and does not stop. @clock 120 in all.

98.title: Pens down: the term's last paper
98.gm: Half past one. Ashdown collects the scripts herself, squares the pile and says: 'Thank you. That is the term.' Outside on the steps the first-years stand blinking in the daylight. Term grades are posted tomorrow morning at half past seven at the job board. The finals END (@did finals written). @clock 10.

99.title: Term grades in the glass cases
99.gm: The glass cases again, the same clerk, a quieter crowd than at midterm. Rowan's letters appear by themselves. Livvie [livvie] works out her average on her fingers; Rana [rana] reads hers once and walks off; {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] has scraped his C in Lore if anyone helped him read, and says the letter aloud as if it might change. @clock 10–15.

99.title: Probation notices; the last week
99.gm: The clerk pins a short second list: students on probation report to the Chancellor's office today at half past two. If Rowan has two F he is on it, and Teobalt [teobalt] offers to walk up with him. For everyone else the last week is light — classes are reviews — and by the bell the whole alcove is talking about Friday's Gala. @clock 10–15.

99.title: Probation hearings in the Chancellor's office
99.gm: ONLY if Rowan has two F (otherwise this passes unseen behind a closed door: say nothing). A bench in the corridor, names called one at a time. His hearing is a real scene with Chancellor Vicar [okonkwo]: his record on the desk, what probation means next term, and one direct question about what he intends to do. She is hard and not unkind. @clock 20–30.

100.title: Shuttle to town for the fittings
100.gm: After class the school cart leaves the main gate for town at a quarter past two, and again on the half hours; sign out with the proctor at the gate. On the bench: who has asked whom to the Gala is the only topic on the island — louder than usual, to drown out this morning's news. Rowan can ride down with whoever he likes, or be asked on the way. @clock 20.

100.title: Maison Topdeck: fittings and hire
100.gm: @place boutique. The narrow shop is full to the door: formal dress is required on Friday. Hire from 30 cr, to be paid now; the cheap routes are Marit's [marit] costume rail at the theatre or {H=baylee?'Baylee's'|Baylee's} cousin's suit. Inya [inya] and Pippa [pippa] are behind the curtain giving each other marks out of ten. Let Rowan choose, try on and pay (or walk out); what he will wear is noted (@journal Plans). @clock 15–20 per answer.

100.title: Jessica holds court
100.gm: Jessica [jessica] has the armchair by the long mirror as the shop's unpaid consultant, with Ashton [ashton] holding her bag. Her verdicts are quick, and right. She will DRESS someone she has decided to take an interest in — choose, pin, and tell the tailor what to charge — if his pride allows it; refusing gracefully is also an answer she respects. @clock 15–20 per answer.

100.title: Last cart up the hill
100.gm: The shop turns its sign at twenty past five. The last cart leaves Main Street at half past; everyone signed out must be through the gate by six. Boxes on knees all the way up. @place main_gate on arrival. @clock 30.

100.title: Octavia's birthday: she works through it
100.gm: At the far end of the tower terrace Octavia [octavia] has a table, a lamp and the council's Gala file. The council has left a card, signed by all four. A porter brings orchids from Mr Marrow and, with them, a letter: the offer of a position after graduation, in writing. She reads it once and puts it under the file. The terrace is for residents and guests; someone with council business, or a coffee, is let up. @clock 10–15.

100.title: A late coffee on the terrace
100.gm: A person who brings her nothing but a coffee and ONE honest question finds her, for ten minutes, almost unguarded: about the offer, the empty chairs she has to seat on Friday, or what she actually wants. Flattery or a second question closes it again. She is back at the file by a quarter past eight; residents' lift only after nine. @clock 10–20.

101.title: Crash course: partners by lot
101.gm: On the theatre stage, forty people in socks. Ms Laurent [vivienne] claps once for silence; Marit [marit] holds two hats. Partners are drawn by lot — Rowan's is whoever the GM judges most interesting for him today, not necessarily who he hoped for. {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny], Noor [noor], Inya [inya] and {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] are all in the draw. @clock 10.

101.title: The box step
101.gm: Vivienne counts, Marit demonstrates with a broom: frame, box step, the turn. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} is terrified of treading on someone and turns out to be light on his feet; Noor counts aloud until asked not to. Rowan's Fitness and Charm show in how it goes — let him talk with his partner while they get it wrong. Two answers. @clock 20 each.

101.title: Change partners: by choice
101.gm: After five minutes for water, Vivienne: 'Now ask someone.' Rowan may ask whom he likes, or be asked. A whole waltz with the gramophone. A dance learned here is a dance he can ask for on Friday — note with whom (@journal Plans). @clock 15–20 per answer.

101.title: The last waltz and a bow
101.gm: One last waltz right through without stopping, then the bow and curtsey, which Marit drills three times. Vivienne's verdict on the class: 'You will not disgrace me. Most of you.' The stage is cleared by five. @did waltz learned. @clock 10–15.

102.title: Wildcard Swap: names drawn from the stockpot at breakfast
102.gm: At breakfast Odalys [odalys] carries the big stockpot round the table: everybody on the row draws ONE folded name and shows it to nobody. Limit 15 credits; gifts on the table tonight at half past six, wrapped, unsigned. Tell Rowan whose name he drew (choose someone that makes it interesting) — he has the day, after class, to find something. @journal Plans. @clock 10.

102.title: The Wildcard Swap: supper first
102.gm: One supper, served once, with a heap of badly wrapped parcels down the middle of the table that nobody is allowed to touch. Guessing has started already. Viktor [viktor] has wrapped his in a chart. @clock 15–20.

102.title: Gifts, one at a time
102.gm: Mama calls the names in bungalow order and each parcel is opened in front of everyone: small, silly, or painfully well judged. '{H}' [{H:id}] has given {H:his} draw the single most useful object they could have wanted, wrapped with geometric precision — and is puzzled by thanks: 'You needed it. I had observed that.' What ROWAN gives, and to whom, is opened here and counts; so does what he gets (Inya [inya], Livvie [livvie], {H=baylee?{O} [{O:id}]|Baylee [baylee]} and Rana [rana] all react). Two or three answers. @clock 15–20 each.

102.title: Who gave what
102.gm: The last part of the tradition: one guess each at who gave it; right guesses earn washing-up duty for the giver. Paper is burned in the range. Head count at nine. @did Wildcard Swap done. @clock 15–20.

103.title: The Winter Gala: arrivals
103.gm: @place gala_ballroom. Formal dress; the curfew is lifted inside the hall, with staff at every door. Tavita [tavita] has the door and the list, Pilar [pilar] the running order in her glove — it is her production. WHO ROWAN ARRIVES WITH is seen by everyone on the staircase (second romance checkpoint: note it). Mirrors, three chandeliers, a string quartet tuning. Octavia's [octavia] seating plan stands on an easel, and it is politics. @clock 15–20.

103.title: The Chancellor's toast
103.gm: Everyone standing at their places. Among the round tables stand chairs with name cards and nobody in them, for those in the wards. Chancellor Vicar [okonkwo] speaks for two minutes and raises her glass 'to those who cannot be with us'; it is brittle, and the room answers too quietly. Marrow [marrow] at the top table drinks to it pleasantly. ONE answer with her real words. @clock 10.

103.title: Dinner at Octavia's tables
103.gm: Three courses, served once. Put Rowan at a table of eight chosen by the plan (not by him): two people he likes, one he does not, one stranger — and perhaps an empty chair. Talk across the cloth; Imara [imara] is counting covers for tomorrow's books, Sebastian [sebastian] is at Marrow's elbow. @did Gala dinner eaten. @clock 20–30 per answer.

103.title: The first dance
103.gm: The quartet stands; Pilar gives the sign. Jessica [jessica] opens the floor with her first dance. Lilia [lilia] and Willas [willas] dance like people who have done it for years, and the team pretends not to stare. Whoever Rowan asks FIRST, or is asked by, is the thing people will remember (a dance learned on Wednesday can be asked for now). @clock 10–15.

103.title: Dancing
103.gm: The long middle of the evening: whom he dances with and is seen with — Jessica, Marit [marit], Inya [inya], Livvie [livvie], Noor [noor], {H=sunny?{O} [{O:id}]|Sunny [sunny]}, Rana [rana], Pippa [pippa] with her camera, Bex [bex]; Ms Kirishima [hana] and Nurse Camille [camille] at the staff end; Chuck [chuck] dancing badly and gladly. The Guest [{H:id}] watches the floor for four minutes and then dances every dance, flawlessly, with anyone who asks; its partners' hands are cold afterwards. @clock 15–25 per answer.

103.title: Ten o'clock: the terrace doors are opened
103.gm: Georgie [georgie] is taken home at ten, protesting. The doors to the terrace are opened for air: cold, stars, the sea below, staff at the balustrade ends. It is the place for the conversation that cannot be had on the floor — and the last good chance before the break to expose the false {H}, if Rowan has what it takes and does it publicly (then as in the calendar entry and the plot). Gideon [gideon] and Ashton [ashton] hold a corner of it. @clock 15–20 per answer.

103.title: The last dance at midnight
103.gm: Pilar announces it at a quarter to twelve: the last dance. Whoever Rowan stands up with now is the answer to the evening. The quartet plays it slowly; the clock tower strikes twelve through the open terrace doors on the final bars. ONE answer, and it is his. @clock 15.

103.title: Carriages: escorted home by dorm
103.gm: Lights up. Tavita reads the dorms out and proctor pairs with lanterns walk each group home — the Commons down the long path to the cove, shoes in hand. Pilar is the last out of the hall. The Gala ENDS (@did Winter Gala over); the curfew is back in force from the door. @clock 20–30.

104.title: End-of-term bonfire: Mama lights the pit
104.gm: With the wardens' permission, and only until the end of the evening. Odalys [odalys] insists on lighting the pit herself, whatever was found beside it on Monday morning: she stands over the kindling a moment before she strikes the match. The whole row on the logs; Saoirse [saoirse], Marit [marit] and {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] come down with passes. Those who were promoted will come back with other collars. @clock 10–15.

104.title: Burn your worst decklist
104.gm: The ceremony: one at a time people stand up, read out their worst decklist of the term — or its worst three cards — to general abuse, and put it on the fire. Rana's [rana] is short. {H=baylee?'Baylee's'|Baylee's} [baylee] is long and he is proud of it. Rowan's turn comes: ASK the player which list or card he burns and what he says. @clock 15–20 per answer.

104.title: Promises for next term
104.gm: The fire burns down and the talk gets quieter: promises for next term, made aloud across the pit — Inya [inya], Livvie [livvie], Viktor [viktor], and whoever sits beside Rowan. REMEMBER every promise made to or by him (@journal Plans, one line each). The fire has a green edge on the side where {H} sits, if {H:he} still sits there; people have left a gap on that log. @clock 15–25 per answer.

104.title: Embers and the head count
104.gm: Sand on the embers at a quarter past nine; guests walked up by the proctor pair. Mama counts the row on the boardwalk — the last count of the term — and is a long time saying goodnight. The last ferry of the term leaves tomorrow at noon. @clock 10–15.

105.title: Bags down the avenue; boarding begins
105.gm: From mid-morning (boarding from half past ten) the avenue is a procession of trunks and handcarts. The Second Chance lies at the Academy pier with Captain Stroud [abel] checking names at the gangway; Mr Grieve [silas] works the luggage sling. Some stay on the island: Livvie [livvie] cannot afford the fare, Viktor [viktor] will not leave, and Wren did not notice it was a holiday. Rowan's last errands and goodbyes on the hill belong here. @clock 15–20 per answer.

105.title: Goodbyes at the gangway
105.gm: @place ferry_dock. Odalys [odalys] has come down with a paper bag of food for every one of hers and presses one on Rowan. Inya [inya] and {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] are at the rail or on the planks according to how things stand. Whoever stands at the rail with him as the lines come in is decided by his routes: give that person the last real exchange of the term. @clock 15–20 per answer.

105.title: Noon: the Second Chance casts off
105.gm: The horn; the island turning slowly behind the stern, the clock tower last. On the pier Mama, Livvie and Silas grow small; nobody at the rail says anything clever. Rowan only watches: ONE answer, ending when the harbour mole hides the pier. @clock 10.

105.title: The winter break (one interlude)
105.gm: As in the calendar entry: ONE interlude scene for the whole break — Aunt Dee's laundromat in the rain, a letter or two, one thing that does not fit — told in a single long answer, and then straight on to Day 106. Nothing else is played out from the break. If the false {H} was exposed, what happens to Gideon happens now, off stage, and is not shown. @clock 0, then the game moves on to Day 106.

106.title: The first ferry of the Spring Term
106.gm: The Second Chance brings the school back at half past seven: fewer students than it took away.
