On the pier, waiting for Rowan's ferry, stands the Guest — {H} [{H:id}], gentle as ever, or, if {H:he} was exposed, Gideon Pryce [gideon] in white gloves, very polite and very still — and carries his bag up the avenue. Play the one that applies. @place ferry_dock. @clock 20–30.

106.title: Opening assembly in the Great Arena
106.gm: The whole school in the lower stands; empty rows show. Chancellor Vicar [okonkwo] is shorter and harder than in September: the curfew stays; Ward B is 'stable'; the Interschool Cup WILL be hosted in March. Santángel [santangel], Coach Rox [rox], Lilia [lilia] with the team and Octavia [octavia] with the council sit behind her. Marrow, who has wintered on the island, is in the box. Rowan only listens: ONE long answer with her real words. @clock 20–30.

106.title: Notices; then classes as normal
106.gm: Santángel reads the notices: Ladder Season 2 opens on Friday; new keys and collars this afternoon from two on the Quad; timetables unchanged. Then: 'To your classes.' The Morning class starts late and runs short today. On the way out — if {H} was exposed — nobody says {H:his} name, and people take the other stairs from Gideon. @clock 10–15.

106.title: Moving Day: the key table opens
106.gm: The council table on the Quad at two: Teobalt [teobalt] with the lists from Day 92, new room keys in envelopes; new collars are issued at the campus store against the key slip. If Rowan won his Promotion Duel his envelope says Rare Hall — he may take it, or petition on the spot to stay in the Commons (Odalys [odalys], who happens to be standing there, pretends not to care which). @clock 10–15.

106.title: Trunks on carts
106.gm: All afternoon carts cross the Quad both ways and collars change colour. Willas [willas] carries half the Commons' boxes personally and swears at every stair. Rana [rana] watches other people's trunks go up the hill. Rowan either moves (three answers: packing, the way, the new room and who is in it) or helps others move, which is its own scene. @clock 20–30 per answer.

106.title: The row counts its faces
106.gm: By a quarter to five the last cart is through. On the Commons boardwalk there are new faces in the doorways and one or two fewer old ones; Inya [inya] and {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] sort out who sleeps where now. Odalys reads the new row list aloud once, start to finish, and sets the table for the number on it. @clock 15–20.

107.title: Spring sign-ups: the stalls open
107.gm: A smaller, tighter fair than September's: fewer stalls, more purpose. Pilar [pilar] runs it from the fountain with a running order and a hand bell; Imara [imara] sits beside her with the pay sheet. The crew lists for the Island Open and the Interschool Cup hang at their table. @clock 10.

107.title: Pitches, three minutes each
107.gm: Each club and elective gets three minutes on the fountain steps and Pilar's bell: Marit [marit] for the theatre, Noor [noor] for the Judge Circle, {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] for the swim squad, Wren [wren] for the lab hours, Bex [bex] recruiting 'anyone who can climb a hill and hold a cable'. Teobalt [teobalt] reads the volunteer rotas. Tell them in two answers, with real lines. @clock 25–30 each.

107.title: Sheets and rotas
107.gm: Free scene among the tables: a second chance to join whatever Rowan missed in September (write what he signs: @journal Plans). New this term: the volunteer rotas for the Open and the Cup, paid through Imara's sheet, and a plain list in Nurse Camille's handwriting — infirmary helpers — with four names on it and room for more. @clock 10–20 per answer.

107.title: The bell: lists close
107.gm: Pilar rings the hand bell at five; sheets are collected, counted and handed to Imara, who reads the totals for the minute. Stalls are folded and off the Quad well before dark; Rowan gets the carbon copy of anything he signed. @clock 10.

108.title: Jun-ho's birthday, to specification
108.gm: Jun-ho [junho] has issued a written specification for his own party: duration forty-five minutes, noise ceiling stated, cake density stated. His roommate Teobalt [teobalt] has followed it to the letter except in one particular, which is that it is a surprise: fifteen people behind the lab benches at three o'clock precisely. Rowan may be one of them. @clock 5–10.

108.title: A bug report, closed
108.gm: Cake of the specified density. Jun-ho files a bug report against the surprise aloud, in numbered points — and then, quietly, closes it as 'works as intended'. A small present or simply having remembered is worth real affection; he logs it. The party ends at a quarter to four, as specified. @clock 15–20.

108.title: The Top Deck returns: studio audience in
108.gm: Now live in the late afternoon, under the curfew. A dozen students on the bench behind the glass; Pippa [pippa] on camera two, Ms Laurent [vivienne] in the gallery with the approved script and a pencil. Bex [bex] does the warm-up herself. The ON AIR lamp is tested twice. @clock 10–15.

108.title: 'The Top Deck', live at five
108.gm: A vetted show: results, Season 2 and Island Open previews, an interview with Marit [marit] about the spring play — and no mention of Ward B. Rowan watches from the bench (or from any screen on campus): ONE long answer with real lines from the desk. At the end Bex signs off with one line that was not in the approved script; Vivienne's pencil stops. @clock 40.

108.title: Off air
108.gm: The lamp goes dark. Vivienne says nothing, which is worse. In the tape room behind the set Bex and Pippa have a box of tapes and photographs that do not add up, and they are choosing whom to show it to: someone they both trust may be asked to stay behind for five minutes. The studio is locked at six. @clock 10–15.

109.title: Season 2 registration: the clerk's desk
109.gm: Before the Thursday session: Noor [noor] at the desk by the council chamber door with the register and the set files; Sebastian [sebastian] at the next desk with the stamp for late forms and penalties. Register or update a decklist before Friday's opening — one list per player, signed. Octavia [octavia] looks in once. @clock 10.

109.title: Decklists handed in
109.gm: Routine: a queue, lists checked against the set files, a stamp. If Rowan registers or changes his deck, do it properly (the list as he actually plays it). What is not routine: Noor now reads EVERY registered list for cards she cannot find in any set file. There is one such list. She has not decided what the rules require her to do about it — and asking Rowan, quietly, away from the next desk, is not beneath her. Sebastian has not been told what she is looking for. @clock by what he does.

109.title: The register is closed for the season opening
109.gm: Half past five: last lists; Teobalt [teobalt] runs in with three from the Commons. Noor rules the line and locks the register in the cabinet herself, which she did not do in September. Season 2 opens on the Quad tomorrow at a quarter to eight. @clock 10.

110.title: Ladder Season 2: the board is reset
110.gm: Before the Morning class Santángel [santangel] unlocks the big board on the Quad and turns the season counter: season points to zero, ranks as they stood. Top 8 at the March snapshot qualify for the Interschool Cup side event. The top of the ladder is now Battle Team names — Lilia [lilia], Dom [dom], Saoirse [saoirse] — and one other. Rowan's rank is read off the board. @clock 10.

110.title: The first challenge slips
110.gm: Zeynep [zeynep] opens the registrar's box and the first slips of the season go in. Kenji [kenji] has put in four before the bell; Priya [priya] reads the board for a long time. The Guest ({H} [{H:id}], or Gideon in white gloves) stands looking at the top names with its head on one side: it has learned the word 'champion'. Ends with the bell for class. @clock 10–15.

110.title: Opening afternoon at the Trial Domes
110.gm: The first ranked games of the season, domes booked back to back until five. If Rowan wants a ranked game today he gets one (@duel ladder as the last line). In the next days — not necessarily today — the first of the Guest's formal approaches to a team member is made: correctly worded, witnessed, with an ante it finds reasonable; Kenji, who cannot refuse a game, is the likeliest first. Today it only watches him play. @clock by the play.

111.title: Sign-out at the gate; lanterns down the avenue
111.gm: The proctor at the main gate signs students out in a book from the Evening bell: back by the end of the evening, no exceptions. Groups walk down with lanterns, breath smoking. Josie [josie] has sent word there is mulled apple. @clock 25 for the way down.

111.title: Winter Night Market: chestnuts and lanterns
111.gm: @place night_market. Hot chestnuts, mulled apple, a lantern stall where one paints one's own. Mika [mika] and Dex [dex] have a table of singles and the Island Open poster; Selene [selene] sells bath salts. The pawnbroker's stall has his covered cabinet with him — standing OPEN and empty tonight, whoever bought what was in it; he will not say. Free scene; one snack eaten once. @clock 10–20 per answer.

111.title: Last call for the hill
111.gm: A quarter past nine: a proctor walks the yard with a lantern calling the Academy in. The walk up takes half an hour and the gate book closes at ten. Whoever leaves now is safe. Whoever stays has decided to — say plainly that it is a curfew breach — and that is where the good scenes are. @clock 30 for the way up.

111.title: After the bell: the tent at the far end
111.gm: ONLY if Rowan stayed past the bell: Madame Oru's [oru] lanterns are lit only now. She does not read; she says: 'What cannot be fought can be bound. Ask the one who knows the rules by heart.' And nothing further. Getting home is then a matter of the unlit paths, luck and Nerve (see CURFEW). @clock 15–20.

113.title: Island Open: the list opens
113.gm: At the Sleeve & Binder Dex [dex] pins the poster — the Island Open, Days 124–126, sanctioned, prizes 6,000 / 3,000 / 1,500 cr — and Mika [mika] opens a ledger on the counter and reads the terms: sign up here or at the campus store by Day 123; the ladder top 8 enter directly; everyone else plays the qualifier here on the evening of Day 123. Mainland players will come over on the ferry. @clock 10–15.

113.title: The first names in the book
113.gm: Rana [rana] signs first, in block capitals: it is her last chance to win a sanctioned event and not be sent down for good, and everyone in the shop knows it and looks at the singles case. Livvie [livvie] signs after reading the prize line three times. Inya [inya] signs with a doodle. Rowan may sign today or any day until Day 123 (@journal Plans); town is by sign-out, back before the Evening bell ends. @clock by what he does.

113.title: Midwinter in the kitchen: candles down the table
113.gm: ONLY if someone helped {H=freya?'Freya'|Freya} [freya] find a curfew-legal way (then there was a notice on the board). If nobody did, there is NO supper here: skip all Midwinter points — the party is at the cove after dark, with everything that means under curfew. Otherwise: Bungalow 1 by candlelight, every candle the row owns down the long table; {H=freya?'Freya'|Freya} in a paper crown of candles she is not allowed to light; Rafa [rafa] and Trixie [trixie] carrying dishes. @clock 10–15.

113.title: Midwinter supper
113.gm: (Only if the legal supper takes place.) One supper, served once: Rafa's fish, Trixie's honey cake, saffron buns from a recipe {H=freya?'Freya'|Freya} dictated from memory. Dmitri [dmitri] has come out of his room for it; {H=tobias?'Tobias'|Tobias} [tobias] is on his best behaviour, which is visible as an effort. Odalys [odalys] sits at the head and misses nothing. @clock 15–20 per answer.

113.title: The northern song; one bottle
113.gm: (Only if the legal supper takes place.) {H=freya?'Freya'|Freya} stands on her chair and starts the northern song again; by the second verse the table has the chorus. Then the ONE bottle, which Mama measures out herself, a thimble each, and corks. {H=freya?'Freya'|Freya} makes no speech and looks at whoever helped her. Candles are pinched out at nine for the head count. @did Midwinter supper held. @clock 15–20 per answer.

114.title: Island Open registration (day 2 of 11)
114.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. The ledger lies open on the counter of the Sleeve & Binder every afternoon until half past five (a second sheet hangs at the campus store). Today the talk at the counter is who is already in the book, and whether the ladder top 8 really enter directly. If Rowan comes to sign, Mika [mika] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

114.title: Noor's birthday: a present from the Judge Circle
114.gm: After its afternoon meeting in Seminar Room 2B the Judge Circle keeps Noor [noor] back: Ms Kirishima [hana] hands her an annotated first-edition rulebook, signed by the whole Circle on the flyleaf. Noor is quietly pleased, and turns to the charter chapter before she has finished saying thank you. Rowan is there if he is in the Circle, or looks in because he remembered. @clock 10–15.

114.title: Tea, and a question about the charter
114.gm: Tea from a flask, a tin of dates. Under the pleasure she is troubled: she is the charter clerk, and she knows more about the register than she has told anyone. Someone who asks her TODAY what the charter says about winning back what was lost gets a long, exact and hopeful answer, with chapter and clause (@journal Mysteries). Asked anything about the wards she closes the book. The room is cleared at five. @clock 15–20 per answer.

114.title: Island Open: the day's count
114.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Mika [mika] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. Six names so far, four of them from the Commons. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

115.title: Island Open registration (day 3 of 11)
115.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open on the counter of the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. Dex [dex] has started a chalk tally of entries on the door frame. If Rowan comes to sign, Mika [mika] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans); otherwise mention it only if he is in the shop. @clock by what he does.

115.title: Island Open: the day's count
115.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Dex [dex] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. Dex adds a chalk stroke to the door frame for every entry and loses count at eleven. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

116.title: Island Open registration (day 4 of 11)
116.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. A letter has come from the mainland asking for six places and somewhere to sleep; Mika [mika] is doing sums about beds at the inn. If Rowan comes to sign, she takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

116.title: Victoria's tea party: guests received at the stair door
116.gm: Guests climb the unmarked stair from the library's top gallery from a quarter to four; nobody is early by more than that, because the schedule card said so. Ophelia [ophelia] stands at the stair door like a sentry and thanks each guest, stiffly and by name, for coming. Victoria [victoria] is already seated under her parasol and does not get up. Rowan may hand over a present here or keep it for the table. Ends when the tower clock strikes four. @clock 15.

116.title: Tea at exactly four
116.gm: At the stroke of four Victoria pours; whoever comes in after the stroke is noted aloud. A proper tea: one pot, small cakes, the campus spread out below. She opens the presents one by one and judges each on its looks in a sentence, kindly and without mercy. This is the free part: Rowan can talk to her, to Ophelia or to the other guests. Tea is poured ONCE; when the pot is empty the table is finished (@did tea drunk). @clock 40.

116.title: The prettiest present; the garden cleared before dusk
116.gm: Victoria stands, taps her cup and tells the whole table which present is the prettiest and why; the giver gets a curtsey, and everyone else is told theirs was 'also very nice'. Then she declares the party over, as announced, because she does not like things that trail off. Ophelia collects the cups and sees every guest to the stair. Play it in ONE answer; it ENDS with the stair door closed behind the last guest. @clock 20.

116.title: Island Open: the day's count
116.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Mika [mika] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. The mainland six are entered in pencil until their fee arrives. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

117.title: Island Open registration (day 5 of 11)
117.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. It is Friday and the weather is turning; Dex [dex] is taking the poster in from the window between gusts. If Rowan comes to sign, Mika [mika] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

117.title: Island Open: the day's count
117.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Dex [dex] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. Counted early today: the wind is getting up and the shutters go on before the Friday draft. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

117.title: Harbourmaster's warning: Friday Night Draft breaks off
117.gm: The gale arrives in the middle of the last round at the Sleeve & Binder: shutters bang, the lamps dip, the harbourmaster's boy comes in soaked to say the avenue is closed by a fallen tree and nobody walks up tonight. Dex [dex] calls the draft where it stands, splits the prizes and bolts the shutters; Mika [mika] counts the students present and writes the names down for the gate. Everyone is sent across the street to the inn in one group, coats over their heads. Curfew is nobody's fault tonight, and the adults say so. Ends at the inn door. @clock 30.

117.title: Stranded at the Drowned Anchor: blankets, soup, a list of names
117.gm: @place inn. The dining room fills with students, fishermen and two commercial travellers. The landlord hands out blankets and soup; Mika's list of names goes on the bar so that the school can be told when the line works (it crackles and dies twice). Captain Stroud [abel] comes in from doubling the ferry's lines and says the Saturday boat will not sail. Free scene: Rowan can find a corner, help carry, talk to whoever is stranded with him. It ends when the electric light goes out for good and the candles come out. @clock 60.

117.title: By the fire with the lamps out
117.gm: The heart of the night. Josie [josie] has shut the Mulligan and come across with two bottles; she pours for the adults and listens. With the students half asleep on the benches the townspeople talk about the school in a way students never hear: about a fourth house, about a professor, about children who were 'played'. Nobody explains; they break off when they notice who is awake. Rowan may listen (a reads check to catch a name), ask ONE question before the room closes up, or sleep. Give clues only from CLUES POSSIBLE HERE. Ends when Josie banks the fire. @clock 90.

117.title: Bedding down at the inn
117.gm: A sound like a rifle shot carries down from the north ridge over the wind: one of the radio mast's guy cables has gone, and Silas [silas], who sat the storm out by the door, says so, puts on his coat and is talked out of leaving before daylight. He will need a hand with it on Sunday (he does not ask; he mentions it). Students bed down on benches and floor, two to a blanket. Play it in ONE answer and end with sleep (@sleep) unless Rowan insists on staying awake. Whatever happened on campus tonight is NOT known here. @clock 30.

118.title: The walk back up the avenue; names checked at the gate
118.gm: For whoever was stranded in town: the tree is sawn through by eight and the group walks up through torn palm fronds, Dex's boy carrying the list. At the main gate a proctor ticks every name; nobody is written up. If, by the plot timeline, something was found in the Trial Domes this morning, this is where the walkers hear of it, from people who are not sure what they saw: stage that only from the plot file, never invent it. If Rowan slept on campus he sees the group come in. Ends in the Quad. @clock 60.

118.title: Harbour notice: no Saturday ferry
118.gm: The slate outside the harbour office reads NO SAILING and the Second Chance lies under doubled lines with her gangway in; Captain Stroud [abel] says Wednesday, perhaps. Mail, supplies and anyone who meant to leave today wait with it. On campus the news comes with the midday bell. Seen in passing only: one or two lines, no scene of its own unless Rowan is at the harbour. @clock 10.

118.title: Island Open registration (day 6 of 11)
118.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. Halfway: Mika [mika] reads the count to anyone who asks, and who has NOT yet signed is becoming a subject. If Rowan comes to sign, she takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

118.title: Island Open: the day's count
118.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Mika [mika] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. Past twenty. Somebody has drawn a small shark beside one name and Mika rubs it out without comment. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

118.title: Second night of the gale: shutters barred, the wind dropping
118.gm: The wardens bar the storm shutters on every dorm and count heads early; the wind is still loud at ten and audibly dropping by midnight. From the row one can see that the red lamp on the radio mast is dark. Silas [silas] has left word that he goes up to the cable on Sunday morning and can use two steady hands (a way into q_radio_tower if it is open). One answer; it ENDS with lights out. @clock 20.

119.title: Ed's birthday: muster on the bungalow steps
119.gm: IF ED IS IN ONE PIECE: he stands on the steps with a map that has a fresh red cross on it and asks who is coming. Viktor [viktor] hands him a proper climbing harness without a word and checks the buckles himself. Whoever comes brings a rope: that is the present. IF HE IS IN THE INFIRMARY or was lately: no outing; the row carries a card up and signs his cast or sling instead (@place infirmary), Viktor leaves the harness on the bed, and the next two points are skipped. Ends when the party sets off. @clock 20.

119.title: Island Open registration (day 7 of 11)
119.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. Sunday: town is quiet and the shop half empty; Dex [dex] is sorting prize cards into three unequal piles. If Rowan comes to sign, Mika [mika] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

119.title: The place with the red cross
119.gm: Only if {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} [ed] is fit. He chooses the spot: somewhere within an hour of the Commons that the staff map marks with a red cross. Play the outing in two or three answers: the walk, the one moment where it would have gone wrong without the rope (Rowan on the line: a fitness or nerve check decides how gracefully), {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} delighted by the view from the wrong side of a railing, a tin of biscuits at the top. Nobody is hurt if he is roped. They TURN BACK at half past four: the wild is closed after the Afternoon bell. @clock by the stations.

119.title: Island Open: the day's count
119.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Dex [dex] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. A quiet Sunday count; the campus-store sheet has more names on it than the shop's. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

119.title: Back on the row before the bell
119.gm: The party comes down the path scratched and loud, in time for the Afternoon bell. {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} tells the story to the row twice, larger each time; Viktor coils the rope and says the harness is to be worn, not owned. Mama's supper follows at the usual hour and is not part of this. One answer; it ENDS with the rope hung on the porch nail (@did {H=ed?'Ed's'|Ed's} birthday outing finished). @clock 15.

120.title: Island Open registration (day 8 of 11)
120.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. Decklists for the Open may be handed in sealed from today; Mika [mika] has a shoebox for them and a look for anyone who asks to see inside. If Rowan comes to sign, she takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

120.title: Island Open: the day's count
120.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Mika [mika] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. The sealed decklists in the shoebox are counted too, and do not match the names by one. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

121.title: Island Open registration (day 9 of 11)
121.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. Three days left: the entry levy for travel and lodging is due with the signature, and not everyone has it. If Rowan comes to sign, Mika [mika] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

121.title: Felix's birthday: the wall of portraits
121.gm: After the day's classes the design lab pins up its present: a whole wall of portraits of Felix [felix] drawn by everyone who could be made to, all of them terrible, each signed. Wren [wren] pins the last one without comment. Felix walks along the wall and reviews them like a gallery opening. If Rowan drew one (or does now, on the spot) it goes up too. Ends when the cake is carried in. @clock 25.

121.title: Cake among the cutting mats
121.gm: Cake on a drafting table, plates of scrap card. A vote on the worst portrait; the winner is framed with tape. Free scene with the lab regulars. The cake is eaten ONCE (@did cake eaten); when the plates are stacked, people go back to their own benches. @clock 30.

121.title: Felix lays out his sketches
121.gm: His present to himself: he finishes the sequence of dream sketches and lays them on the long table in order. They show a hall of tiled walls and a round bright thing sitting down at a table. He looks at them for a while and asks whoever is nearest, lightly, whether they have had that one too. Let Rowan answer for himself; others in the room go quiet a moment too long. No explanation is offered. It ENDS when Felix stacks the sheets and puts them in his portfolio. @clock 20.

121.title: Island Open: the day's count
121.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Mika [mika] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. Rana's name is still first. The window of the pawn shop across the street is being rearranged. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

122.title: Island Open registration (day 10 of 11)
122.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. Ledger open at the Sleeve & Binder until half past five, second sheet at the campus store. Last full day: he reminds everyone at the counter that tomorrow the book closes at five and that the qualifier is played here tomorrow evening. If Rowan comes to sign, Dex [dex] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

122.title: Volunteer sign-on with Pilar
122.gm: Seminar Room 2B after the Midday class. Pilar [pilar] has three lists on the front desk: floor judges (rules grade B or Judge Circle), scorekeepers, runners. Everyone signs for the days they can work; 20 cr a day and a meal ticket. Noor [noor] signs as scorekeeper before the ink is dry; Mika [mika] is down as a floor judge for the town. Rowan decides here whether he works the Open or plays it: a player cannot judge. Ends when Ms Kirishima closes the door. @clock 15.

122.title: Head judge's briefing: rounds, penalties, reporting
122.gm: Hana [hana], head judge, at the board: fifty-minute rounds, how a result slip is filled in and who carries it, when the clock stops, the three penalties and who may give them, how to call for the head judge. Then, in the same even voice: any challenge 'outside tournament play' made on the venue floor is to be reported to her AT ONCE, by anyone, whoever makes it. Nobody asks why. It is the only official acknowledgement so far of what everyone fears. Rowan listens; one question from him is possible. One long answer. @clock 40.

122.title: Postings and pay
122.gm: Pilar reads the postings by day and table block; swaps are allowed until she has left the room. Imara [imara] explains the pay: 20 cr for each day worked, counted out at the council table at the end of that day, signature against the list, no advances. If Rowan volunteered he gets a posting now (@plan for Day 124, Morning, great_arena) and a lanyard. Ends with the lists pinned up at the job board. @clock 20.

122.title: Walk-through of the venue
122.gm: Volunteers only: Hana walks the crew through the arena floor and the terraces, table numbers taped down, the pairings board, the scorer's table, the judges' corner. Each floor judge makes one practice ruling on a staged board. Rowan, if he is on the crew, gets a small task and a first word from Hana on how he carried it out. Ends at about twenty past four; the rest of the afternoon is free. @clock 30.

122.title: Island Open: the day's count
122.gm: Background only — do NOT move the scene for it. A quarter past five: Dex [dex] brings the two sheets together — the shop's ledger and the one from the campus store — and reads out the running count of entries for the Open to whoever is in the shop. Dex does today's count alone — Mika is up at the Academy for the judges' briefing — and gets it right on the second try. The book goes under the counter at half past five. Mention it only if Rowan is there or asks someone who was. @clock 5.

123.title: Island Open registration: last day
123.gm: The last afternoon: a queue at the counter of the Sleeve & Binder for once, and the campus-store sheet is carried down at four. Rana [rana] checks that her name is still in the book. If Rowan has not signed and wants to play, it is now: Mika [mika] takes his name and deck registration (@journal Plans). @clock by what he does.

123.title: The book is closed
123.gm: Twenty to five: Mika calls last names; at five Dex [dex] rules a line under the last entry, counts aloud and chalks the number on the door frame. The ladder top 8 are marked with a star; everyone else in the book plays the qualifier here this evening. Registration for the Island Open is CLOSED. @clock 10–15.

123.title: Qualifier: registration and deck check
123.gm: The Sleeve & Binder, tables pushed into two rows. Dex [dex] takes the names, Mika [mika] checks every deck against its list; sixteen seats, single elimination, one game a round, thirty minutes on the clock. The two proctors lent by Ms Kirishima sit by the door with the sign-out sheet. Rana [rana] is here early and says nothing to anyone. Rowan enters only if he is outside the ladder top 8 and not registered already; otherwise he watches. Ends when Dex chalks the bracket on the board. @clock 20.

123.title: Qualifier: round of sixteen
123.gm: Eight tables at once. If Rowan plays, his table is a tournament duel against a drawn opponent from the list of those present (a townsman, or a first-year he knows); otherwise show two tables in passing. Rana wins hers ahead on tempo and nearly lets it go at the end. Losers are out and may stay to watch. Ends with Dex wiping eight names off the board. @clock 35.

123.title: Qualifier: quarter-finals
123.gm: Four tables. Rowan's second game if he is still in. Rana's quarter-final is the first real test of whether she has learned to close: at match point she either takes the line Rowan has taught her (if he did) or hesitates; go by her quest state, by default she wins this one narrowly and looks ill afterwards. Ends with four names left. @clock 35.

123.title: Qualifier: semi-finals — the four left are through
123.gm: Dex announces that all four semi-finalists have a seat in tomorrow's Open; from here it is played for seeding and for the shop's prize wall. Two tables, everyone else standing round them. Rowan's third game if he is in. Ends with two finalists. @clock 35.

123.title: Qualifier: final
123.gm: One table under the lamp. If Rowan is in it, play it as a full scene; otherwise summarise it in a few lines through the people watching. The winner picks first from Dex's prize wall, the runner-up second. Ends with the handshake. @clock 35.

123.title: Names phoned up to the head judge; proctors walk the students home
123.gm: Mika telephones the four names to Ms Kirishima. The proctors collect every student on the sign-out sheet and walk them up the avenue with lanterns; the group passes the main gate before the night bell. Nobody stays behind. Rana walks at the back. One answer; it ENDS at the gate (@place main_gate). @clock 45.

124.title: Island Open, day 1: check-in, deck lists, player badges
124.gm: Doors at half past seven. About 110 players queue at the scorer's table: students, staff, townspeople, mainland players off Wednesday's ferry. Noor [noor] takes the deck lists, Mika [mika] spot-checks decks, runners hand out badges with a table number. Players and crew are excused from Friday's classes; everyone else has a normal timetable and comes down after the Midday bell. Rana [rana] is third in the queue; Livvie [livvie] has borrowed sleeves. The Guest registers like anyone else, politely. Rowan checks in as a player or reports for his posting. @clock 45.

124.title: Player meeting and the first pairings
124.gm: Hana [hana], head judge, from the stage: seven Swiss rounds over two days (four today, three tomorrow), fifty minutes each, one game a round; the top 8 play on this stage on Sunday; prizes 6,000 / 3,000 / 1,500 cr. No antes exist in sanctioned play, and she says that sentence slowly. Then the pairings go up on the board and the hall empties toward the terraces. Rowan only listens: ONE long answer, ending with his table number for round 1. @clock 25.

124.title: Swiss round 1
124.gm: @place duel_terraces. Fifty tables in the open air, the feature table in the arena on Bex's stream (Bex [bex] and Ms Laurent [vivienne] casting). Rowan's round is a tournament duel against a stranger: a mainland player or a townsman, drawn fresh. If he is on the crew instead, give him one slip to carry and one floor call to witness. Time is called at ten to ten; result slips go to the scorer's table. @clock 55.

124.title: Swiss round 2
124.gm: New pairings at five past ten: winners meet winners. Rowan's second game as a scene if the opponent is someone who matters (a classmate, a Battle Team starter), otherwise in a few lines with the result. In passing: Livvie loses a close one and does the arithmetic on her fingers. @clock 55.

124.title: Swiss round 3
124.gm: The last round before the break; the non-playing school arrives from class during it and the rails fill. If the standings allow, Rowan is paired up against a name: Saoirse [saoirse] or Dom [dom]. The Guest wins its third game in eleven minutes and spends the rest of the round watching other tables with real interest. @clock 55.

124.title: Lunch break
124.gm: One hour. The Mess serves players first on their badges; volunteers eat on their meal tickets. A free scene around ONE meal (@did lunch eaten): standings talk, who is 3–0, Rana alone with her list and a pencil. Runners call the players back at five to one. @clock 55.

124.title: Swiss round 4
124.gm: The last round of the day and the one people tilt in. Rowan's game is a scene: he is tired, and nerve tells. Rana wins or loses per her state (by default she is 3–1 tonight, alive). Time at ten to two. @clock 55.

124.title: Day-1 standings posted
124.gm: Noor pins the standings by the arena doors: records, tiebreaks, tomorrow's start at nine. Imara pays the day's crew at the council table. Hana reminds the floor that the venue closes at the Afternoon bell and that nothing is played here after hours. The rest of the day is free; the players' tiredness is real (Nerve). It ENDS with the board read. @clock 25.

125.title: Island Open, day 2: Swiss round 5
125.gm: Saturday, no classes: the whole school and half the town are on the rails. Pairings at nine sharp. Rowan's round as a scene if he is still in contention for the top 8 (roughly: two losses at most), otherwise briefly. The Guest is 4–0 and is put on the feature table; the cast struggles to find anything to say about it. @clock 55.

125.title: Swiss round 6
125.gm: The round in which most people's tournament ends. Livvie [livvie] is mathematically out of the money here by default and finishes her game properly anyway. Rana [rana] must win. Play Rowan's game, or his view from the rail of someone he cares about. @clock 55.

125.title: Midday break
125.gm: Fifty minutes and ONE meal at the Mess (@did lunch eaten), players served first on their badges. All the talk is the bubble: who needs a win in round seven, who is safe, whose tiebreaks are poor. If Rowan is on it, people tell him so, unhelpfully. Rana [rana] eats nothing and goes over her list. Runners call the players back at five to twelve. @clock 50.

125.title: Swiss round 7: the win-and-in tables on the arena stage
125.gm: The top tables are moved onto the arena stage under the big board. If Rowan plays for the top 8, this is a full tournament duel in front of the stands, crowd and all. Rana's win-and-in is here too: by default she gets through, ahead all game and shaking at the end. Time at ten to one; the last slip is walked to Noor by Hana herself. @clock 60.

125.title: The top 8 are read out
125.gm: Hana reads eight names from the stage in seeding order, slowly; by default the Guest first and unbeaten, Dom [dom], Saoirse [saoirse] and Rana among them, Livvie not. Rowan's name is read if he earned it (then: @plan for Day 126, Midday, great_arena). The bracket is posted; quarter-finals tomorrow at noon. Day pay at the council table. The Night Market is on in town tonight for whoever signs out. One long answer; it ENDS with the board. @clock 30.

126.title: Finals day: doors, bracket, players called to the stage
126.gm: Sunday. The stands fill from half past eleven; four tables stand on the stage. Hana [hana] calls the eight players up by seed and has them shake hands; Bex [bex] and Ms Laurent [vivienne] open the broadcast. Rowan is on the stage or in the stands. ONE answer, ending with the first cards cut. @clock 30.

126.title: Quarter-finals
126.gm: Four games at once, the big board switching between them. Rowan's quarter-final (if he is in) is a full duel. RANA [rana] at match point: whether she closes depends on what Rowan has done for her (her quest flags); by default she sees the line, does not trust it, and falls short. She must win this EVENT to keep her place, so losing here ends it: she packs her deck without a word. Do not soften it and do not decide it against the flags. Ends with four names on the board. @clock 70.

126.title: Semi-finals
126.gm: Two tables. By default the Guest beats Saoirse [saoirse] and Dom [dom] beats the last outsider; third place goes to the semi-final loser with the better Swiss record. If Rowan meets the Guest here or in the final it is an ordinary game: a flawless opponent, no cold, no ante. Play his game; give the other in three lines. @clock 60.

126.title: The final
126.gm: After a fifteen-minute stage reset: one table, full house, the cast hushed. By default the Guest against Dom, and Dom plays the best prepared game of his life and loses on the last turn to a line nobody in the booth saw. If Rowan is in the final, play every phase. Beating the Guest in this game is possible and counts (see the quest: worthy_rival). It ENDS with the handshake. @clock 60.

126.title: Prize-giving
126.gm: The Chancellor [okonkwo] presents third, second, first: 1,500 / 3,000 / 6,000 cr and the trophy. If the Guest won, it carries the trophy off the stage in both hands like a bowl of water, and the applause is a beat late. Livvie needed a money finish; Rana needed the title: show each of them once, as things stand. Crew are paid and thanked. If Rana has nothing left to lose she may do something tonight that is in the plot file, not here. ONE answer; the Open is over (@did Island Open finished). @clock 25.

127.title: Rana's birthday: supper at Mama's table
127.gm: The day after the Open, and the whole table knows how it went. IF SHE IS STAYING: the loudest supper of the term; Rana [rana] sits through it red to the ears. IF SHE IS LEAVING in the morning: one duffel stands by the door, Mama Odalys [odalys] cooks her favourite without being asked, and nobody at the table knows where to look. Supper is served ONCE at half past six. Rowan may give his present now. Ends when the plates are stacked. @clock 40.

127.title: The cake
127.gm: Mama brings the cake and the row sings. Staying: Rana lets Mama hug her for a full three seconds, counted aloud by the table. Leaving: she blows the candle out fast and thanks everyone in one flat sentence, and Mama hugs her anyway. ONE answer; it ENDS with the cake cut (@did cake eaten). @clock 20.

127.title: After the cake
127.gm: Staying: washing-up, the porch, an ordinary good evening; let it be short. LEAVING: Noor [noor] comes down the boardwalk at half past seven with the regulation marked in pencil: a formal hearing before the Chancellor on a student's behalf may be requested by her friends, and the office receives petitioners until the night bell. If Rowan and the others go (@place chancellor_office), Dr Vicar [okonkwo] hears them for fifteen minutes; what they can show decides it (plot file: rana_hearing_won), never mere pleading. If nobody goes, the evening ends on the porch and the boat is in the morning. @clock by what happens.

128.title: Exhibition scrim: doors and line-ups
128.gm: Free entry; the stands half fill after the last class. Five tables on the floor. Coach Rox [rox] reads the team's line-up as loudly as if nothing were wrong; if a starter has been in Ward B since Day 118 she names a reserve in the same breath and looks at nobody. Opposite sit the top finishers of the Open who are still on the island. If Rowan finished high he is called down by name to take a board. Bex [bex] has a camera on it. Ends with the boards drawn. @clock 20.

128.title: Five boards at once
128.gm: One game on each board, no ladder points, no ante. If Rowan plays: his first game against a starter with the school watching — a tournament-length duel against Saoirse [saoirse], Priya [priya] or whoever of the team is whole. Otherwise show the room: Willas [willas] loud and winning, the team trying hard to look like a team. Ends when the fourth board finishes. @clock 55.

128.title: The captain's board
128.gm: The last game left is Lilia's [lilia], and the stands come down to the rail for it. She plays at half speed, visibly, and still wins; her opponent thanks her and means it. Rowan only watches: ONE long answer. It ENDS with her standing up before the applause is over. @clock 35.

128.title: Chairs stacked; a question at the scorer's table
128.gm: While the tables are folded away Lilia asks Rox, not quietly, who on the ladder could make her play at full speed. Rox does not want to say and answers with next week's training plan. If Rowan played well today Lilia looks at him once during that silence. Rox sends the team to the showers. It ENDS with the floor clear. @clock 20.

129.title: Jessica's birthday: guests received in the tower lobby
129.gm: Twelve invitations, written by hand. The concierge has the list; guests are received from a quarter to seven and taken up together on the hour. Dress matters tonight. Arriving at one minute past seven is LATE, and Jessica [jessica] will remember it for weeks; say the time plainly if Rowan dawdles. If he is not invited there is no scene here. Ends with the lift doors. @clock 15.

129.title: Candlelit dinner on the terrace, twelve covers
129.gm: @place spectral_terrace. One long table at the pool's edge, place cards, three courses served by the tower kitchen, everything exactly right because she planned every inch of it. Jessica wears her grandmother's sapphires. Where Rowan's place card stands says what she hoped for. Free scene over ONE dinner (@did dinner eaten): the talk at his end of the table, her eyes going to one chair. Courted properly, this is the high point of her route so far. Ends when the plates are cleared. @clock 75.

129.title: The toast and the presents
129.gm: A toast by her oldest friend at the table, then the presents, opened in front of everyone: she is gracious about all of them and exact about one. A careless gift is thanked beautifully and remembered for weeks; a thoughtful one gets a second, private look. Rowan may say something of his own. Ends with coffee. @clock 30.

129.title: Goodnights before the bell
129.gm: Guests from other dorms must be home by the night bell and the concierge starts looking at his watch at nine. Jessica sees each guest to the lift herself. Whether Rowan gets thirty seconds alone with her at the rail depends on the evening. It ENDS at the lift (@place spectral_lobby). @clock 30.

132.title: Pre-release, Saturday flight: registration
132.gm: Saturday, no classes. The crates of 'Ashfall Crown' stand sealed behind the counter until the clock says eleven. Dex [dex] takes 90 cr a head and seats thirty-two; Mika [mika] hands every player a sealed pool and a checklist. Livvie [livvie] is here to sell, not to play, with a folding table of singles. Rowan pays and sits, or watches the prices move. Ends with Dex's 'Open them.' @clock 20.

132.title: Pools opened, decks built
132.gm: Forty minutes on the wall clock to build a deck from the sealed pool: a room full of people reading cards for the first time, trading opinions, groaning. If Rowan plays, tell him what his pool roughly offers (strictly by GAME_RULES and the card data, no invented cards) and let him choose a direction. Mika answers rules questions and is short with everyone today. Ends at noon. @clock 40.

132.title: Three rounds
132.gm: Three rounds of thirty-five minutes, casual stakes, prize packs by record. Play ONE of Rowan's games as a duel and give the other two in a few lines. Between rounds: Mika, asked the right way, says what is bothering her — among this month's trade-ins were cards with a deep-sea-and-stars frame that are in no set list and are not fakes; she gave them back. Wren [wren] comes down from the lab for the first time in weeks, studies the new set's print under a loupe and leaves before round three. @clock 105.

132.title: Prizes and the trade tables
132.gm: Dex pays out prize packs by record; the trade tables form at once and Livvie does the best business of her month. Through the shop window: Wren is across the street at the pawn shop window, standing very still, looking at something in it. She does not come back in. Ends when the shop goes back to ordinary Saturday trade. @clock 20.

133.title: Pre-release, Sunday flight: registration
133.gm: The second flight is smaller and older: townspeople, the players who judged yesterday, anyone who wants another pool. Same terms: 90 cr, sealed pool, three rounds. Yesterday's prices are already chalked on the board and half of them are crossed out. Dex [dex] opens the crate at eleven. @clock 20.

133.title: Sunday flight: build and three rounds
133.gm: Forty minutes to build, then three rounds of thirty-five. If Rowan plays again, play one game and summarise the rest; if he played yesterday he now knows which cards people underrate. Mika [mika] judges; during the last round she takes a card out of someone's trade binder, looks at its frame for a long moment and hands it back. Prize packs at about a quarter to two; then the weekend is over and the shop sweeps up. @clock by the rounds.

133.title: Expedition No. 9: muster and sign-out at the main gate
133.gm: IF ed_on_a_line (he learned to go roped): {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} [ed] is at the gate with two coiled ropes and a helmet that is too big; Viktor [viktor] checks every knot, Saoirse [saoirse] has come for the climb. Everyone signs out; back before the Afternoon bell. IF NOT: the poster had no rope in it. Viktor is not there, the gate proctor asks to see the gear and there is none; the party is turned back, or {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} goes over the wall alone later (plot file), and by evening a staff notice is pinned over his poster. In that case the next three points do not happen. @clock 15.

133.title: Down the iron rungs
133.gm: Only with the rope. Half an hour along the Cliff Path to the head of the rungs: rusted staples in the rock, the sea loud underneath. Viktor leads, {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} second, the others clipped in between; Rowan chooses his place on the line. ONE check for him on the worst pitch (fitness or nerve; a slip on a rope is a fright and a scraped shin, nothing more). {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} narrates the geology wrongly the whole way down. Ends on the ledge at the cave mouth. @clock 60.

133.title: The Singing Cave
133.gm: Half an hour on the ledge and just inside: at this state of the tide the cave sings, one low note and one above it. Biscuits. It is the first expedition anyone enjoys, and {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} knows it and goes quiet for once. Rowan can look, listen, talk to Viktor about routes, or to Saoirse about the water. What can be FOUND here is only what CLUES POSSIBLE HERE lists. Viktor calls the turn at four. @clock 30.

133.title: The climb out and the walk home
133.gm: Up is slower than down. Viktor last, coiling as he comes. On the path home {H=ed?'Ed'|Ed} plans No. 10 aloud and is told by three people at once that it will be roped. The party signs back in at the main gate before the Afternoon bell (@place main_gate). TWO answers at most; it ENDS at the gate (@did Expedition No. 9 finished). @clock 90.

134.title: Open Playtest: sign-in and tables
134.gm: After the Midday class. Wren [wren] has a clipboard at the lab door: name, table, 12 cr per completed session, paid at the end. Eight prototype tables, snacks on the paper cutter. Felix [felix] is drawing box art for anyone who stands still; Teobalt [teobalt] has come as a tester; Livvie [livvie] is here for the 12 cr and says so. Rowan picks a table (name two or three he can choose from, each with its designer). @clock 15.

134.title: Session one
134.gm: Forty-five minutes at a prototype: the designer watches Rowan's hands, not his face, and writes down everything he says. Junho [junho] goes from table to table collecting bug reports on everybody else's game; Eloise's [eloise] prototype is two metres wide and needs four people to shuffle. Play it as a free scene with ONE small design decision put to Rowan. It ENDS when Wren rings the bench bell. @clock 45.

134.title: Demonstration at the bench by the fuse box
134.gm: Between the sessions everyone turns round: Maisie Voltage [maisie] demonstrates her touchable-hologram rig. BY DEFAULT it flickers, holds for a second, and a fuse goes; people are kind about it. WITH lattice_rig it works: a hand closes on something that is not there (q_maisie_push_back). Either way a young man from the board's staff stands in the back row, writes nothing down and leaves first (plot: t_maisie_demo). Rowan watches or helps as his quest stands. ONE long answer. @clock 25.

134.title: Session two
134.gm: Tables swap. A second prototype, shorter, with the snacks nearly gone. If Chuck [chuck] has wandered in from the workshop he plays one hand of a student's game, breaks it in an interesting way and praises it for breaking. Ends with Wren paying out at the door: 12 cr a session against a signature. @clock 45.

134.title: The side bench
134.gm: The lab empties. On the side bench under the lamp lies Wren's private project: a first-print frame and a page of mineral names crossed out one by one. If Rowan stays and helps stack chairs she lets him see it. ONLY if he has earned it (her trust, q_wren_ink) does she say what she thinks the ink is — and that the only place to prove it would be wherever the first set was actually printed. Otherwise she turns the page over. It ENDS when she switches the lamp off. @clock 20.

135.title: Kenji's birthday: his floor's present
135.gm: Visitors sign in at the Rare Hall lobby. His floor has a crate of energy drinks with a ribbon on it and a card that says GO OUTSIDE, signed by all of them. IF KENJI [kenji] IS HIMSELF he takes the crate, laughs, and does not go outside. IF, by the plot timeline, he has been in Ward B since Day 118, the floor stands round the crate and somebody says, 'We take it over.' Go strictly by his flags; do not decide it here. @clock 15.

135.title: Kenji's evening
135.gm: HIMSELF: the common-room league tables, game after game; he can never say no to one, and Rowan can sit down across from him (a casual duel) or keep the bracket. He plays until two as usual; guests do not. IN WARD B: the floor carries the crate across the Quad (@place infirmary_ward). Nurse Camille [camille] lets them in four at a time for ten minutes each. The crate goes by his bed and the headphones on top of it, still playing, quietly. Nobody makes a speech. Rowan may go in. @clock 60.

135.title: Visitors signed out before the night bell
135.gm: The Rare Hall porter closes the visitors' book at half past nine and reads out whoever has not signed out. An ordinary end to the evening either way: the walk home under the lanterns in pairs, the proctors already on the paths. ONE answer. @clock 15.

136.title: Lantern Workshop: paper, frames, the fold
136.gm: After class, up the unmarked stair. Trestle tables among the planters; Marit [marit] hands out paper and split-cane frames, Livvie [livvie] shows the fold once, quickly, and then again slowly for Pippa [pippa]. One lantern each, one candle stub each, names on a paper tag. Rowan takes a place at a table: say who is on either side of him. Ends when everyone has a frame that stands. @clock 30.

136.title: Folding and gluing
136.gm: Glue, thumbs, the whole campus spread below. The free part of the afternoon: talk across the table, somebody's lantern collapsing, Felix [felix] making his octagonal out of spite, Wren [wren] correcting everybody's corners. Noor [noor] has read the fire regulations for Saturday and recites one. Rowan's lantern turns out as well as his hands allow; no check. Ends when the glue pots are collected. @clock 45.

136.title: Paint, and the wish
136.gm: Each lantern is painted and carries ONE written wish inside the fold. What Rowan writes is the player's own business: ask him, and never reveal or invent it; it stays private unless he shows someone. Livvie's is very small and very neat. Inya writes hers, crosses it out and writes another. People are careful to write ordinary wishes, and several fail: let it be seen in faces, not in words.. @clock 45.

136.title: Lanterns racked to dry; the garden cleared before dusk
136.gm: The lanterns go on the drying racks in the library's top gallery, tag outward, to be collected on Saturday at dusk. Tables folded, brushes washed in the watering can. Marit counts the racks twice. ONE answer; it ENDS with the stair door (@did lantern made for Lantern Night). @clock 20.

137.title: Supper as usual
137.gm: An ordinary Thursday supper at half past six, and a conspiracy: {H=tobias?'Tobias'|Tobias} [tobias] told nobody, {H=sammy?'Sammy'|Sammy} [sammy] found the date in the register and told Mama. The whole table knows and is bad at hiding it. {H=tobias?'Tobias'|Tobias} eats with his head down and notices nothing, or pretends to. Supper is served ONCE. If Rowan has a present he should keep it for the cake. Ends when Mama Odalys [odalys] says nobody is to get up yet. @clock 35.

137.title: The cake
137.gm: The lamp is turned down and the cake comes in with the candles lit and the row singing. {H=tobias?'Tobias'|Tobias} sits through it with his jaw set like a man being arrested. Nobody has ever made him a cake before, and he does not say so; Mama does not make him say anything. He blows the candles out when told. Play it in ONE answer and keep it plain. @clock 15.

137.title: Tobias washes up
137.gm: When the table breaks up he rolls his sleeves and washes every dish in the kitchen without being asked, and will not hand the cloth over. Whoever dries next to him gets about nine words, all of them true. This is Rowan's chance, if he wants it; a present given now is taken without a joke. It ENDS with the last pot on the rack and Mama turning the lamp out (@did {H=tobias?'Tobias's'|Tobias's} birthday kept). @clock 40.

138.title: Rose Day: the stall opens by the fountain
138.gm: In the break between the Morning and the Midday class the stall opens at the fountain, on the pitch Pilar [pilar] gave it: buckets of roses bought honestly from Silas [silas], a ledger, a jar. Ashton [ashton] runs it as if born to it. 3 cr a stem; the buyer names the recipient, chooses the colour and decides whether the tag is signed. Deliveries are tomorrow at noon on the Quad, in front of everyone, so an order is a public act. A queue forms at once and pretends not to be one. Rowan may order (@credits -3 a stem) or watch who does. Ends with the class bell. @clock 30.

138.title: Last orders
138.gm: After the Midday class the queue is longer and braver. Octavia [octavia] buys one, unsigned. Teobalt [teobalt] buys three and blushes at none of them. Jessica [jessica] does not buy; she looks at the ledger upside down. Whoever Rowan is close to may ask, lightly, whether he has been to the stall. Ashton closes the ledger at two on the bell and takes no order after it. @clock 30.

138.title: The takings counted
138.gm: Imara [imara] counts the jar stem by stem against the ledger on the fountain rim and hands the whole sum to Nurse Camille [camille] with a receipt: every credit goes to the ward, which Ashton has not advertised and does not mention now. {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] and Marit [marit] carry the buckets to the cool of the arcade for tomorrow. ONE answer; the orders are final. @clock 20.

139.title: Rose deliveries on the Quad
139.gm: Saturday noon, no classes. Ashton [ashton] and four runners deliver yesterday's roses in front of everyone: recipient called by name, colour seen by all, the tag read out if it is signed. Deliver EVERY rose Rowan ordered and any rose ordered FOR him by someone whose affection and nerve make that plausible (from the route states, not invented). People keep count. An unsigned rose is the talk of the lunch hour. Play it in one or two long answers; it ENDS with the empty buckets. @clock 40.

139.title: Lantern Night: stalls and music open on the Quad
139.gm: @place festival_grounds. Pilar [pilar] opens it from the bandstand at six: food stalls round the fountain, a student band, the curfew lifted on campus until midnight. People arrive in pairs and in careful groups; several routes are in one place tonight and they can all see each other. Free scene: who Rowan arrives with, who he looks for. The talk is of who will release a lantern with whom. Ends when the gallery racks are carried down. @clock 40.

139.title: Lanterns handed out and lit
139.gm: Marit [marit] and her helpers hand out the lanterns from the racks by their tags (whoever made none gets a plain one and a pencil for the wish). Tapers go from hand to hand. Tavita [tavita] and his proctors form up with storm lamps at the head of the avenue. THIS is where Rowan asks, or is asked: whom he walks down with is his declared choice, and others see it. Do not choose for him. Ends when the procession moves off. @clock 20.

139.title: The procession down to the Commons beach
139.gm: The whole school in one line of lights down the boardwalk to the beach behind the row; the proctors mark the line between the beach and the dark. Walk it in ONE answer with Rowan's companion: what is said on the way down, who is ahead and behind. Staff routes stay secret and ache for it: one look, no more. It ENDS at the water's edge. @clock 20.

139.title: The release
139.gm: On Pilar's count the lanterns go up, one per wish. Whoever Rowan releases his with is his declared choice. Lilia [lilia] and Willas [willas] release ONE between them: make the player love them. The Guest releases one because everyone does, and watches it with great attention. The flight drifts north over the island, and far off over the crater every light goes out at the same instant. A silence; then somebody says the wind took them, and the band on the Quad starts up. Rowan mostly watches: one or two LONG answers. @clock 40.

139.title: Music and stalls on the Quad until midnight
139.gm: The long free part of the night: dancing by the fountain, the stalls, the terraces dark and full of couples. Every route Rowan has opened gets its moment or its absence; people talk about what they saw on the beach, and some are hurt. The Night Market is on in town for those who dare sign out. Scenes close on their own; do not stretch one evening over the whole clock. @clock by the scene.

139.title: The midnight count
139.gm: The band plays its last number at twenty to twelve. Tavita and his proctors count everyone back up from the beach and through the Quad by dorm, name by name; whoever is missing is fetched. The curfew is back at midnight, exactly. ONE answer; it ENDS with Rowan on his own boardwalk (@place commons_beach). @clock 20.

141.title: Last call at the registrar's table
141.gm: The Evening bell opens the last twenty-five minutes of the ranking period. Zeynep Arslan [zeynep] has her table at the foot of the terraces: a result slip signed and handed in before 18:25 counts, one handed in after does not, and she says so to three people who try. Two or three ladder matches are still being finished under lamps with a crowd round them; if Rowan has one open, this is its deadline. Ends when she caps her pen and carries the box up to the Quad. @clock 25.

141.title: The board freezes
141.gm: @place quad. At half past six the split-flap board on the Quad rattles through every rank once and stops. Prof. Santángel [santangel] reads the top of it aloud without comment. The name directly under Lilia Mann's is no longer a team member's: by default (plot timeline) the vice-captain was found at the captain's table this very morning, and the Quad reads that line in silence. Rowan finds his own rank: give the number and who stands just above and below him. ONE long answer. @clock 20.

141.title: The eight for the Cup's open bracket
141.gm: Coach Rox [rox] reads the top 8 players outside the Battle Team: they play the Interschool Cup's open bracket in March (Days 166–168). If Rowan is among them she says his name like any other and tells the eight to be at the gym on Wednesday of next week for the schedule (@plan). If he missed it by a few places, somebody tells him exactly by how many. It ENDS with the Quad emptying toward supper. @clock 20.

142.title: Leona's birthday: supper and Mama's cake
142.gm: Supper at half past six, then Mama Odalys's [odalys] cake and the row's singing; Leona [leona] thanks everybody pleasantly, ordinarily, the way she does everything in public. A present from Rowan is received with real, brief warmth. Supper and cake are served ONCE (@did supper and cake eaten). Ends when the table breaks up. @clock 40.

142.title: On the bench outside
142.gm: On the bench outside the kitchen lies a small parcel with no card. Leona opens it on the step: a woman's wristwatch, old, the strap worn to the shape of a narrower wrist. She knows whose it was and who left it, and says neither. BY DEFAULT she closes her hand on it, puts it in her locked suitcase and says nothing; IF father and daughter are speaking (plot: helicals_reconciled) she holds it a moment longer, and is wearing it tomorrow. If Rowan is there she lets him see it; she does not explain unless he has her trust. ONE answer. @clock 20.

143.title: Movie Night: doors and seats
143.gm: The student lounge after supper: sofas dragged into rows, a sheet for a screen, Bex [bex] at the projector. It is the first movie night since the curfew, an early showing negotiated by Teobalt: start at a quarter to seven, lights up by half past eight, everyone home before the night bell. Tonight's film is a romance, by vote, and the people who voted against it have come anyway. Who Rowan sits next to is the first choice of the evening. @clock 15.

143.title: The film
143.gm: The film is sentimental from its first minute. Play it in two answers at most: the dark room, what the people nearest Rowan do with their hands, Marit [marit] mouthing the lines, Pippa [pippa] and {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] sharing a blanket, Inya [inya] pretending to be bored. By the end the whole room cries, including people who will claim otherwise. Rowan can whisper, reach for a hand or just watch. It ENDS with the lights. @clock 105.

143.title: Lights up; walking someone home before the bell
143.gm: Sofas pushed back, red eyes, loud denials. Then the real scene: the walk home under the lanterns. Whom Rowan offers to walk to their dorm door, and by which path, is his choice; the proctors are already out and nod people along. Each dorm door closes before the night bell. It ENDS with Rowan on his own boardwalk (@place commons_beach). @clock 40.

144.title: Lilia's birthday: Willas's party
144.gm: Residents and their guests only: Rowan is here if Lilia [lilia], Willas [willas] or a Spectral friend put his name at the desk. She did not want a party. Willas has organised one anyway, loudly and badly: a banner with her name spelt wrong, far too much food, the Battle Team in paper hats. She lets him, and that is the whole of it. Free scene: the team off duty, Willas insulting every guest by way of welcome. Ends when he bangs a spoon on a glass. @clock 60.

144.title: Cake, and a card in crayon
144.gm: Willas's speech is three sentences and one of them is an insult. The cake. Among the cards there is one in crayon from the Founder, with a drawing that might be a dragon; she reads it twice and puts it inside her jacket. Rowan may give his present. ONE answer; it ENDS with the cake cut (@did cake eaten). @clock 25.

144.title: At the infinity edge
144.gm: Late, with the party thinning, Lilia stands at the pool's infinity edge. To whoever is beside her — Rowan, if he goes over — she says that she has been promised a real game at last, 'all-out, for everything', and that she has not felt this awake in four years. She has not told Willas the terms. He has guessed: he is watching her from the food table and has stopped being loud. She does not name the opponent unless Rowan already knows. Guests are out by half past nine for the night bell. @clock 30.

145.title: Karaoke Night: the cover comes off
145.gm: Visitors sign in at the Rare Hall lobby from half past six. In the common room the dust cover comes off the karaoke machine to a cheer; Bex [bex] has the song book and a sign-up sheet, Teobalt [teobalt] the door. The league whiteboard on the far wall has been wiped at last, and in one corner somebody has written three names with a small drawn candle; nobody mentions it and everybody has seen it. Rowan can sign up for a slot or not. @clock 20.

145.title: First set
145.gm: Bex and Marit [marit] open with a duet and it is a catastrophe, gladly. Pippa [pippa] does a novelty song with actions. Then {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny], who is simply good, and the room is surprised into listening. Rowan mostly watches and may heckle: one or two answers. Ends with the sign-up sheet going round again. @clock 40.

145.title: Open microphone
145.gm: If Rowan signed up, his name is called: taking the microphone is a nerve check, and it counts for Nerve whichever way it goes; the song is the player's choice. Later Noor [noor] is coaxed into one song by the whole room and has a lovely voice, which silences everybody, herself included. Free scene between the songs. @clock 60.

145.title: Last song; visitors out by the bell
145.gm: The last song is sung by everybody, badly, at half past eight. The cover goes back on. Visitors sign out at the lobby and are home before the night bell; on the way out the candle in the corner of the whiteboard is the last thing one sees. It ENDS at the Rare Hall door (@place rare_lobby). @clock 40.

147.title: Beach Clean: sacks and gloves at the Commons steps
147.gm: Sunday, the first warm one of the year, no classes. Pippa [pippa] with two cameras and {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] with the swim squad's clipboard hand out sacks, gloves and a stretch of shore each. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] takes four sacks. Low water is at half past twelve, so: the cove first, the pools after. Bare feet are allowed and advised against. Rowan picks a partner or is given one. @clock 15.

147.title: Cleaning Driftwood Cove
147.gm: @place beach_cove. An hour of honest work along the tide line: net, bottle glass, a boot, a crate stencilled with a mainland name. Free scene with whoever Rowan is paired with; Saoirse [saoirse] works the rocks nobody else can reach, Livvie [livvie] sorts what can be sold. The squad sings. The sacks are stacked above the wrack at a quarter past twelve. @clock 60.

147.title: The tide pools at low water
147.gm: @place tide_pools. The photo walk: Pippa photographs everything and everyone. The northern pools are empty and very clear, emptier than pools should be, and among the sea-glass there are beads of black fused glass (a clue only if CLUES POSSIBLE HERE lists it). Georgie [georgie] finds the nine-basin pool the locals call the Board and asks, reasonably, who plays on it. Nobody knows; one of the squad says her grandmother would not let her swim here. Rowan can look closer. The tide turns at one. @clock 75.

147.title: Sacks carried up; a late picnic on the steps
147.gm: The sacks are carried up to the row and counted for the council bulletin; bread, fruit and Mama's lemonade on the bungalow steps. Pippa promises prints by Wednesday. ONE answer; it ENDS with the afternoon free (@did beach clean finished). @clock 30.

148.title: Study Week, Monday: extended hours begin
148.gm: The library stays open until a quarter past nine all four evenings. Sign in at the desk with dorm and name: the list is what the escorts count by. Every carrel is taken by seven. The school studies as if grades could keep it safe; people who never came before are here, in pairs. Noor [noor] has a table plan. Rowan signs in and finds a seat: say who is at his table. (An evening of work counts as study: it is entered at the closing bell.) @clock 20.

148.title: Dr Blum's problem clinic in the reading room
148.gm: Dr Blum [blum] takes the long table in the reading room for an hour: old midterm problems on the board, chalk on both cuffs. He lets slip, as he does every year, that one problem on Sunday's paper will not be solvable as stated. Georgie [georgie] and Livvie [livvie] are in the front; Teobalt [teobalt] brings the questions of people too shy to ask. Rowan can work one problem at the board (knowledge) or listen. @clock 60.

148.title: Closing bell; escorts to the dorms
148.gm: The desk bell at a quarter past nine. Three groups form at the door by dorm, each with two proctors and lanterns: Tavita [tavita] counts every group against the sign-in list before it moves. The Commons run goes down the boardwalk and is in before the night bell. ONE answer; it ENDS at Rowan's door. @clock 30. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

149.title: Ophelia's birthday: Victoria calls the room to order
149.gm: Four o'clock in the Rare Hall common room. Ophelia [ophelia] does not see the point of birthdays and has said so. Victoria [victoria] taps a teaspoon on a cup until the whole room is looking, positions her sister in front of the fireplace, and produces a card with ribbons. Visitors who signed in at the lobby are welcome to witness. ONE short answer. @clock 10.

149.title: The card, read aloud
149.gm: Victoria reads the card aloud to her, all of it, in complete seriousness: what Ophelia is good at, in a numbered list, and what Victoria would do without her, which is 'nothing whatsoever'. It is the only time anyone on the island sees Ophelia not know what to do with her hands. Nobody laughs. Rowan only watches: ONE answer, ending with Ophelia taking the card with both hands. @clock 15.

149.title: Tea afterwards
149.gm: Tea is poured as though nothing had happened. Ophelia thanks each well-wisher in the same stiff sentence and keeps the card in her blazer pocket with her hand over it. A present from Rowan is accepted with a nod that, from her, is a great deal. It ENDS when Victoria announces that it was a success. @clock 25.

149.title: Study Week, Tuesday: sign-in
149.gm: Second evening. The same list, the same seats; people have started leaving a book on a chair to keep it. Somebody has pinned the exam timetable from the job board on the library door: Friday design hand-in and Practicum, Saturday Tempo and Rules, Sunday Probability and Lore. Rowan signs in. @clock 20.

149.title: Ms Kirishima's rulings drill
149.gm: Hana [hana] runs a whispered rulings drill in the periodicals room: she reads a board state, points, and the person pointed at rules in one sentence and names the principle. Fifty minutes, no mercy, exact praise. It is also the briefing for Saturday's practical: candidates will judge a staged match and are graded on procedure. Rowan gets pointed at twice (knowledge; let the player answer in his own words). @clock 50.

149.title: Closing bell; escorts to the dorms
149.gm: As on Monday: desk bell, three groups, Tavita's [tavita] count against the list, lanterns. On the Commons run somebody is quizzing somebody else all the way down the boardwalk. In before the night bell. ONE answer; the evening is over (@did study evening finished). @clock 30. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

150.title: Evening on the tower terrace
150.gm: Plot timeline, t_challenge_lilia: on the tower terrace, in front of Willas [willas] and the pool lights, the Guest says: 'Lilia Mann, I challenge you under the Charter.' Lilia [lilia] defers three days, as Article 3 allows; she is almost smiling. Willas is not. OFFSTAGE unless Rowan is on the terrace as somebody's guest: if he is elsewhere do NOT narrate it; he hears of it tonight or tomorrow from someone who was there (the team has known this was coming). Set lilia_challenged. If Rowan is present, he is a witness and may speak afterwards, to either of them. @clock 20.

150.title: Study Week, Wednesday: sign-in
150.gm: Third evening, the fullest. The Spectral table has two empty chairs for the first hour and then one: Willas [willas] comes in late, signs the list, opens no book and looks at the clock more than at the page. If Rowan knows him he gets a nod. Sign in, find a seat. @clock 20.

150.title: Course groups
150.gm: No clinic tonight: the tables sort themselves by course. Noor's [noor] Rules group, Teobalt's [teobalt] Tempo ledgers, Georgie [georgie] explaining Probability with sweets. A free study scene (the study is entered at the closing bell, not here). If Rowan watches the Spectral table, or already knows what was said on the terrace this evening, he may get one exchange with Willas before closing: he is courteous, absent, and says he has 'an errand' later. Keeping him talking matters tonight (see the plot file); do not say so. @clock by the scene.

150.title: Closing bell; escorts to the dorms
150.gm: The escorts form up. Tavita [tavita] takes the Spectral run himself tonight and his count comes out one short: Willas, his year-mate and old neighbour on the Row, told him on the steps that he had 'an errand', and Tavita let him go. He says so aloud, unhappy about it. The other runs leave on time. If Rowan asks, pushes, or goes after Willas, that is his move and breaks the curfew (risk as usual). Otherwise he is walked home. @clock 30. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

150.title: The Great Arena, after the night bell
150.gm: Canon unless Willas was saved. He goes alone to the arena and takes Lilia's place as one bound to her (Article 5); the Guest, scrupulous, accepts. He plays the best game of his life and it is not close. If Rowan is NOT there it is OFFSTAGE: narrate NOTHING of it tonight. PREVENTABLE if Rowan acts in time: warn Lilia, keep Willas talking past the hour, take the seat himself (it would rather not: 'You are roommate'), or have Noor contest whether Willas may stand without Lilia's word. If Rowan is present and fails, he sees the last phase. Set flags only as the plot file says. @clock 60.

150.title: Dawn at the captain's table
150.gm: ONLY if the duel was played and lost tonight (willas_hollowed). Lilia [lilia] finds him at first light at her own table in the arena, sleeves rolled up, eyes open. She does not make a sound. She sits down across from him and stays there until Coach Rox [rox] comes; then Nurse Camille [camille] and a stretcher. After that she goes cold. Rowan is not here unless he broke the curfew or was called: otherwise he learns it at breakfast, from the row, in one sentence. Do not stage it twice. @clock 45.

151.title: Study Week, Thursday: sign-in
