151.gm: The last evening before the papers. If Willas was found this morning the library is nearly silent and nearly full: nobody wants to be alone and nobody can read. Two proctors stand at the door instead of one and the sign-in list is read back. Otherwise it is an ordinary last-night scramble. Rowan signs in. @clock 20.

151.title: The last evening
151.gm: Free study (entered at the closing bell); whoever shares Rowan's table tonight matters more than the book. Ms Kirishima [hana] comes through at eight with tomorrow's seating lists and stops, once, at an empty chair. Dr Blum [blum] leaves a tin of barley sugar on the desk without a word. Let ONE person say something true to Rowan about being frightened and working anyway. @clock by the scene.

151.title: Closing bell; escorts to the dorms
151.gm: The bell goes five minutes early. Every run is counted twice, at the library door and at the dorm door, and nobody is let go on an errand tonight. Exam assembly is tomorrow at eight in the lecture hall. ONE answer; it ENDS at Rowan's door (@did study week finished). @clock 30. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

152.title: Midterms, Friday: exam assembly
152.gm: Friday's two class slots ARE the exams (Card Design in the Morning, Table Practicum at Midday); Saturday and Sunday carry the rest. The whole intake in the lecture hall at eight. Ms Kirishima [hana] reads the rules of the examination (own pen, no notes, no talking, cheating is an F and a hearing) and her voice is not quite steady; at the Battle Team's table there is an empty chair that everybody has agreed not to look at. Lilia [lilia] sits her papers this week, top marks, and speaks to no one. Then today's lists: design hand-in until nine, Practicum from a quarter past eleven in the Trial Domes. Rowan only listens: ONE answer. @clock 25.

152.title: Card Design: submission hand-in (closes 09:00)
152.gm: The Morning slot of Card Design is the hand-in: the design submission is handed in at the lab counter, in an envelope with name and course: Wren [wren] stamps each one with the time for the Founder, who is 'marking in the workshop'. At nine exactly she closes the hatch; a submission at one minute past is late and loses a grade. If Rowan has not finished his (see his study record for gd110) he has these minutes and a borrowed pencil. Ends with the hatch. @clock 30.

152.title: Table Practicum: decks handed over
152.gm: @place trial_dome. Coach Rox [rox] hands every candidate a sealed deck box and an opponent's name, ten minutes before the first game: an unknown deck, ten minutes to read it. The benches are silent except for cards. Rowan gets his box (tell the player what kind of deck it is in two lines, by the real card data) and his opponent: a second-year, drawn. Low Nerve shows here first. Ends with Rox's whistle. @clock 15.

152.title: Table Practicum: the two-game set
152.gm: A two-game set with the handed-over deck, recorded, graded on procedure and composure and only then on the result. Play it as an exam duel (@duel, exam kind); the second game in summary if the first was played in full. Rox marks on a clipboard and says nothing until the handshake, then one sentence that is the whole of her feedback. Results on Monday. After it the day is free; the wise go to bed early. @clock 75.

153.title: Midterms, Saturday: seating for Tempo & Resource
153.gm: Seating by list, alternate seats, bags at the wall. Prof. Santángel [santangel] writes the finishing time on the board before he says good morning. The paper lies face down. Rowan finds his seat: say who is on either side. Ends with 'Turn over.' @clock 15.

153.title: Tempo & Resource: written paper
153.gm: Ninety minutes: annotate a recorded World Final game turn by turn with a tempo ledger for both players. Play it in ONE or two answers: the one turn where the obvious reading is wrong (a knowledge check decides whether Rowan sees it, helped by his study record), the clock, Santángel walking the rows. 'Pens down' at a quarter past ten, to the second. Then half an hour of air before the practical. @clock 90.

153.title: Rules & Judging: the staged-match practical
153.gm: @place trial_dome. Candidates are called in fours. In each dome two upper-years play a staged match with planted errors while the candidate judges it from the floor: Ms Kirishima [hana] watches with a checklist. Rowan must catch what he can and rule aloud, in procedure (let the player rule in his own words on TWO incidents; knowledge and nerve). She thanks him exactly as she thanks everybody. Called by noon; the afternoon is free. @clock 75.

153.title: Conditioning: the heartbeat drill
153.gm: The gym, as in autumn: the track, and at the end of it a table with a sequencing puzzle laid out in cards. Coach Rox [rox] with the pulse meter. Each student runs until it reads above 150, then goes STRAIGHT to the table and solves the puzzle aloud in front of a judge. Rowan's turn when his name is called (@check fitness 8 | reach the table with breath to think; then @check nerve 8 | solve it with a hammering pulse). Short and brutal; compare it, in one line, with how his hands were in October. The Night Market is on in town tonight for whoever signs out. @clock 30–45.

154.title: Midterms, Sunday: seating for Probability
154.gm: The last day. Same seats; the hall is tired and a little giddy. Dr Blum [blum] cannot find the papers, which are under his arm; Georgie [georgie] tells him. Rowan finds his seat. Ends with 'You may begin — oh. Yes. Begin.' @clock 15.

154.title: Probability & Game Theory: six problems
154.gm: Six problems in seventy-five minutes. One cannot be solved as stated, and saying so on the paper earns full marks for it: if Rowan was at the clinic, or works it honestly (knowledge), he may notice; do not tell the player which one unless he looks for it. ONE or two answers. Papers in at ten. Fifteen minutes' break on the steps. @clock 75.

154.title: Lore & History: the comparative essay
154.gm: Prof. Ashdown [ashdown] writes the question on the board and sits down with her field notebook: a comparative essay under exam conditions, ninety minutes. Ask the player in one line what Rowan argues; grade it by his study record and by what he has really learned about the lore this year (what he knows from the plot may go in, and she will read that paragraph twice). Pens down at a quarter to twelve. @clock 90.

154.title: Papers in; results Monday morning
154.gm: Ashdown collects the scripts herself. Ms Kirishima [hana] announces that the letters will be posted in the glass cases at the job board tomorrow at half past seven. The hall empties into a Sunday midday; nobody quite knows what to do with their hands. ONE answer (@did spring midterms finished). @clock 15.

155.title: Midterm letters go up in the glass cases
155.gm: Before the first class. A clerk from the registry unlocks the cases in the arcade and pins the sheets, course by course, letters against student numbers. Fewer people have come than in October. Rowan finds his own row: give each letter plainly, from the game's record (never invented), in one answer. Ends when the case is locked again. @clock 15.

155.title: At the glass
155.gm: Those who care, care fiercely, because ordinary things have become precious. Teobalt [teobalt] reads other people's letters to them when they cannot look. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] nods once at his. Livvie [livvie] has her count on the back of a job slip: the C average a scholarship needs; she works it out twice. If Rana [rana] is still on the island, she checks one course and leaves. A word from Rowan matters to one of them. It ENDS with the bell for the Morning class. @clock 30.

157.title: Cup squad: the gym fills
157.gm: After supper. The Battle Team sits on the bottom bleacher in training kit, the ladder's top players and half the school above them. Coach Rox [rox] has her standards sheet on a clipboard and waits for silence without asking for it. Prof. Santángel [santangel] stands by the door with his arms folded. Rowan finds a seat (or is told to sit with the eight). @clock 15.

157.title: Coach Delgado reads seven names
157.gm: Five starters and two reserves. BY DEFAULT (plot timeline) four of the names that should be on the sheet lie in Ward B: she reads THOSE first, aloud, standing, and only then names who will sit in their chairs — the home team is Lilia [lilia], Saoirse [saoirse] and whoever is left. Any team member Rowan helped to save is here, is named, and knows why. If the bench is empty enough a top-ladder first-year is named: it can be Rowan (by his rank), or Gideon, or Georgie [georgie]. Go strictly by the flags and the ladder. ONE long answer. @clock 20.

157.title: The squad's first meeting
157.gm: Rox clears the bleachers and keeps the seven: the Cup timetable (Days 166–168, team rounds and the open bracket), training before dawn from tomorrow, jackets on Friday. Santángel adds two sentences on North Crown. If Rowan is in the squad he is in this meeting and gets his first instruction from Lilia, who is brief. If not, he is outside with everyone else, hearing who got in. It ENDS well before the night bell. @clock 30.

158.title: Dom's birthday: an afternoon in the arena stands
158.gm: IF DOM [dom] IS HIMSELF: he spends it alone high in the stands with a tape player, reviewing the unbeaten first-year frame by frame, charts squared beside him; the team trains below and leaves him be. Rowan can climb up. IF, by the plot timeline, he has been in Ward B since Day 141: there is no one in that seat; practice stops at three for a minute, and Lilia [lilia] leaves for the infirmary. Go by his flags. @clock 45.

158.title: Dom's afternoon
158.gm: HIMSELF: to a Rowan who has taken a game off a team member or reached the top 30 he offers his one analysis session: forty minutes on Rowan's own games, merciless and useful (a real gain: say what he learns). He was never fair to Willas and knows it now; the apology he owes is not Rowan's to receive, and he says who it belongs to. Otherwise he nods and goes back to the tape. IN WARD B (@place infirmary_ward): three weeks of squared charts on the locker; Lilia sits with him and with Willas in turn. Rowan may bring something and sit ten minutes. @clock 45.

159.title: Benefit Draft: sign-up and raffle tickets
159.gm: The Sleeve & Binder is fuller than on any Friday this year: town and gown both. 60 cr entry, raffle tickets 5 cr, all of it into a biscuit tin marked INFIRMARY on the counter. Students have signed out at the gate and walk home with the proctors at a quarter to nine. Dex [dex] seats the pods so that fishermen sit next to first-years. Mika [mika] keeps the list, and has quietly marked on it which regulars have stopped coming. Rowan pays in or just buys a ticket. @clock 30.

159.title: A word from Dex; Nurse Moreau says thank you
159.gm: Dex stands on a chair and says in four gruff sentences what the school will not: that the town knows who is lying in that ward, and that this is what the town can do. He will match the tin from the till. Nurse Camille [camille] thanks the room and cannot finish the sentence; Josie [josie] finishes it for her. Rowan only listens: ONE answer. @clock 15.

159.title: The draft and three rounds
159.gm: The draft, then three short rounds. Play ONE of Rowan's games as a duel (casual stakes, good manners, an old fisherman who plays slowly and well) and the rest in passing. Inya [inya] drafts at the next pod and is fierce about it. Between rounds Mika, if asked the right way, says who has stopped coming on Fridays, and why. @clock 105.

159.title: The raffle and the tin
159.gm: Dex draws the raffle: a framed old-set rare, valuable, not a first print (if Rowan holds the ticket, it is drawn by honest chance: decide by a plain roll, not by story). Then the tin is counted on the counter, Dex puts the same again beside it from the till, and Camille carries both out in her nurse's bag. The proctors call the students at a quarter to nine; they are through the gate before the night bell. @clock 30.

160.title: Spring Market on Main Street
160.gm: Saturday, no classes; half the school has signed out. Bunting from house to house, stalls the whole length of Main Street: the first greens, smoked fish, rope, a tombola. Mama Odalys [odalys] is buying for the week and has two students carrying. Students are treated with a new, awkward tenderness: extra in the bag, a hand on the arm, no questions. At five to twelve the brass band forms up and marches the street down to the harbour, and everybody follows. Free scene until then. @clock 55.

160.title: The Blessing of the Boats
160.gm: @place harbor. Noon. The fleet lies dressed with flags along the quay; a priest with a bucket and a sprig goes from boat to boat, the Second Chance last, and Captain Stroud [abel] takes his cap off for it. The fleet has not fished the north side since October, and the blessing lingers pointedly on 'safe return'. Silas [silas], in a clean coat, stands by the wreck memorial and does not join the hymn. Saoirse [saoirse] is on her family's foredeck. Rowan only watches: ONE long answer; it ENDS with every horn in the harbour at once. @clock 35.

160.title: 'A word for the fish'
160.gm: @place fish_market. {H=hedda?'Hedda'|Hedda} Njord [hedda] arrives under the market roof with her megaphone to shame the fishing fleet, {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] carrying her placards because she asked. She finds the gutting women already saying aloud what the school will not: that the children in the ward 'have been played'. She lowers the megaphone and listens. Rowan can stand with her, or listen too. Ends when she looks at the thing in her hand. @clock 30.

160.title: After the word
160.gm: For the first time all year {H=hedda?'Hedda'|Hedda} hands the megaphone to someone else: the oldest of the gutting women, who says four sentences about the north side and gives it back switched off. Josie [josie] and Captain Stroud have come to the roof's edge to hear. Nobody claps. {H=hedda?'Hedda'|Hedda} says nothing at all on the walk back, which {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} reports later with awe. ONE answer. @clock 15.

160.title: The market's long afternoon
160.gm: The band plays outside the Mulligan, Dex [dex] has a table of singles on the pavement, and the first boats put out on the afternoon tide, all of them turning south at the harbour mouth. A free scene to close the town day; students are due back through the gate by the end of the Evening slot. @clock 45.

162.title: Cup volunteers: sign-on in the council chamber
162.gm: After the Midday class, in the council's Monday session hour. Pilar's [pilar] lists lie along the long table: hosts (two to each North Crown player and their coach), runners, scorekeepers, stage crew. 20 cr a day for Days 166–168, counted out by Imara [imara] each evening. Bex [bex] and Pippa [pippa] are down for broadcast and photographs. Rowan signs where he likes, unless he is playing the open bracket or is in the squad. @clock 15.

162.title: Teobalt's briefing
162.gm: Teobalt [teobalt] runs it from a single sheet: the three days hour by hour, where the visitors lodge (the inn), who meets Wednesday's ferry at half past twelve, what a host does and does not do. Octavia [octavia] signs off the budget at the end of the table and is visibly thinking about something else; she reads one page twice and does not turn it. Noor [noor] corrects one clause of the visitors' code. Rowan listens: ONE answer. @clock 25.

162.title: Pilar casts the crews
162.gm: Pilar casts hosts and runners like a show: by height, by voice, by who can be trusted with a banner. The host posted to the North Crown delegation spends three days in Isolde Varga's company: if Rowan wants that posting he must ASK Pilar for it now and give her a reason she can use. She reads the lists out once; they are final when she caps her pen. @clock 25.

162.title: Door and floor crews: walk-through in the arena
162.gm: @place great_arena. Tavita [tavita] takes the door and floor crews through the arena: entrances, the visitors' rail, the tunnel, who may be on the floor during play, and that any approach to a visiting player 'outside the schedule' is reported to him or to Ms Kirishima at once. Each crew member gets a post and a lanyard. Ends at twenty-five to five. @clock 30.

163.title: Priya's birthday: at the gym
163.gm: IF PRIYA [priya] IS HERSELF: she trains through it. Coach Rox [rox] hands her the archery wrist guard with a new strap on it, wordlessly, between two sets, and that is the party. IF, by the plot timeline, she has been in Ward B since Day 131 (she played, properly and with a judge's form filled in, to win a teammate back): Rox hangs the wrist guard on the gym door at half past three and trains the others under it. Go by her flags. Rowan may be here to train or on purpose (if he trains, the session is entered at the end of the next point, not here). @clock 45.

163.title: A sparring game at the mat tables
163.gm: HERSELF: she asks for a game at the mat tables, pulse still up, and whoever spars with her (Rowan, if he offers: a casual duel) hears what she wants: one Cup match that nobody can say was given to her. A present is accepted with a nod and put in her kit bag. IN WARD B: the team plays one silent game at the mat tables with her seat left empty, and Rox ends practice early. ONE or two answers. @clock 30. If Rowan trained with the team this afternoon, end the LAST answer of this point with @train <stat> instead of @clock.

164.title: The welcome party forms at the Academy dock
164.gm: Wednesday, during the Midday class: the welcome party and the appointed hosts are excused, everyone else hears the horn through the classroom windows and comes down after the bell. On the pier: the Chancellor [okonkwo], Coach Rox [rox] with what there is of the home team, Lilia [lilia] in the captain's jacket, Teobalt [teobalt] with the hosts in a line and a banner. The Second Chance is in sight. @clock 15.

164.title: The North Crown delegation comes down the gangway
164.gm: Captain Stroud [abel] ties up at half past twelve. Seven players and a coach in teal and grey, Isolde Varga [isolde] first, Rex Tanaka [rex] behind her carrying two bags and talking trash at the pier in general. Isolde stops on the gangway and counts the Academy's team on the pier. She sees who is missing. She does not gloat; she is angry, on Lilia's behalf, and it shows only in how carefully she shakes hands. Rowan watches from the line or the avenue: ONE long answer. @clock 20.

164.title: Words of welcome; the captains shake hands
164.gm: The Chancellor speaks for two minutes, the visiting coach for one. The captains shake hands for Pippa's camera; Isolde says something to Lilia too low for the pier, and Lilia answers with her half-smile. If Rowan has history with Isolde she finds him with her eyes once. Ends when the luggage carts roll. @clock 15.

164.title: Luggage carts and the walk to the Drowned Anchor
164.gm: The hosts walk the delegation and its luggage down to Port Mulligan, where they lodge at the inn. If Rowan is the North Crown host this is his first half hour in Isolde's company (@place inn at the end): she asks precise questions about the ladder and none about the ward. Otherwise the pier empties and the day goes on. Her windows from now: the opening ceremony, the Cup, the inn in the evenings, the departure on Day 169. @clock 45.

166.title: News before the first bell: the Founder
166.gm: It is all over the school before the first bell, wherever Rowan is: at dawn Silas found the Founder on the north ridge, on the threshold of the Ruin Gate — alive, not speaking — and brought him down on the tramway cart; he is in the infirmary, and Nurse Camille lets nobody in but Inya. Card Design will be taken by Wren Ishikawa until further notice. It reaches Rowan through whoever he is with, each telling it a little differently; nobody knows what an old man wanted up there at night, and you do not explain it. Inya is not at breakfast. Then the Cup day begins as planned. ONE answer. @clock 5.

166.title: Interschool Cup, day 1: doors, team sheets, the open-bracket draw
166.gm: No ordinary Friday: players, squad and crew are excused from class, and the lectures are thin. Doors at eight; the visitors' rail is draped in teal. Both coaches hand their team sheets to Ms Kirishima [hana], head judge. Then the open bracket is drawn from a bowl on the scorer's table: the Academy's eight ladder qualifiers against North Crown's entrants, single elimination, one round today, down to two players tomorrow, the final on Sunday. Rowan hears his pairing here if he qualified. Bex [bex] and Ms Laurent [vivienne] open the broadcast. @clock 30.

166.title: Team round 1: five boards
166.gm: Five boards on the arena floor, Academy against North Crown; three team rounds a day, and the Cup goes to the school with more rounds won by Sunday afternoon. The home team fields whoever is left: by default Lilia [lilia] on board one, Saoirse [saoirse] on two, reserves below. If Rowan was named to the squad he has a BOARD: play his game as a tournament duel. Otherwise show two boards in passing. Lilia wins hers like something being sharpened. The Guest is at the rail for every game. @clock 90.

166.title: Open bracket: first round
166.gm: The side tables under the big board. If Rowan qualified at Snapshot III this is his round, against a North Crown player he has never seen (tournament duel; Rex Tanaka [rex] talks through his own game two tables down and wins it). If Rowan is crew or spectator, give the bracket's results in a few lines. Losers are out. @clock 75.

166.title: Lunch: the two schools at the Mess
166.gm: One hour. The visitors eat at their own long table with their hosts; the teal jackets and the red ones look at each other over the trays. ONE meal (@did lunch eaten). Isolde [isolde] eats little and watches the door. A free scene: Rowan can sit with either school. Runners call the boards at a quarter past twelve. @clock 60.

166.title: Team round 2
166.gm: The second five-board round. The reserves are tiring and North Crown is deep; the round is close on the lower boards. Lilia plays her second match of the day at the same pace as the first. Rowan's board again if he is in the squad; otherwise he may watch from the rail, where the Guest watches too and may say one polite, accurate thing about a board. @clock 90.

166.title: Team round 3
166.gm: The school arrives from the Midday class and the stands fill for the last round of the day. By default the Academy takes it on Lilia's and Saoirse's boards and leads the Cup two rounds to one. Coach Rox [rox] does not celebrate. Play Rowan's part, then the room. Ends with the day's score on the big board. @clock 90.

166.title: Day-1 score read; the floor cleared for the ceremony
166.gm: Hana reads the day's results: the team score, the eight names still in the open bracket. Imara pays the crews at the council table. Gani Villaluz [gani] and the stage crew strike the tables and set the stage for tonight; the arena closes until the doors reopen at six. The time until then is free. @clock 30.

166.title: Opening Ceremony: doors
166.gm: The arena doors reopen at six and it is a full house by twenty past: the school by dorm, the town in the upper tiers, the delegations in the front blocks. Mr Marrow [marrow] has the centre seats with the board's people. The Founder has a seat in the front row (he is in it only if he is on his feet this week; if he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185), the chair is empty and people look at it). Rowan finds his seat or his post. @clock 30.

166.title: Flags, anthems, the Chancellor's welcome
166.gm: Both squads march in behind their flags, the Academy's line short. Marit [marit] sings the anthem unaccompanied, and it is the best thing in the evening. The Chancellor [okonkwo] welcomes North Crown in three exact sentences and does not mention the ward. Pageantry on a brave face. Rowan only watches (or marches, if he is in the squad): ONE long answer. @clock 30.

166.title: The captains' exhibition
166.gm: A five-minute exhibition between the two captains on the centre table, cast live by Ms Laurent [vivienne]. Lilia [lilia] plays it like a metronome: correct, quick, nothing in her face. Isolde [isolde] looks at her across the table with real concern and loses politely. Applause. ONE answer. @clock 20.

166.title: An announcement for Sunday
166.gm: Mr Marrow is given the microphone and announces, softly, so that the house leans in, a 'special technical demonstration' for the final day. The house applauds. Chuck [chuck], if he is in the front row, does not clap for that. The Chancellor closes the ceremony at twenty-five to eight. ONE answer. @clock 15.

166.title: The arena empties
166.gm: Plot timeline (t_lilia_counter), unless she has stood down or the Vault duel is won: while the house empties, in the players' tunnel, Lilia challenges the thing that took Willas — Day 180, at the Gate, for everything. It accepts. This is OFFSTAGE unless Rowan is in the tunnel (squad, crew, or because he followed her): then he hears it, and anything he does to change it goes by the plot file. If he is not there, narrate only the crowd going home under the lanterns; he may learn of it later. Set lilia_duel_set. @clock 20.

167.title: Cup, day 2: team round 4
167.gm: Saturday, no classes; the stands are full from the first card. North Crown has slept on yesterday's score and come out hard: by default they take this round on the lower boards and level the Cup. Lilia [lilia] wins her board in silence; Isolde [isolde] wins hers and looks across at once. Rowan's board if he is in the squad. @clock 90.

167.title: Open bracket: quarter- and semi-finals
167.gm: The open bracket plays down to two today on the stage tables: a quarter-final at a quarter to eleven and, for the winners, the semi-final straight after. If Rowan is in it, the first is a full duel and the second a short one (he is tired: nerve). By default Rex Tanaka [rex] reaches the final, loudly; who meets him depends on Rowan. @clock 75.

167.title: Lunch
167.gm: Forty-five minutes, ONE meal (@did lunch eaten). The schools mix more than yesterday; somebody from North Crown asks, carefully, what is wrong with this place, and gets three different answers. Rowan may be the one asked. @clock 45.

167.title: Team round 5
167.gm: Coach Rox [rox] changes the order of the lower boards; Saoirse [saoirse] plays up. Close again. If Rowan is a reserve he may be put in here. The Guest has not moved from its place at the rail since nine. @clock 90.

167.title: Team round 6
167.gm: Lilia's third match of the day, like something being sharpened. By default the Academy ends the day one round ahead; everything is decided tomorrow. Play Rowan's board or the captain's, then the result. @clock 90.

167.title: Standings and Sunday's order of play
167.gm: Ms Kirishima [hana] reads the standings and Sunday's order: team round seven at nine, the open final at a quarter to eleven, a stage interval at a quarter past twelve (Mr Marrow's demonstration, if it takes place), the deciding round at half past one. Crews are paid. The visitors go down to the inn; the Night Market is on in town tonight for whoever signs out. @clock 20.

168.title: Cup, final day: team sheets
168.gm: The coaches hand in the last team sheets. BY DEFAULT (plot timeline, unless rex_saved) North Crown's sheet has a blank on board two: their ace was found by his captain this morning, and Isolde [isolde] hands the sheet in herself, white, and says only that he is 'unwell'. She knows better within the hour. If Rex is whole he is the loudest person in the building. Go by the flags; stage the finding itself only from the plot file. @clock 20.

168.title: Team round 7
168.gm: Five boards, or five against four. The visitors play furious and frightened if Rex fell; the home crowd does not know how to cheer. Lilia [lilia] plays board one as before. Rowan's board if he has one. @clock 90.

168.title: Open bracket: the final
168.gm: One table on the stage. If Rowan reached it, play it in full: against Rex Tanaka [rex] if he is whole, otherwise against the other finalist, with the seat's story told by the cast. The winner takes the open salver and a line in the ladder ledger. If Rowan is not in it, give it in a few lines. @clock 75.

168.title: Midday interval on the stage
168.gm: ONLY as the plot file allows (t_prototype: marrow_has_jar and Marrow not exposed); otherwise an apologetic announcement cancels it and lunch is early. If it happens, Marrow [marrow] unveils 'Living Light': a hero that steps off the projector plate, casts a shadow, looks at the audience for nine seconds and comes apart. Standing ovation. The Guest gets to its feet at the rail: the only time anyone sees it angry. With the lattice or the pigment (see the plot file) it does NOT come apart. Rowan watches: ONE long answer, exactly by t_prototype. @clock 30.

168.title: The deciding round
168.gm: After a break for lunch at the Mess: the last team round, captains on board one, Lilia [lilia] against Isolde [isolde]. By default the Academy wins the round and the Cup, and Lilia wins her board without once looking up. If Rowan has a board, his game matters to the score: play it. Ends with the handshake between the captains, which Isolde holds a second too long. @clock 90.

168.title: The Cup presented
168.gm: The Chancellor [okonkwo] presents the Cup and the open salver; Coach Rox [rox] takes the Cup and hands it straight to her captain, who holds it as if it were somebody else's. The visiting coach thanks the hosts. No party is announced. Crews paid and stood down. ONE answer; the Cup is over (@did Interschool Cup finished). North Crown sails tomorrow at half past twelve. @clock 30.

169.title: North Crown comes down to the pier
169.gm: Monday, during the Midday class: the hosts are excused, others come down if they skip or get leave. A special ferry lies at the Academy dock. The delegation walks down with its luggage. IF REX FELL, his team carries him aboard on a stretcher (he should not leave the island; nobody tells Isolde that unless Rowan does). Captain Stroud [abel] has the gangway out. @clock 15.

169.title: Goodbyes on the pier
169.gm: Isolde's [isolde] last window; she stays on only if given a real reason (go by her route and the plot file). She offers Lilia [lilia] a place on the mainland, 'away from whatever this is'; Lilia declines with her half-smile. To Rowan, IF he has earned it, her honest reading of the unbeaten first-year after three days at the rail: 'That is not a player. That is the game itself, wearing a boy.' If he has not, a correct handshake. Free scene; Rowan may speak. @clock 30.

169.title: The special ferry casts off
169.gm: Boarding at a quarter past twelve; Isolde is the last up the gangway unless she is staying. The Second Chance casts off at half past. From now on no outsider is on the island except Marrow's people, and somebody on the pier says so. ONE answer; it ENDS with the wake. @clock 20.

170.title: Sammy's birthday: places set on the steps of Bungalow 6
170.gm: After supper the row carries a table, plates and a lamp to the steps of Bungalow 6. By now {H=sammy?'Sammy's'|Sammy's} [sammy] coat is mostly for warmth. Set as many places as there are people left on the row to sit in them: count them from the actual state of the campaign and say the number. Mama Odalys [odalys] brings the cake down herself. Rowan helps carry and takes a place. @clock 20.

170.title: Cake on the steps
170.gm: The cake, the singing, a present or two; {H=sammy?'Sammy'|Sammy} tries a mysterious remark and it comes out as thanks. A plain, small party, eaten ONCE (@did cake eaten). Rowan may give his present. Ends when the lamp is turned up. @clock 30.

170.title: Sammy says a few words
170.gm: Nobody asks him to. {H=sammy?'Sammy'|Sammy} stands, looks along the steps at the places that are not laid, and says something for them: let HIM be the one, in his own odd words, short, by name for each person the row is missing (only those really gone by the flags). Then he sits down and the row is quiet with him. ONE answer; do not add a speech by anyone else. Lights out as usual. @clock 20.

172.title: Hustings: doors at the Little Theatre
172.gm: After the Midday class. Two lecterns on the stage, a table for the chair, Pilar [pilar] with a stopwatch. Octavia graduates; the chair is open. Candidates: Teobalt [teobalt] and Sebastian Thorne [sebastian], the vice-president, a Spectral third-year who has waited two years for it. The house is nearly full. Noor [noor] hands out slips for written questions. Rowan takes a seat and may write one. @clock 15.

172.title: The speeches
172.gm: Six minutes each, by the stopwatch, order by coin. Teobalt: a plain platform — tell the students the truth, share the proctor duty fairly. Sebastian: 'calm and confidence', beautifully delivered, with nothing in it one could quote against him. Pilar stops each of them on the second. Rowan only listens: ONE long answer with real speech from both. @clock 30.

172.title: Questions from the floor
172.gm: The open part. Tavita [tavita] asks about one rule for the Tower and one for the Row, and gives his endorsement to whoever answers it. Imara [imara] hands each candidate a page of the budget and asks him to read it aloud: hers goes to whoever can. A good question from ROWAN can swing the room: let the player ask it in his own words and have both candidates answer for real. Bex [bex] records; Marit [marit] heckles once. @clock 40.

172.title: The president's endorsement; closing words
172.gm: Octavia [octavia] is asked for her endorsement from the chair. What she says depends on whether she has taken Marrow's offer (plot state): she endorses, or declines to, in a sentence that tells the careful listener which. Then one minute each to close. Pilar announces the vote: tomorrow in the council chamber from eleven until the Afternoon bell, result at dinner. @clock 20.

173.title: The poll opens
173.gm: The council chamber between classes: a sealed box on the long table, Noor [noor] with the student register, Imara [imara] and Tavita [tavita] as scrutineers. One student, one ballot, name ticked against the register. The queue reaches the stairs in the break before the Midday class and again after it. Both candidates stand in the corridor being pleasant. Rowan votes when he likes before two (@did voted in the council election); nobody sees his ballot. @clock 20.

173.title: Last call at the ballot box
173.gm: After the Midday class Pilar [pilar] walks the arcade with a handbell: fifteen minutes. The last voters run. At the Afternoon bell Noor seals the slot with wax in front of both candidates and no ballot is taken after it, including from a professor's favourite who arrives at one minute past. @clock 15.

173.title: The count
173.gm: Behind a closed door with a window in it: Noor counts aloud, Imara and Tavita tally, both candidates watch. By default it is narrow and goes to Teobalt [teobalt]; Rowan's conduct at the hustings and his standing can move it either way (decide by what has actually happened, not by preference). The result stays in the room until dinner. Rowan sees only faces through the glass unless he is a scrutineer's friend. @clock 60.

173.title: The result announced at dinner
173.gm: @place cafeteria. Octavia [octavia] taps a glass and reads the result. If TEOBALT: as president-elect he gains the charter register and the council's keys, and will use them for Rowan if Rowan has been straight with him; Sebastian [sebastian] concedes in one smooth sentence and shakes hands for Pilar's bulletin. If SEBASTIAN: he thanks everyone warmly, and from now on nothing is ever refused, only 'not this term'. ONE long answer; then dinner goes on. @clock 20.

175.title: Build Day: all hands at the fountain
175.gm: Sunday, two o'clock. Teobalt [teobalt] stands on the fountain rim with the crew lists: stalls, stage, lantern lines, banner, cake. Silas [silas] has the ladders and the only key to the lantern store. The school has turned out nearly whole and builds a fair with something like desperation: nobody wants to be the one not laughing. Rowan is given a crew, or asks for one (name three he can choose). @clock 15.

175.title: Stalls and the stage
175.gm: The heavy work. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] carries beams two at a time and is used as a crane; Marit [marit] chalks the stage marks for the pageant and moves them twice; the stall frames go up round the Quad in a horseshoe. A free working scene with whoever is on Rowan's crew: hammers, splinters, one real conversation over a held ladder. Ends when Mama's lemonade arrives. @clock 75.

175.title: Lemonade on the steps
175.gm: Twenty minutes on the main steps. Inya [inya] has the cake design on squared paper and is fierce about it: a deck box, to scale, and she will not hear of a simpler one. Asked about the Founder, she says she has not seen her grandfather for four days and that he is 'being mysterious about his present to himself'; she says it lightly and looks at the north ridge. (If he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185), she says instead that they will not let her stay past visiting hour.) @clock 20.

175.title: Three thousand lanterns
175.gm: Lines strung from the clock tower to every roof, and three thousand lanterns to hang on them; Silas feeds the lines, students on ladders pass lanterns hand to hand. Felix [felix] paints the birthday banner on the flagstones, on his knees, and Wren [wren] corrects one letter without being asked. Rowan can work a ladder with someone (free scene) or help with the banner. It goes on until half past five. @clock by the scene.

175.title: One string lit as a test
175.gm: At half past five Silas lights a single string from the clock tower to the fountain, to see that it holds. It does. The whole Quad stops and looks up for a moment and then pretends it did not. Tools counted back into the store; Teobalt reads out who is on which stall on Friday. ONE answer; it ENDS with the Afternoon bell (@did festival build finished). @clock 20.

176.title: Wren's birthday: the lab remembers
176.gm: She forgot. She is at her bench at half past six when the lab's lights go out and a cake shaped like a booster pack comes through the door with its candles stuck in with drafting pins. Felix [felix] conducts the singing. Wren [wren] says 'Oh' and then 'the foil is wrong on that', and eats two pieces. Rowan may give his present. The cake is eaten ONCE (@did cake eaten). @clock 25.

176.title: An old brush
176.gm: IF CHUCK [chuck] IS ON HIS FEET he comes by from the workshop, gives her one of his own old brushes, and says, apropos of nothing: 'If anything happens to me on Friday, the chest under the hammock is Inya's and the notebooks are yours. Don't let the suits read the margins.' He laughs. She does not. IF HE IS IN THE INFIRMARY (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185), the brush arrives wrapped in a rag by Inya's [inya] hand with the same sentence written on a card in crayon, and Wren reads it twice. Rowan, if present, hears it or sees the card. ONE answer. @clock 20.

176.title: Back to the bench
176.gm: The lab drifts home before the night bell. Wren puts the brush in her breast pocket and goes back to work, and does not work. If Rowan stays, she may ask him one question about Friday that she would not ask anyone else. It ENDS when she turns off the lamp. @clock 30.

178.title: Dress Rehearsal: the half-hour call
178.gm: The Little Theatre, six o'clock. Marit [marit] calls the half; Ms Laurent [vivienne] sits in row five with a notebook; Pippa [pippa] photographs the costumes; Felix [felix] is still painting a wave. Stagehands wanted: if Rowan volunteers, Gani Villaluz [gani] gives him ONE job (a rope, a lantern cue, the thunder sheet) and shows it once. Otherwise he may sit at the back. Ends with 'Beginners, please.' @clock 25.

178.title: The run: the shipwreck
178.gm: The birthday pageant, first half: the ship, the storm, the wreck on the north shore, as the Founder has told it for forty years. Play it in ONE or two answers through what goes wrong and right backstage; Rowan's cue comes once and matters. In the dark of the back row a door opens and somebody sits down: the Founder, if he is on his feet (not if he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185)), watching it for the first time in twelve years. @clock 45.

178.title: Interval and notes
178.gm: Fifteen minutes. Ms Laurent gives notes in a voice the whole house can hear: three cuts, one compliment. Marit takes them standing. Inya [inya] has seen who is in the back row and has gone very still. @clock 15.

178.title: The run: second half
178.gm: Second half: the cave scene, which the old pageant always hurried through, and then Marit's rewritten ending, in which the deckhand comes home. Nobody has seen it before tonight. Play the new scene in ONE long answer, plainly; let the house be silent after it. @clock 45.

178.title: House lights
178.gm: House lights. If Chuck [chuck] was there, he has watched the whole of it, cave scene and all, and afterwards he holds Inya's hand for a moment without a joke, and leaves by the side door before anyone can ask him anything. If he was not, Inya asks Rowan whether her grandfather would have liked the ending. Costumes on the rail; Friday's call is five o'clock. Everyone is home before the night bell. @clock 25.

180.title: Founder's Festival: the opening on the Quad
180.gm: Friday, no classes. @place festival_grounds. At nine the clock tower bell rings seventy-five times, which takes a while. Pilar [pilar] opens her last and largest event of the year from the stage; the Chancellor (or whoever holds the office by now: go by the plot state) says two sentences; three thousand lanterns hang unlit overhead. The school is brittle and determined to be happy. Tavita [tavita] has the doors; Imara [imara] pays the crews at the council table from the strongbox. Rowan listens: ONE answer; then the stalls open. @clock 30.

180.title: Stalls all morning
180.gm: The horseshoe of stalls: Mama Odalys's [odalys] kitchen stall, the design students' card-painting table, the Battle Team's challenge table with whoever is left to sit at it, a tombola run by Teobalt [teobalt]. The first long free part of the day: every route Rowan has gets a scene somewhere today, so begin one here. Scenes close on their own. People keep saying the Founder is receiving in his workshop from eleven (if he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185): that cards for him go to Nurse Camille's desk, and that Inya is up there with him). @clock by the scene.

180.title: The half-door is open
180.gm: ONLY if Chuck [chuck] is on his feet (if he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185), the half-door is shut, the well-wishers go to Nurse Camille's desk with their cards instead, and this point is a short visit there). His 75th: he receives well-wishers in a paper crown, gives away more presents than he gets, and tells the story of his 'first birthday on the island' — a tin of peaches, a fire, and company 'you wouldn't believe'. Rowan may give a present, ask ONE real question, and gets something small pressed into his hand. Clues only from CLUES POSSIBLE HERE. @clock 20 per visit.

180.title: The long tables
180.gm: Long tables down the avenue, the whole school and half the town at them; ONE meal (@did festival lunch eaten). The student band, speeches nobody listens to, Hana [hana] refereeing an egg-and-spoon dispute by the book. A free scene with whoever Rowan sits beside. Mr Marrow [marrow], if he is still received on campus, moves along the tables learning names. @clock 60.

180.title: The workshop in the afternoon
180.gm: By mid-afternoon the half-door is bolted and a note in crayon says BACK FOR CAKE. He will not be, unless someone fetches him: he has gone to the north shore with Silas, as every year (a long way on foot; by boat two hours in calm weather). Nobody on the Quad knows that; Inya [inya] may guess if asked the right question. If Rowan reads the note, the choice of what to do with the afternoon is his. Show it in a few lines, no scene. @clock 10.

180.title: Dusk: the lanterns lit, the pageant
180.gm: At dusk Silas's lines are lit, if Silas is here to light them; otherwise Tavita's proctors do it, slower. Then the pageant on the Quad stage, with Marit's [marit] new last scene: play it in ONE long answer. The Founder's chair in the front row is empty; Inya is looking for him between scenes (if he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185), the chair is empty for that reason, his paper crown on it, and Inya sits beside it and looks for nobody). LAST MOMENT: anyone who means to be on the north ridge tonight must leave NOW — it takes two parts of the day to get there. Do not prompt Rowan; if he has reason to go he will know. @clock 60.

180.title: The cake
180.gm: The cake is carried out: a deck box, to scale, Inya's design. Seventy-five candles. IF CHUCK [chuck] was fetched or comes back in time, he arrives late for a speech that stops in the middle when he looks at the mountain; he cuts the cake badly. IF NOT, Inya cuts it for him with her jaw set and a slice is put aside. The cake is eaten ONCE. ONE or two answers. @clock 30.

180.title: Music and dancing until the fireworks
180.gm: The curfew is lifted on the Quad until the count after the fireworks. The long free evening under the lanterns: dancing, the stalls selling off, the terraces full. Every open route gets its scene or its absence here. Jessica [jessica], Livvie [livvie], Noor [noor], {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny], Bex [bex], Octavia [octavia] and the rest are where their state puts them. Lilia is not on the Quad after nine; nobody has noticed yet. @clock by the scene.

180.title: The north ridge, half past eleven
180.gm: Canon unless she stood down or the Vault duel is won. Lilia has slipped the festival and climbed to the Ruin Gate, where the Guest waits on the threshold pavement: ante 'everything'; she has her captain's card with her. Silas [silas] is the only human witness. If Rowan is NOT here (he must have known to come and left at dusk), all of this is OFFSTAGE: narrate nothing of it. If he is here, this is his window BEFORE the duel begins, per GUEST.liliaDuel.withRowan: witness; champion under Article 5; the debt called under Article 7 (it takes precedence, and names the Vault); a plain challenge is deferred three days and she plays first. Dread, not spectacle. @clock 30.

180.title: Fireworks at midnight
180.gm: Midnight on the tower bell, fireworks from the terraces. Lilia is not in the crowd. IF, by the plot state, the duel at the Gate is being played tonight and is lost (Rowan not there, nothing changed): during the last rockets the lanterns go out in a wave from the north, string by string, across the whole Quad, and the band stops. If the night went otherwise, they burn on and the fireworks simply end. Decide ONLY from the flags. Tavita [tavita] begins the midnight count at once, dorm by dorm. ONE long answer. @clock 20.

180.title: The north ridge, midnight
180.gm: ONLY if her duel is played (not if Rowan called the debt or she stood down). Five phases, while the festival fireworks go up on the far side of the mountain. WITHOUT a change by Rowan: GUEST.liliaDuel.default exactly — she leads into the Endgame and loses on the last turn; 'everything' included her captain's card, and with it the way in. Set lilia_hollowed, gate_opened. WITH Rowan as witness or second, or with the duel moved into the Vault: the branches of the plot file decide, never this plan. If Rowan is not here, do NOT narrate it. @clock 60.

180.title: The north ridge, after
180.gm: What is left on the pavement depends wholly on the last hour: Silas with his lamp; Lilia whole, or still smiling with her eyes empty; the wall folded shut, or unfolded in leaves with the inner door standing open. If Rowan is here, this is where his night continues (the way down, the Vault, the debt: plot file and finale rules), and nothing is settled FOR him. If he is not, nothing of this is told tonight; tomorrow's first scene tells him. @clock by what happens.

181.title: First light
181.gm: The first thing Rowan learns today, wherever he wakes, decided ENTIRELY by last night's flags (never by this plan). (a) lilia_hollowed and the Vault duel not won: the lanterns hang dead, the hot springs whistle, people wake with small pieces of themselves missing (a name, a tune, the way to the Mess). (b) The Guest was beaten in the Vault: somebody comes running along the row shouting that they are sitting up. (c) Neither — she stood down, the debt is called and pending, or nothing was played: an ordinary grey morning after a party, with the thing still unsettled. Stage exactly ONE of these. @clock 30.

181.title: The Quad at eight
181.gm: The school gathers on the Quad without being called. (a) Tiles of the surface mosaics have gone dark; the Chancellor [okonkwo] (or whoever holds the office) and Nurse Camille [camille] say what little they know; Inya [inya] is looking for her grandfather (if he is in the infirmary (flag chuck_down, Days 166–185): she has been at his bedside since the lanterns went out, and comes down grey). There is a short window to follow it down: until the Midday bell (plot file, t_last_chance). (b) Ward B, or wherever the Hollowed lie, is full of people asking for breakfast: Mama Odalys [odalys] is already carrying trays, Bex [bex] is crying on air, and the last four weeks of term are an aftermath. (c) Teobalt [teobalt] organises the sweeping-up; whatever is pending keeps its own hour. ONE long answer. @clock 30.

181.title: The last half hour before the Midday bell
181.gm: ONLY in case (a). Until Midday the Guest is walking the friezes of the Vault, reading; the debt can still be called there (it now plays with Lilia's game added to its own). At the Midday bell it sits down at the central board alone and begins (plot timeline: t_island_played). Do NOT tell Rowan this as a deadline unless someone who knows is with him (Oru, Chuck, Silas, Noor with the register); show only what he can perceive from where he is: the holograms on campus flickering on by themselves, one by one, as the bell comes nearer. @clock 30.

185.title: The Fool's Draft: voting the worst cards ever printed
185.gm: April 1, after the Midday class. The Commons trade binder lies open on the lounge table: run by Tomi [tomi] if he is himself, otherwise by Inya [inya] with his binder in front of her and his rules read out from the inside cover. First the vote: cards are held up one by one and the table votes them 'worst ever printed' by howling; every deck must contain at least ten of those. IF THE ISLAND CAN LAUGH (a good outcome) the room is packed and riotous; OTHERWISE it is six people in an empty lounge, trying. Go by the state of things. @clock 25.

185.title: The draft
185.gm: The condemned cards and a heap of ordinary ones go round the table hand to hand; people take the terrible ones on purpose and defend them with speeches. Rowan drafts with the rest (let the player say what sort of rubbish he goes for; real cards only, by the card data). Marit [marit] narrates every pick in a commentator's voice until Bex [bex] takes over and is worse. @clock 30.

185.title: Three very bad rounds
185.gm: Three short rounds, casual, no stakes but honour. Play ONE of Rowan's games briefly as a duel and let the deck's badness matter; the rest in passing. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] attacks with something that should not attack. Georgie [georgie] is quietly undefeated with a pile of unplayables. In the subdued version the games are played all the same, carefully, and somebody laughs once and looks surprised. @clock 65.

185.title: The Fool crowned
185.gm: By default Georgie wins and, in the good version, is carried round the room on shoulders with a paper crown; in the subdued version the six of them clap and Inya writes the name into Tomi's binder under last year's in careful capitals. If Rowan won, it is his name and his shoulders. Cards back in the binder. ONE answer (@did Fool's Draft finished). @clock 20.

187.title: Last Friday Night Draft: sign-up and free pizza
187.gm: The Sleeve & Binder, the last Friday of the school year. 60 cr at the counter, pizza boxes stacked on the glass case, no charge. Mika [mika] takes the names and already knows who will not be back in September. Whoever of Rowan's friends is still on the island and drafts is here: Inya [inya]; Rana [rana] only if she stayed. Sign up, eat a slice (@did pizza eaten), find a pod. @clock 25.

187.title: Dex says a few words
187.gm: Dex [dex] stands on his chair again. A short, gruff speech about the year: what the shop saw, who it missed on Fridays, that the door is open in September to anyone who walks through it. He does not mention money. He gets down before anyone can clap properly. Rowan only listens: ONE answer with the speech in real words. @clock 10.

187.title: The draft and three rounds
187.gm: The last draft: the picks, then three rounds. Play ONE of Rowan's games as a duel against someone who matters to him, the others in a few lines. Between rounds the talk is of summer, addresses, who is coming back. If the curfew still stands, students leave with the last round; if it has been lifted, nobody hurries. @clock 115.

187.title: Prizes, and settling up with the shop
187.gm: Prizes by record. Mika has saved a card for someone she likes: for Rowan if q_mika_cardinals or her affection says so, handed over in a sleeve without a word. Last chance to settle with the shop: debts on the slate, trades left open, and the thing in the not-for-sale case if it was lent — Dex names what is outstanding and takes it or forgives it by Rowan's record with him. It ENDS with the shop bell behind him. @clock 30.

189.title: Sunny's birthday: the cove
189.gm: Sunday, the first real swimming weather. @place beach_cove. Half the school over the headland with towels: a volleyball net, a pile of driftwood for later, {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] in the water before anyone has put a bag down. If the birds have come home (a good outcome shows in this), they wheel over the headland and people keep looking up. A free beach scene; a present from Rowan is opened on the spot and worn or eaten at once. @clock 60.

189.title: The race to the diving raft
189.gm: {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} lines everybody up at the water's edge: a race to the diving raft, all in, no excuses. She wants one person in particular to lose gracefully: who that is follows from her route (Rowan, if it is his). If Rowan swims it is a fitness check against the best swimmer in the school: he will lose, and HOW he loses is what she will remember. Ends with a dozen people on a raft built for six. @clock 25.

189.title: Driftwood fire and cake
189.gm: The fire is lit in daylight because she cannot wait. Cake carried over the headland in a biscuit tin, slightly sandy, eaten ONCE. Singing; hair drying; the long easy end of an afternoon. Whoever Rowan sits beside is the scene. People drift back over the headland from five, and the fire is drowned properly before the Afternoon bell. @clock 90.

190.title: Finals Study Week, Monday: sign-in
190.gm: The last four study evenings of the year: the library is open until a quarter past nine. Sign in at the desk as at midterms. Final grades decide probation and next year's standing; scholarship students need their average, and Livvie [livvie] has hers on a slip again. Rowan signs in and takes a carrel: say who shares it tonight. (An evening of work counts as study: it is entered at the closing bell.) @clock 20.

190.title: Dr Blum's formula-sheet evening
190.gm: Sunday's Probability final is eight problems with an open formula sheet, so Dr Blum [blum] spends an hour in the reading room on what belongs on one sheet of paper and what does not. Georgie [georgie] has hers done already, in four colours. Rowan can build his own under Blum's eye (it will really help on Sunday: note it). @clock 60.

190.title: Closing bell
190.gm: The desk bell. If the curfew still stands, the escorts form up by dorm and are counted as before; if it has been lifted, people simply walk home in the dark for the pleasure of being allowed to. ONE answer; it ENDS at Rowan's door. @clock 25. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

191.title: Finals Study Week, Tuesday: sign-in
191.gm: Second evening. The exam timetable is on the door: Friday design pitch and the Practicum final on the arena stage; Saturday Tempo best-of-three, the Level-1 judge certification and the Conditioning circuit; Sunday Probability and Lore. People read it and go pale at 'arena stage'. Sign in, same carrel. @clock 20.

191.title: Ms Kirishima's certification clinic
191.gm: Hana [hana] takes the periodicals room for the Level-1 candidates: what the written paper asks, how the floor practical is marked, the three mistakes that fail people every year. Noor [noor] already knows them and helps the others. Rowan gets two rulings to make in his own words (knowledge). Whoever passes on Saturday holds a real judge's card. @clock 60.

191.title: Closing bell
191.gm: As on Monday: the bell, the walk down, with or without lanterns. On the way somebody asks Rowan what he is doing in the summer, and it is the first time this year that anyone has asked; let the player answer. ONE answer; it ENDS at his door (@did study evening finished). @clock 25. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

192.title: Finals Study Week, Wednesday: sign-in
192.gm: Third evening. Teobalt [teobalt] has organised tea from the Mess at the desk at eight, which is against the library rules and has been signed off by the librarian on a petition form. Sign in. @clock 20.

192.title: Tempo ledgers at the long table
192.gm: The Tempo final is a best-of-three in the Trial Domes with the ledger kept DURING play, and the ledger is what is graded. Teobalt's group practises it at the long table: two play in whispers, a third keeps the ledger, then they swap. Rowan takes a turn at each (technique or knowledge; say plainly what he is still getting wrong). Tea at eight. @clock 60.

192.title: Closing bell
192.gm: The desk bell at a quarter past nine; the cups go back into the Mess crate and Teobalt counts them, because he signed for them. Escorts or no escorts, as the curfew stands. On the boardwalk the ledger group is still arguing about one tempo entry, and nobody minds. ONE answer; it ENDS at Rowan's door (@did study evening finished). @clock 25. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

193.title: Finals Study Week, Thursday: the last evening
193.gm: The last study evening of the year. The seating lists for tomorrow are pinned by the desk and people read them as if they were verdicts. Rowan's carrel has been kept for him by whoever shared it this week, with a book on the chair. Sign in. @clock 20.

193.title: The carrel
193.gm: No clinic tonight. Whoever shares Rowan's carrel now is someone he will miss in May: let the scene be about that as much as about the books (the study is entered at the closing bell). Dr Blum [blum] and Ms Kirishima [hana] walk through once, together, and say good luck to each table in turn. One true exchange; then work. @clock by the scene.

193.title: Closing bell, five minutes early
193.gm: The librarian rings five minutes early and says so: sleep is worth more than a page. Books are returned to the trolley for the last time this year. Exam assembly is tomorrow at eight in the lecture hall. ONE answer; it ENDS at Rowan's door (@did finals study week finished). @clock 25. If Rowan really worked this evening, end THIS answer with @study <courseId> instead of @clock (it counts the session and carries the clock to ten).

194.title: Finals, Friday: exam assembly
194.gm: Friday's two class slots ARE the finals (Card Design in the Morning, Table Practicum at Midday). Eight o'clock, the whole intake. Ms Kirishima [hana] reads the rules of the examination; two F in a term mean probation, three mean expulsion, and she says it without softening it. Today: design pitches from a quarter to nine in the design lab, the Practicum final on the arena stage from a quarter past eleven. Rowan only listens: ONE answer. @clock 20.

194.title: Card Design: the pitch to the staff panel
194.gm: A ten-card set fragment and a pitch to a staff panel of three (the Founder if he can, otherwise Wren [wren] sits in for him; Dr Blum [blum]; Ms Kirishima). Candidates wait on the bench outside and go in for eight minutes each, five of them the pitch; the panel sits until a quarter to eleven. Let the player pitch in his own words; grade it by his gd110 record and by whether the idea is honest. One question from each panellist. Rowan's turn comes when he is there. @clock 60.

194.title: Table Practicum final: call to the arena stage
194.gm: @place great_arena. The Practicum final is played on the arena stage with crowd audio: Gani Villaluz [gani] runs a recorded crowd through the house speakers at match volume. Coach Rox [rox] and two colleagues sit as the panel at the scorer's table. Candidates are called in pairs; own deck. Rowan checks his deck in and waits in the tunnel, where the noise is worst. @clock 15.

194.title: The stage duel
194.gm: Play it as a SCENE (@duel, exam kind): Rowan against a drawn classmate, on the stage where he watched the Open, with the noise of a full house and nobody in the seats but three examiners. It measures how far his hands have come since the Placement Duel on Day 1: say so through what he notices about them. Rox's verdict afterwards is one sentence. Then the day is free. @clock 75.

195.title: Finals, Saturday: the draw for Tempo
195.gm: @place trial_dome. Prof. Santángel [santangel] draws the pairings from a hat at a quarter past eight: one classmate each, best of three, ledger kept during play and handed in with the result. The ledger is graded, not only the score. Rowan hears his opponent's name and his dome. @clock 15.

195.title: Tempo & Resource: best of three
195.gm: Up to three games in a Trial Dome, a proctor at the door. Play the first game in full (@duel, exam kind) and the others in summary unless it goes to a decider; in each, ask the player ONE ledger entry at a turning point and grade it. Santángel reads the ledger at the handshake and says 'adequate' or does not. Done by half past ten. @clock 120.

195.title: Level-1 judge certification: written paper
195.gm: @place lecture_hall. Forty-five minutes, closed book, set by Ms Kirishima [hana]: rulings, procedure, one question on conduct. ONE answer, with two questions put to the player for real. Papers in at half past eleven; the floor practical follows after a short lunch. @clock 45.

195.title: Level-1 certification: floor practical
195.gm: Back in the Domes, in threes: each candidate judges ten minutes of a staged match and then defends three rulings against Ms Kirishima, who argues the wrong side on purpose. Let Rowan defend ONE in his own words (knowledge, nerve). Whoever passes is handed a Level-1 card on the spot, and she shakes hands as with a colleague. @clock 60.

195.title: Physical Conditioning: the circuit
195.gm: @place gym. Coach Rox's [rox] final: the full circuit against the clock (fitness), then, pulse still up, a composed-play test at the mat tables — three sequencing puzzles, judged. ONE or two answers. She writes a time on his hand in marker. The Night Market is on in town tonight; most people sleep instead. @clock 60.

196.title: Finals, Sunday: seating for Probability
196.gm: The last exam morning of the year. Formula sheets are inspected at the door by Dr Blum [blum], who admires several. Same seats. Rowan's sheet is as good as he made it on Monday. Ends with 'Begin.' @clock 15.

196.title: Probability & Game Theory: eight problems
196.gm: Eight problems, open formula sheet, ninety minutes. ONE or two answers: the problem Rowan is glad of, the one he is not (knowledge, helped by the sheet and his study record). Pens down at a quarter past ten; fifteen minutes on the steps. @clock 90.

196.title: Lore & History: essay, and the oral-history file handed in
196.gm: Prof. Ashdown [ashdown] sets the essay and collects the oral-history files at her desk during it: each student's file of what island people TOLD them this year. Ask the player whom Rowan's file quotes; what he really gathered counts, and she turns his pages slowly. If he knows more than is safe to write, that is his decision to make. Pens down at a quarter to twelve. @clock 75.

196.title: Pens down: finals are over
196.gm: Ashdown ties the scripts with tape. Ms Kirishima [hana] announces that year-end grades go up at the job board tomorrow at half past seven. The hall empties into the sun, and somebody throws a pencil case in the fountain. ONE answer (@did spring finals finished). @clock 15.

197.title: Year-end grades go up
197.gm: The last crowd at the glass, before the Morning bell. Final letters for the Spring Term and the year, course by course. Rowan's row: give every letter plainly from the game's record, and what it means (clear, probation, or the Chancellor's office). Teobalt [teobalt] reads for those who cannot look. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] looks once and nods. @clock 20.

197.title: At the glass
197.gm: Relief, arithmetic, one person crying behind the arcade pillar. If Rana [rana] is still on the island she finds her name and stands there a little longer than she needs to. The Chancellor [okonkwo] (or whoever holds the office) passes through the arcade and stops to congratulate two students by name. A free scene; it ENDS with the bell. @clock 30.

197.title: Tuition notices at the mail window
197.gm: From nine the notices are handed out at the mail window of the campus store: scholarship renewals, and for everyone without one the bill for year two, 9,000 cr. Livvie's [livvie] deadline is real and falls now: what she has, what her friends can LAWFULLY add, and what the Academy can be shamed into decides whether she is on the ferry for good on Day 210 (q_livvie_9000; by default she is short). If she has left already, her envelope lies uncollected. Rowan gets his own notice: state the sum from his record. @clock 30.

198.title: Yearbook photograph: everyone to the main steps
198.gm: The Midday class is let out early for it; jackets on. Pippa [pippa] is on a stepladder at the fountain, shouting rows into shape: fourth-years at the back, first-years sitting. Georgie [georgie] carries her spare film. Who stands where is the scene: say who ends up beside Rowan, and where a gap is left ON PURPOSE for someone who cannot be here (only from the real state of the campaign). @clock 15.

198.title: The whole-school photograph
198.gm: Three exposures: one stiff, one with the Chancellor [okonkwo] (or the acting chancellor) in the middle, one in which Pippa says something unrepeatable and gets the picture she wanted. Rowan may do something in the last one. ONE answer. @clock 20.

198.title: Dorm groups
198.gm: Spectral first, on the steps, in order of height by somebody's decision. Rare Hall second. The Commons last, barefoot by tradition, with Mama Odalys [odalys] in the middle and Teobalt [teobalt] holding the bungalow numbers: this one will hang on Mama's wall with all the others, and she shows the row where. A place in it is left open or not, as things stand. ONE or two answers (@did yearbook photograph taken). @clock 30.

199.title: Senior Send-Off: the fire is lit
199.gm: The Commons hosts all three dorms at the pit. Mama Odalys [odalys] has cooked for a hundred; {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] built the fire. The fourth-years arrive together with shoeboxes under their arms: Octavia [octavia], Wren [wren], and of the Battle Team whoever is whole and on the island. ONE meal on laps (@did supper eaten). Free scene. If Lilia and Willas are both here and whole, they sit on one log and it is plain to everybody what that is worth. @clock 45.

199.title: The fourth-years burn their first-year decklists
199.gm: One by one each fourth-year reads the worst card on their first-year decklist aloud, says one sentence, and puts the list on the fire. For a senior who cannot be here, the seniors keep a place on the log, and a friend reads the list for them. Rowan only watches: ONE long answer, with three or four of them in real words. @clock 30.

199.title: The talking shell goes round
199.gm: The talking shell goes round the fire one more time: whoever holds it says one true thing about the year, and nobody answers. It reaches the first-years too. When it reaches ROWAN, the player speaks (or passes it on, which is allowed). Inya [inya], Livvie [livvie] and Rana [rana] speak only if they are still here. Let it take its time; no check. @clock 45.

199.title: Songs and embers
199.gm: Songs, the fire burning down, people two by two along the shore. The last free scene of the evening; if the curfew still stands the other dorms are counted home at half past nine, otherwise the fire is allowed to go out by itself. It ENDS with Mama's lamp on the kitchen step. @clock 60.

201.title: Graduation Exhibition: the thesis sets
201.gm: Friday afternoon; doors at two. On tables round the arena concourse Game Design's graduating students show their thesis sets: Wren's [wren] is the one with a queue. Staff and students walk the tables and play sample hands; the Founder, if he can, plays every set once and loses on purpose. Rowan can try one set (a few lines, real mechanics only by GAME_RULES) and talk to its designer. @clock 45.

201.title: The seniors' broadcast
201.gm: The house takes its seats. Commentary's graduating class runs a live broadcast from the stage desk: the year in ten minutes, produced by Bex [bex], with Ms Laurent [vivienne] in the front row with a red pen and, for once, not using it. What the broadcast can say about the year depends on what the school has been told: go by the plot state. Rowan only watches: ONE answer. @clock 30.

201.title: The captain names her challenger
201.gm: The Captain's Exhibition Match: the outgoing captain names her opponent from the stage. IF LILIA [lilia] STANDS and Rowan has become what she was looking for (lilia_rival), she names HIM, and waits. OTHERWISE she says 'nobody yet', and Gani brings up a screen: Isolde, by video link from North Crown. IF SHE IS IN THE WARD: an empty captain's chair on the stage with her jacket over it; Coach Rox [rox] says three sentences and the next point is a minute's silence, not a match. Go strictly by the flags. @clock 20.

201.title: The Captain's Exhibition Match
201.gm: If she named ROWAN: an all-out exhibition on the arena stage, full house, nothing wagered but the game — the truest duel of the year. Play every phase (@duel; she plays at full speed for the first time, and enjoys it). If it is Isolde by video link, play it in ONE long answer through the house's reactions. If the chair is empty, the house stands for a minute and Prof. Santángel [santangel] reads her record. @clock 60.

201.title: The house empties
201.gm: The Chancellor [okonkwo] (or the acting chancellor) thanks the graduating class in four sentences. Dom [dom], Willas [willas], Octavia [octavia] and the others are where their state puts them: on the stage, or named. People stay in their seats a while after the lights come up. ONE answer (@did Graduation Exhibition finished). @clock 20.

203.title: Beach volleyball: the net goes up
203.gm: Sunday, the last beach day of the year. @place beach_cove. Commons against Spectral, six a side, best of three sets; the losing dorm cooks for the winners tonight. Jessica [jessica] referees from under a parasol with total authority and a whistle. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] at the net is unfair. {H=sunny?'Sunny'|Sunny} [sunny] captains whichever side will have her; Saoirse plays only if she is still on the island. Rowan plays or cheers: his choice. @clock 20.

203.title: Three sets
203.gm: Play it in two or three answers, one per set: ONE fitness check for Rowan at a point that matters if he is on the sand. Ashton [ashton] takes his shirt off for the audience and gets sunburnt. Marit [marit] and Pippa [pippa] run the score in the sand and argue about it; Georgie [georgie] and Inya [inya] heckle impartially. Nothing is at stake but dinner. A closing-credits afternoon: let every thread that ended well show its face once, in passing. @clock 90.

203.title: The result, and the last swim
203.gm: Jessica announces the result as if it were a verdict. Everyone goes into the water, winners and losers. A free scene on the raft or the sand with whoever Rowan wants one with. Towels over the headland by half past five. @clock 60.

203.title: The losers cook
203.gm: In Mama's kitchen, whichever dorm lost: Spectral students in aprons under Mama Odalys's [odalys] wooden spoon, or the row cooking for a table of white collars who have never eaten here. ONE meal (@did dinner eaten). It is much better or much worse than expected, and either is fine. It ENDS with the washing-up shared. @clock 60.

205.title: Awards Night: doors
205.gm: The split-flap board has been rolled into the arena and stands on the stage, still running. Staff in the front row: Prof. Santángel [santangel], Coach Rox [rox], Ms Kirishima [hana], Ms Laurent [vivienne], the Founder if he can. The last ladder results of the season are signed at Zeynep's [zeynep] table in the concourse until five to seven. Rowan finds a seat with his dorm. @clock 25.

205.title: The bell: the board is stopped for the year
205.gm: At seven the bell; the board rattles through every rank one last time and stops. Santángel reads the top ten. Then every student looks for one line: Rowan's FINAL RANK — give the number from the game's record and who stands either side of him. Next year's dorm lists follow from these standings, and the house knows it. ONE answer. @clock 15.

205.title: The year awards
205.gm: Presented by the Chancellor [okonkwo] (or the acting chancellor), Bex [bex] at the microphone: Freshman of the Year, Most Improved, the Judge's Whistle (Ms Kirishima's, for the best new judge), and the Commons Spoon — Mama's own, for whoever she says, and she says it from the back of the house without coming down. Award them by what has actually happened this year; Rowan gets one only if he earned it. One or two LONG answers. @clock 45.

205.title: What the staff say; next year's dorm lists
205.gm: The staff come down from the stage and say one sentence each to the students they taught: what Santángel, Rox and Hana say to Rowan sums up his year (from his grades, his rank and his conduct; no flattery). Teobalt [teobalt] pins next year's provisional dorm lists by the doors: tell Rowan where his name is. It ENDS before the night bell. @clock 30.

207.title: Room check-out: Tavita's round begins at Bungalow 1
207.gm: Thursday afternoon; packed duffels on every porch. Tavita [tavita] does the Commons round himself, his last as head proctor, with Mama Odalys [odalys] and a clipboard: mattress, shutters, lamp, key. He works up the row from Bungalow 1 and reaches 7 at about three. Rowan packs what is left: a free scene with his roommates, while across the campus the graduating class goes up to the arena to rehearse. @clock 60.

207.title: Bungalow 7 inspected
207.gm: @place commons_room. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] folds his blanket with military corners and says more than nine words: let them be about the year, and plain. What is left on the THIRD bed depends on the ending and ONLY on the flags: an empty mattress, a tin, or a small square tile with {H=nathan?a loud grin|a face} on it. Do not explain it; let Rowan look. Tavita inspects without comment and waits on the step. @clock 25.

207.title: Graduation rehearsal in the arena
207.gm: The graduating students rehearse walking and sitting under Pilar's [pilar] stopwatch; anyone may watch from the stands. Teobalt [teobalt] reads names for the absent, as a stand-in, and stops once. If Rowan comes up, it is a quiet half hour with whoever else is watching. @clock 60.

207.title: Keys signed in by the bell
207.gm: By the Afternoon bell every key on the row is signed back in on Tavita's sheet; he signs the last line himself and hands the clipboard to Mama, who gives each bungalow its key back until Sunday 'on her own authority'. ONE answer (@did room checked out). @clock 20.

208.title: The families' ferry
208.gm: No classes today. A special ferry docks at a quarter to eleven with the families: hats, cameras, grandmothers. Captain Stroud [abel] hands every one of them down the gangway. Students meet their own; those with nobody coming carry bags for the others. If Rowan has family aboard is the player's to say (ask once, do not invent them). The avenue fills. @clock 30.

208.title: Seats on the Quad
208.gm: Folding chairs in rows facing the fountain, a low stage in front of it; ushers in jackets, parents fanning themselves with programmes. The undergraduates stand at the sides by dorm. Mama Odalys [odalys] is in the second row in a hat nobody has seen before. Rowan finds his place: say who is beside him. @clock 30.

208.title: The procession at midday
208.gm: The tower bell. The fourth-years walk in two by two from the arcade, gowns over red, gold and black jackets, Coach Rox [rox] and the staff behind them. Where someone should be walking and is not, the line keeps the gap. Rowan only watches: ONE answer. @clock 15.

208.title: The addresses
208.gm: The Chancellor [okonkwo] (or the acting chancellor, by the plot state) speaks for five minutes. Then Octavia's [octavia] valedictory: EITHER the speech of someone who sold something, smooth and applauded, OR of someone who refused to, shorter and harder — decided only by what she did about Marrow's offer. Give it in real words. ONE long answer. @clock 25.

208.title: The scrolls
208.gm: The fourth-years cross the stage in front of the fountain. Chuck [chuck], if he can, hands over every scroll with a different wrong name as a joke, and gets Wren's [wren] exactly right. The names of those who cannot cross are read out too, in their place in the alphabet, and their scrolls are laid on the table. Lilia [lilia], Willas [willas], Dom [dom]: each as the flags have them. One or two LONG answers. @clock 50.

208.title: Hats in the air; families on the Quad
208.gm: The class is declared graduated. Photographs by the fountain, parents meeting professors, Inya [inya] introducing nobody to anybody. A free scene for goodbyes to the fourth-years Rowan knew. The families' ferry leaves again before the Evening bell. @clock 30.

209.title: The last Night Market: the lamps are lit
209.gm: @place night_market. The old customs yard at dusk; every stall has hung an extra lamp and the curfew, if any remains, is lifted for it. The town has come to say goodbye to its students: free tastes, prices rounded down, questions about the summer. Captain Stroud [abel] reminds everyone the ferry boards tomorrow from half past ten. Rowan arrives with whoever he came down with. @clock 30.

209.title: Goodbyes round the yard
209.gm: The free part: Mika [mika] at the shop's stall with a goodbye she has prepared and delivers badly; Josie [josie] with a paper cup of something and the truth, if he knows her; Selene [selene] with an address for the summer, if that route is his; Dex [dex] pretending to haggle. One scene each for the ones who matter to Rowan; let each END. @clock by the scene.

209.title: The indigo tent, one last time
209.gm: Madame Oru's [oru] tent stands at the far end. Tonight she reads for free, and for once says something plain about the summer ahead: fit it to the ending Rowan has earned (if she counted at the Vault, she speaks as someone who was there). She does not sell him anything. ONE scene, short. @clock 30.

209.title: The market packs up
209.gm: When he steps out she folds the indigo cloth in four movements, and it is as if there was never a tent: bare flagstones, a lamp hook. The market begins to pack up round the gap. Students walk up the avenue in groups. ONE answer (@did last Night Market over). @clock 20.

210.title: Boarding begins
210.gm: Sunday. Luggage carts down the avenue from mid-morning; the Second Chance at the Academy pier with her gangway out and Captain Stroud [abel] counting heads. Mama Odalys [odalys] has packed food for the crossing for every one of the Commons and checks each bag. Livvie [livvie] and Rana [rana] are in the queue only if they are still students here; otherwise say where they are instead. Rowan carries his duffel down. @clock 45.

210.title: Goodbyes on the pier
210.gm: Who stays: Silas [silas] at the end of the pier with his hands in his pockets, Mama, the staff. Who is going the same way as Rowan and who is not. {H=baylee?'Baylee'|Baylee} [baylee] shakes hands and then does not let go at once. Inya [inya] is either coming aboard or standing with her grandfather. A free scene for the goodbyes the player wants; each one ENDS. The horn gives five minutes at a quarter to twelve. @clock 30.

210.title: The horn: casting off
210.gm: Gangway in at noon. Who waves from the dock; who stands at the rail with Rowan, with which collar on his jacket, with what in his deck box: state all of it from the record. @place ferry_deck. ONE answer, ending as the pier slides away. @clock 15.

210.title: At the rail
210.gm: The epilogue. The island going down behind the wake: the clock tower, the north ridge, the crater. Whether the gulls follow the ferry all the way out is decided by the ending. Close with the ending the campaign has EARNED, strictly by the plot file's ENDINGS and its conditions (@ending <id> | <Title>), not by this plan; give the people Rowan loved their last line each, and stop. @clock 45.
